content:
Ho visitato la Jozani Forest durante un''escursione organizzata e la considero una tappa imperdibile per chi visita Zanzibar. È l''unico parco nazionale dell''isola e offre un''immersione nella natura, tra sentieri circondati da una vegetazione tropicale rigogliosa fatta di alberi secolari, palme e piante tipiche della foresta.
L''attrazione principale sono senza dubbio le celebri scimmie colobo rosso di Zanzibar, una specie endemica che vive esclusivamente qui. Se ne incontrano davvero tantissime lungo il percorso: sono abituate alla presenza dell''uomo, si muovono liberamente tra gli alberi e spesso attraversano i sentieri, permettendo di osservarle e fotografarle da molto vicino senza disturbarle.
Il tour è ben organizzato, con guide che spiegano le caratteristiche della foresta, della fauna e della flora locale, rendendo la visita ancora più interessante. Se siete a Zanzibar, consiglio vivamente di inserire la Jozani Forest nel vostro itinerario: è un''esperienza che permette di conoscere un lato dell''isola completamente diverso dalle sue splendide spiagge.
translated_content:
I visited Jozani Forest on an organized excursion and consider it a must-see for anyone visiting Zanzibar. It's the island's only national park and offers a true immersion in nature, along trails surrounded by lush tropical vegetation of ancient trees, palms, and typical forest plants.
The main attraction is undoubtedly the famous Zanzibar red colobus monkeys, an endemic species that lives exclusively here. You'll encounter countless of them along the trail: they're accustomed to human presence, move freely among the trees, and often cross paths, allowing you to observe and photograph them up close without disturbing them.
The tour is well-organized, with guides who explain the characteristics of the forest and the local fauna and flora, making the visit even more interesting. If you're in Zanzibar, I highly recommend including Jozani Forest in your itinerary: it's an experience that allows you to see a side of the island completely different from its splendid beaches.
full_address: Jozani Forest, Mapopwe, Tanzania

The mangrove boardwalk was also beautiful, especially seeing the black crabs moving through the mangroves. You can really tell the guides care about the forest and want visitors to understand why this place is so special for Zanzibar.

- eine halbe Stunde durch den Wald gegangen mit 22 anderen Menschen
- Guide hat nichts erzählt, sondern am Handy gedaddelt
- es hieß, man soll Abstand halten, allerdings wurde ich von dem Guide in den Busch gedrückt, damit ich näher an den Affen bin. Für mich grenzüberschreitend
- nach 30min mussten wir in unser Auto und sind 15min lang zu den Mangroven gefahren und da dann auch noch einmal 15min durchgegangen
- Stau und alles extrem überlaufen
- Zum Schluss wollten wir dennoch Trinkgeld geben, allerdings wurde das abwertend abgewunken und uns wurde gesagt, dass es unterhalb des Minimums liegt. Einfach nur frech und anscheinend geht es den Mitarbeitenden zu gut, dass Ansprüche bzgl der Höhe beim freiwilligen! Trinkgeld ausgesprochen werden können
Bucht lieber eine Schnorcheltour mit Said Sansibar Tours. Da könnt ihr mit dem Boot noch in die Mangroven fahren und habt viel schönere Einfrücke undkönnt ebenfalls die Affen sehen!
translated_content:
An absolute disaster and not recommended!
- We walked through the forest for half an hour with 22 other people.
- The guide didn't say anything, just fiddled with his phone.
- We were told to keep our distance, but the guide pushed me into the bushes so I could get closer to the monkeys. I found this completely unacceptable.
- After 30 minutes, we had to get back to our car and drove for 15 minutes to the mangroves, where we then walked through them for another 15 minutes.
- Traffic jams and everything extremely crowded.
- In the end, we still wanted to leave a tip, but it was dismissed dismissively, and we were told it was below the minimum. Simply outrageous, and apparently, the staff are doing too well to feel the need to make demands regarding the amount of a voluntary tip!
Better to book a snorkeling tour with Said Zanzibar Tours. There, you can take a boat into the mangroves, have a much more beautiful experience, and see the monkeys too!

content:
Beznadziejne miejsce totalnie nie warte tych pieniędzy. Zacznijmy od tego że zanim tam przyjechałam zapytałam znajomego z Zanzibaru który bardzo dobrze zna wyspę i jej atrakcje oto miejsce i odpowiedział on że jeżeli gdziekolwiek indziej zejdę z drogi i wejdę w ścieżkę w las których nie brakuje to będzie to dokładnie tak samo wyglądać jak w tym parku. Na wstępie płacimy 12 dolarów za wejście a potem jeszcze 10 za wycieczkę z przewodnikiem. Przewodnik przez 40 minut sprowadza nas po krzakach opowiadając kilka historii o okolicznych roślinach drzewach i resztkach rafy, niestety miejsce to naprawdę zasługuje na nazwę krzaki. Udało mi się zobaczyć całe pięć małp i oczywiście rozumiem że nie czekają one specjalnie na turystów i jest to kwestia wypadkowości jednak te same małpy zobaczyłabym stojąc cierpliwie przy głównej drodze.   Cześć trasy - do lasu namorzynowe go leży poza parkiem, są tam domu miejscowych a małpy siedzą u nich na podwórkach jak pieski. Jest to droga dokładnie naprzeciwko wjazdu do parku.
Na koniec przewodnik kilkakrotnie wspomina że można dać mu wysoki napiwek za wątpliwie dla mnie cudowny spacer po chaszczach.   Radzę te pieniądze wydać na coś lepszego. Np na jedzenie.
translated_content: A hopeless place, totally not worth the money. Let's start by saying that before I arrived, I asked a friend from Zanzibar who knows the island and its attractions very well about this place, and he replied that if I went anywhere else and took a path into the forest, of which there's no shortage, it would be exactly the same as this park. We pay $12 for the entrance fee and another $10 for a guided tour. The guide leads us through the bushes for 40 minutes, telling us stories about the surrounding plants, trees, and remnants of the reef. Unfortunately, this place truly deserves the name "bushes." I managed to see five monkeys, and of course, I understand that they don't wait for tourists and that it's accidental, but I would have seen the same monkeys if I had stood patiently by the main road. Part of the route to the mangrove forest lies outside the park. There are local homes there, and the monkeys sit in their yards like dogs. This road is directly opposite the park entrance. At the end, the guide mentions several times that you can tip him generously for what I consider a rather dubious walk through the thicket. I suggest spending that money on something better. Like food.

content:
Il tour organizzato da Zantour che include Butterfly Center, Jozani Forest e la passeggiata nelle mangrovie è nel complesso ben gestito, anche se molto “classico” come tipo di escursione.
Il Butterfly Center è carino, una visita breve ma piacevole: poche spiegazioni, ma vedere da vicino le diverse farfalle in un ambiente tranquillo ha il suo perché. Non è un’esperienza che rimane particolarmente impressa, però è un buon inizio per la giornata.
La Jozani Forest è sicuramente la parte più interessante del tour. L’incontro ravvicinato con le scimmie colobo e le varietà di piante locali è la ragione principale per cui vale la pena. La guida Zantour è stata chiara e disponibile, anche se il percorso segue il solito tracciato battuto da tutti i gruppi, quindi c’è un po’ di movimento attorno.
La Mangrove Walk è breve ma suggestiva. La passerella in legno permette di vedere da vicino le radici e capire come funziona l’ecosistema delle mangrovie, anche se la visita dura davvero pochi minuti.
In sintesi: un pacchetto ben organizzato, comodo e interessante per farsi un’idea della natura dell’isola. Non eccezionale o particolarmente approfondito, ma una buona scelta se si vuole vedere più luoghi in un’unica uscita senza complicazioni.
translated_content:
The tour organized by Zantour, which includes the Butterfly Center, Jozani Forest, and the mangrove walk, is overall well-managed, although very "traditional" in its nature.
The Butterfly Center is nice, a short but pleasant visit: little explanation is given, but seeing the different butterflies up close in a tranquil environment is worth it. It's not a particularly memorable experience, but it's a good start to the day.
The Jozani Forest is definitely the most interesting part of the tour. The close encounter with the colobus monkeys and the local plant varieties is the main reason it's worth it. The Zantour guide was clear and helpful, although the route follows the usual route used by all groups, so there's a bit of traffic around.
The Mangrove Walk is short but evocative. The wooden walkway allows you to see the roots up close and understand how the mangrove ecosystem works, even though the visit only lasts a few minutes.
In short: a well-organized, convenient, and interesting package that gives you a glimpse of the island's natural beauty. It's not exceptional or particularly in-depth, but it's a good choice if you want to see multiple places in a single, hassle-free trip.

To miejsce daje ogromną frajdę zarówno dzieciom, jak i dorosłym. Świetna wycieczka, blisko natury i lokalnej kultury 🌿🐒
translated_content:
A beautiful park where you can see the famous red monkeys – a species found only in Zanzibar. They are lively, playful, and very inquisitive. Feeding them is prohibited, so you'll need a bit of determination not to succumb to their charms 😉
Local vendors sell fresh fruit along the main road in the park. You can try interesting flavors there, including cocoa and jackfruit. The park itself is naturally preserved and well-maintained, free of litter.
This place is a real treat for both children and adults. A great trip, close to nature and local culture 🌿🐒

content: Das war kein Highlight, für 2 Erwachsene, 2 Kinder 48 Dollar und noch Trinkgeld, welches der Guide für die 1 h nicht verdient hat. Die 2 Affenarten gesehen. Die eine Art ist hier endemisch, der Colobus Affe. Der mit dem roten Rücken.  Den könnte man einfach von der Straße sehen. Sie haben eine Affenleiter über die Straße gespannt. Den hat man nur vom weiten gesehen. Der Guide hat sehr schnelles Englusch gesprochen und ist rücksichtslos durch den Wald gerast.  Ke I n Wunder, dass man da keine Tiere sehen kann. Den einen Busch rannte er um, auf dem ich einen kleinen Frosch gesehen habe und auf Frage was es für einer ist, antwortete er, ein Frosch.  Er hat von seiner Umgebung selbst keine Ahnung. Dann gab es kaum Trinkgeld, da man viel bezahlt und die Tour schlecht war. Da war er sauer. Es soll ein Schutzgebiet sein und überall liegt Müll. Am dortigen Restaurant sieht man bereits die ersten Affen, dann könnte man eigentlich wieder gehen. Zu den Mangroven wird man gefahren. Unterwegs Shops. Immer die gleiche Masche überall. Es geht immer darum den Touristen abzuzocken.  Es gibt schöne Strände. Danach waren wir im Butterfly Center, das war wesentlich netter. Hierhin werden wir auf jeden Fall nicht noch mal fahren. Da ist Thailand eine wesentlich bessere Alternative.
translated_content: That wasn't a highlight at all. $48 for two adults and two children, plus a tip, which the guide didn't deserve for just one hour. We saw two types of monkeys. One of them is endemic here, the colobus monkey, the one with the red back. You could easily spot it from the road. They've even strung a monkey ladder across the road. But we only saw it from a distance. The guide spoke very fast English and sped recklessly through the forest. No wonder you can't see any animals there. He ran over a bush where I saw a small frog, and when I asked what kind it was, he just replied, "A frog." He clearly doesn't know anything about his surroundings. Then there was hardly any tip because we'd paid so much and the tour was terrible. He was angry about that. It's supposed to be a protected area, but there's trash everywhere. You can already see the first monkeys at the restaurant there, and then you might as well just leave. You're driven to the mangroves. There are shops along the way. It's always the same scam everywhere. It's always about ripping off tourists. There are some beautiful beaches. Afterwards, we went to the Butterfly Center, which was much nicer. We definitely won't be going back here. Thailand is a much better alternative.

translated_content:
A star for the monkeys and the mangrove forest scenery!
Four of us did the three-hour tour! Highly not recommended. Of the three hours, we only spent five minutes observing the monkeys and another five in the mangrove forest, which in itself is worth the entrance fee. The rest of the time was spent in the sun and dust trying to reach unclear places! The paths aren't marked, and the guide doesn't care about waiting for everyone. We were left behind on a path outside the park while we were trying to remove thorns from our pants, so much so that we almost got lost since no one waited.
The tour includes a visit to the butterfly sanctuary, but we didn't even get close to it. Two hours wandering around in circles in the forest without any explanation of where we were or what we were seeing—a brisk walk!
$35 isn't worth it! Take the short tour to see the monkeys and mangroves, which are worth it! For the other two hours, they just find a way to pass the time. And not even too pleasantly.

content:
Déception immense. Je m''en veux d''avoir participer à cette visite. J''ai fait beaucoup d''observation d''animaux dans différents pays mais elle reste de loin la pire que j''ai pu faire. Les larmes coulent encore tellement je suis triste de voir que l''espèce humaine peut avoir si peu de respect pour les animaux.
La visite n''a aucun sens si ce n''est de nous balancer au milieu d''un groupe de touriste bruyant en dessous d''un arbre où se trouve quelques singes. Cool on peut les prendre en photos mais où est le respect ? Où sont les explications ? On nous dit de ne pas s''approcher et de rester à moins de 3 m et on voit les guides mettrent littéralement le téléphone devant le  nez du singe. Une honte. Huge disappointment. I'm so angry at myself for going on this tour. I've done a lot of wildlife viewing in different countries, but this is by far the worst experience I've ever had. Tears are still flowing because I'm so sad to see that humankind can have so little respect for animals.
The tour makes absolutely no sense other than to throw us into the middle of a noisy group of tourists under a tree where there are a few monkeys. Great, we can take pictures, but where's the respect? Where are the explanations? We're told not to get too close and to stay within 3 meters, and yet we see the guides literally putting their phones right in front of the monkeys' noses. It's a disgrace. I beg you, avoid this kind of place 🙏🙏

content:
Visiting Jozani Forest was one of the highlights of my trip to Zanzibar. This lush and peaceful nature reserve offers a rare glimpse into one of the island’s last remaining natural treasures—and it absolutely lives up to the hype.
The forest is home to the endangered Zanzibar red colobus monkey, which is found nowhere else in the world. Seeing them up close in their natural habitat was both exciting and heartwarming. They’re surprisingly calm around visitors, and the guides are great at making sure tourists don’t disturb them.
Beyond the monkeys, the forest itself is stunning. Towering mahogany and eucalyptus trees create a cool canopy overhead, while butterflies and birds flit through the undergrowth. The air feels fresh and earthy, and walking the trails is a refreshing escape from the beach heat.
One of my favorite parts of the tour was the mangrove boardwalk. It winds through a surreal, otherworldly landscape where you can see crabs scuttling along the roots and learn about the importance of mangroves for the local ecosystem.
The guides are knowledgeable, friendly, and passionate about conservation. They explained not just the wildlife but also how the community is involved in protecting the forest.

content:
We decided to take a half-day trip that included a stop at Jozani Chwaka Bay National Park. The journey itself was already quite an experience, offering a firsthand glimpse into the reality of corruption, with around 8–10 police checkpoints seemingly set up just to collect bribes. While this is worth mentioning, it does not influence our rating of the park itself.
The park is undeniably beautiful, showcasing lush nature and a rich variety of flora and fauna. It was a pleasure to observe the animals in their natural habitat, and our guide provided plenty of interesting information about the different plant species.
Unfortunately, the negative aspects outweighed the positives for us:
Mass tourism: Visitors are herded through the park in groups of approximately 40 people, which significantly diminishes the experience.
Tipping culture: Even during the initial briefing, there was already a strong emphasis on tipping the guide.
Disregard for rules: While sensible rules are explained—such as keeping a respectful distance from the monkeys—they are largely ignored. Most visitors end up crowding the animals, and the guides do little to enforce these guidelines.
Littering: One of the rules is to avoid leaving trash behind, which is ironic considering the park is littered with plastic waste. Rangers don’t seem to take any initiative to clean up or maintain the area.
In the end, Jozani Chwaka Bay National Park felt like just another location in Zanzibar being exploited to the maximum for tourism. A real shame, considering the natural beauty and ecological importance of the area.

Fortunately, we were able to reconnect with our driver, who then brought us to the mangrove section of the forest. Overall, Jozani is worth a brief visit, particularly if you’re interested in Zanzibar’s biodiversity, but it is not an all-day activity.

Парка Джозани или Джозани форест е най големият Национален парк на остров Унгуджа (Занзибар). Наред с маймуните е възможно да срещнете и миниатюрна жабка (възрастните са големи до около сантиметър), слонска земеровка, над 200 вида пеперуди, земни раци, хапещи мравки и много други интересни животинки. Ще се запознаете и с множество растения, огромни дървета отрупани с манго (кората на плода е любима на Червеният Колобус), евкалипт, тамаринд и др.
Задължително посетете и мангровата гора.
Прекрасно място за разходка, снимки и опознаване на различни видове растения и животни.
translated_content:
Jozani Park or Jozani Forest is the largest National Park on the island of Unguja (Zanzibar). Here you can observe several species of monkeys, including the rare Red Colobus - an endemic species that is found only on the island of Unguja. They are characterized by the fact that they do not eat ripe fruit and have only four fingers. Along with the monkeys, you can also meet a miniature frog (adults are up to about a centimeter long), an elephant shrew, over 200 species of butterflies, land crabs, biting ants and many other interesting animals. You will also get to know many plants, huge trees laden with mangoes (the fruit's bark is a favorite of the Red Colobus), eucalyptus, tamarind, etc.
Be sure to visit the mangrove forest.
A wonderful place for walking, taking pictures and getting to know different types of plants and animals.

content:
Je n’ai pas beaucoup apprécié cette visite. Cela peut être intéressant pour quelqu’un qui n’a jamais vu de singes auparavant, mais sinon, je trouve que le prix du billet n’en vaut pas la peine. J’ai fait la visite courte, qui dure environ 75 minutes, donc je ne peux pas juger des éventuelles randonnées plus longues.
Ce qui m’a le plus dérangé, c’est que les touristes étaient autorisés à s’approcher beaucoup trop près des singes colobus. Certains allaient jusqu’à se coller à eux pour prendre des selfies. Nul doute que c’est stressant pour les singes et cela perturbe clairement leur comportement.
Les singes restent proches des groupes de touristes, espérant récupérer de la nourriture, ce qui n’est pas souhaitable non plus.
La partie mangrove est un peu plus intéressante, et au moins, les animaux y sont laissés tranquilles.
Par contre, la route menant à la mangrove est en très mauvais état. C’est dommage, car avec les revenus générés par le parc, on pourrait au moins l’entretenir un peu mieux.
translated_content:
I didn't particularly enjoy this visit. It might be interesting for someone who has never seen monkeys before, but otherwise, I don't think the ticket price is worth it. I did the short tour, which lasts about 75 minutes, so I can't comment on the longer treks.
What bothered me most was that tourists were allowed to get far too close to the colobus monkeys. Some even went so far as to press themselves against them to take selfies. This is undoubtedly stressful for the monkeys and clearly disrupts their behavior.
The monkeys stay close to groups of tourists, hoping to get food, which is also undesirable.
The mangrove section is a bit more interesting, and at least the animals are left undisturbed there.
However, the road leading to the mangrove is in very poor condition. It's a shame, because with the revenue generated by the park, we could at least maintain it a little better.

It is worth the couple of hours if you are interested in nature

Die Besichtigung des Jozani Forest ist dreigeteilt.

The Jozani Forest tour is divided into three parts.
Unfortunately, you can't explore it independently. You pay an entrance fee and are then assigned a guide. The guide first points out what you're not allowed to do. Of course, they also mention that a tip is expected.
The tour then begins with a short walk through the forest, during which our guide seemed to be rushing. However, we did manage to see our first monkeys.
Afterward, we crossed the road to another section where we saw more monkeys, some with their young. Here, we were able to take our time, observe them, and take photos.
Finally, we walked through the mangrove forest. We moved through this section relatively quickly as well.
All the explanations seemed rehearsed and simply recited.
At the end, the promised tip was collected.
All in all, the tour lasted about an hour.
It was nice to have seen it once, but it's not something we'd do again.

content:
Erfahrungen der 3-Stunden-Tour:
Dschungel:
Schöner Dschungel mit unzähligen Mahagonibäumen (habe ich vorher noch nie gesehen). Viele Affen, Mini-Frösche (die sind wirklich erstaunlich klein und sehr süss!), Schmetterlinge und Vögel. Schlangen haben wir nur durch Rascheln wahrgenommen. Wobei dies bei den giftigen grünen Mambas und indischen Kobras und den (ungiftigen) 6-Meter-Pythons für mich ganz ok war.
Die Mangroven zum Schluss der Tour waren sehr beeindruckend, benötigen aber einen zusätzlichen Marsch von 2 x 15 Min in der Sonne hin und zurück.
Kleidung:
Geschlossene Schuhe (unbedingt) und trotz Hitze lange Kleidung (persönliche Ansicht) würde ich empfehlen, da wir tatsächlich etwas Angst vor den giftigen Schlangen hatten - wahrscheinlich unbegründet, da die Schlangen sich verziehen, bevor die Menschen in ihre Nähe kommen.
Es war sehr heiss (Ende September) und wir mussten viel Marschieren bei tropischer Hitze, streckenweise über staubige Strasse ohne Schatten.
Fazit: drei Stunden waren etwas lang für das Erlebnis, aber die Mangrovenwälder möchte ich nicht verpasst haben. Ich weiss nicht, ob die Mangroven bei der 1-Stunden-Tour mit dabei sind.
translated_content:
Experiences from the 3-hour tour:
Jungle:
Beautiful jungle with countless mahogany trees (I'd never seen anything like them before). Lots of monkeys, tiny frogs (they're amazingly small and very cute!), butterflies, and birds. We only noticed the snakes by their rustling. This was perfectly fine with the venomous green mambas and Indian cobras, and the (non-venomous) 6-meter pythons.
The mangroves at the end of the tour were very impressive, but require an additional 15-minute walk each way in the sun.
Clothing: I would recommend closed shoes (absolutely essential) and, despite the heat, long clothing (personal opinion), as we were actually a bit afraid of the venomous snakes – probably unfounded, since the snakes slither away before people get too close.
It was very hot (late September) and we had to do a lot of walking in the tropical heat, sometimes on dusty roads with no shade.
In conclusion: three hours was a bit long for the experience, but I wouldn't have wanted to miss the mangrove forests. I don't know if the mangroves are included in the one-hour tour.

content:
Booked this tour because my room wasn''t ready and thought the drive through the towns would be interesting.
Thus, I consider the drive which was about an hour really engrossing. The monkeys were cute and our guide Shaeeb was committed to environmental conservation which was fantastic. He explained the salinity and uniqueness of the mangroves (similar to the swamps in Florida) which is fascinating considering this is the same seawater from the magnificent turquoise Indian Ocean. The mangroves protect the island from flooding and there used to be a lot more. The forest is beautiful and used to house the extinct Zanzibar Leopard…videographic evidence suggests that the leopard is still alive, illusive but not extinct. The last sighting was in the 80’s so thats a nice little mystery.
Another interesting story was the introduction of the Eucalyptus tree to the forest in an attempt to control water levels but its invasive and not attempts are being made to remove these massive trees. Consequently, there are magnificent uprooted trees which I found awe-inspiring.
I enjoyed my time here. As someone who was not driving, I found the drive, the monkeys, the mangroves and the forest for $80 plus tip worth it.
This is Africa and Im happy to support the local economy 💜🇹🇿

Beim Mangroven-Teil angekommen läuft man einen Steg zwischen den Mangroven entlang (ca. 10 min). Rückfahrt mit dem Daladala schwieriger als die Hinfahrt, haben dann ein Taxi für 10.000 TZS genommen.

translated_content:
We travelled from Paje by dala-dala without any problems for 1500 TZS (approx. €0.50) per person. Entrance fee was $11. The tour itself was just a short walk through the forest (about 10 minutes). You see the forest, but no monkeys or other animals. Back at the parking lot, we were told that the rest of the tour unfortunately had to be done by car. After some haggling, we were driven for 40,000 TZS for about 5 minutes to the next station. Right next to the road, you stop to observe monkeys. This part of the tour is the absolute highlight and highly recommended, as you get within a few meters of the animals. Then it's back to the car for a mere 2-minute drive. Once you reach the mangrove section, you walk along a boardwalk among the mangroves (about 10 minutes). The return trip by dala-dala was more difficult than the trip there, so we ended up taking a taxi for 10,000 TZS.
... Overall, it's a bit too expensive, and we've already only paid about 50% of the price the hotels are offering the tour for.

We went on this excursion expecting to see lots of monkeys. We can't give a price because it was included in a day trip, but what's certain is that it's not worth more than €10 per person! The guide picked us up and added us to a group for a walk, with no explanation about the monkeys, only an explanation about a plant. The terrain was uneven, so wear sneakers. After walking for 30 minutes along a dangerous road, we spotted three monkeys. After that, we had to get back in the car with the guide to see some mangroves for another 30 minutes—completely pointless. The visit was rushed. We were told not to approach the monkeys closer than 3 meters, but when tourists from other groups got within a meter, he said nothing. Lots of unwritten rules were ignored.
Furthermore, there's a fantastic wildlife park next door with reptiles, turtles, etc., which belongs to the same park, but it's impossible to visit it unless you pay significantly more! Shameful!

On nous dit avant de payer à l’entrée que sans guide c’est possible de faire le tour ( les lois sont après le guichet d’entrée où l’on paye, donc impossible de les voir), puis une fois payer on nous explique que c’est impossible sans guide ( ce que nous comprenons complètement). Nous demandons alors de récupérer notre argent pour partir sans visiter vu que nous sommes à l’entrée et que nous n’avons encore rien vu. Et la, comme c’est plus facile de prendre de l’argent mais plus compliquer de le rendre, sans suit un va et vient de fausses explications incohérentes pour nous faire tourner en rond et nous faire abandonner. Puis voyant que nous tenions bon et de manière très calme, le personnel et un guide commence à nous menacer et nous agresser verbalement de manière raciste : «  vous ne récupérerez jamais votre argent, partez, ici c’est pas l’Europe c’est l’Afrique «  en rigolant. translated_content:
Extremely disappointed, we live in Zanzibar and we do not recommend this place. The forest is supposed to be visited with a guide, but most guides just take you around a roadside area to see three millipedes and two monkeys. It's a tourist trap like few others. Josiani is supposed to have a mangrove, a large forest, etc.
Before paying at the entrance, we were told that it was possible to visit without a guide (the regulations are posted after the entrance where you pay, so it's impossible to see them). Then, once we paid, we were told it was impossible without a guide (which we completely understood). We then asked for our money back so we could leave without visiting, since we were at the entrance and hadn't seen anything yet. And then, because it's easier to take money but more complicated to give it back, what followed was a series of incoherent and false explanations designed to lead us in circles and make us give up. Then, seeing that we were standing firm and remaining very calm, the staff and a guide began to threaten and verbally abuse us in a racist manner: "You'll never get your money back, leave, this isn't Europe, this is Africa," they laughed. Imagine if we had said the same thing to a Tanzanian visitor? "This isn't Africa, this is Europe, so leave!"... I absolutely do not recommend this place. There are many other places on the island, less than 5 km away, where you can see monkeys and a couple of woodlice with a much more respectful attitude. Avoid at all costs.

In conclusion, my visit to Jozani Forest was nothing short of magical. translated_content: We were really disappointed with this place. I don't recommend going there. The entrance fee is 25,000 Tanzanian shillings, not including the mandatory, limited tip for the guide. They take you into a mahogany forest with ferns at its base—this is just a way to waste some of your time during the hour-long tour. Then they take you out of the forest to see monkeys. When you reach the junction where you're supposed to turn left into the forest, I advise you to take the road on the right, because that's where the monkeys are. This way you'll avoid paying the 25,000 entrance fee unnecessarily. You can't get lost; it's a straight road. You'll see the monkeys on your right near the huts of the local people. A little further on, you'll find the mangrove where you can take a short 5-minute walk. That's the gist of it. The guide's three-sentence summary is practically useless. So unless you're a mahogany enthusiast, I advise against visiting Jozani Forest. It's much better to explore the monkeys and mangroves on your own...

Наблюдение за красными обезьянами просто восторг. В живой среде множество чудесных особей, множество крошечных малышей,висящих на мамах. Это мило и забавно. Но гулять там особо негде. Прогулка -это поиск обезьян на отрезке в 200 метров и фотографирование их.

Так что ставлю оценку 4.
translated_content:
Watching red monkeys is simply a delight. There are so many wonderful specimens in their natural habitat, so many tiny babies clinging to their mothers. It's cute and amusing. But there's not much room to walk there. A walk involves searching for monkeys over a 200-meter stretch and photographing them.
There are also mangrove swamps, with wooden walkways running across them. Occasionally, you might spot a crab. But if you've seen mangrove forests in the Amazon or Sri Lanka, you'll be saddened by the modest size of the Zanzibar mangroves.
So, I give it a 4.

Mixed feelings… 25,000 TZ per person for a one-hour tour that felt rather rushed. They explain the rules, the last and most important being: leave a generous tip for the guide.
The first part of the tour: the Jozani forest to spot the monkeys. This involves a walk through the forest to reach the base of a tree where the monkeys have "made their home." It's impossible to stop on the path, even when we spot monkeys, because the guide walks quickly ahead. No explanation is given; we only saw about eight monkeys!
The second part of the tour: the mangrove. This is simply a short, 600-meter marked trail surrounded by mangroves! The only explanation given was the presence of old posts that marked the former path before the mangroves grew over it. Again, we walked very quickly behind the guide!
The final moment: the guide laughing when given a 5,000 tz tip because the general rule is a minimum of 10,000 tz.

translated_content: Challenging tour! We did the long jungle trek. The guide led us for 3.5 hours through the deepest jungle (a total of 3 km). He led the way with a machete, pushing through dense foliage, stooping through branches, and crawling over and under fallen tree trunks. In some places, the jungle was very swampy. Jozani je jedno z mála míst na Zanzibaru kde se dbá na přírodu a její ochranu v tom smyslu, jak to chápeme u nás v Evropě. English
Jozani is one of the few places in Zanzibar where nature and its conservation are taken into consideration in the sense that we understand in Europe. The park is divided into three parts, between which you need to drive a short distance by car. In the first part, you''ll find a jungle with many plants. Some of them you might recognize from Europe, but they''re more like small plants rather than big trees, as they are here. The second part is probably the most popular. Here, you can observe monkeys very closely. Beware, you''re not allowed to feed them or touch them. But even so, it''s quite an experience. The last part is the mangrove forest. It greatly depends on whether it''s high tide or low tide. We were lucky to have low tide, so we could see the tangle of roots and many crabs among them.
We can recommend the visit; it''s a very beautiful place with friendly people.

After that we approached a big tree where the monkeys were resting. They didn’t express any interest to us whatsoever, they were just chilling and living their monkey lives, people were watching, taking photos.
After monkey encounter we walked through the mangrove forest, and that was very beautiful and unusual.
As for me, I would like the tour to last longer, as sometimes I had a feeling that the guide is rushing us, just to bring us to the finish faster.
Other than that - no complaints, the place is beautiful and definitely worth the visit.

the Jozani Forest National Park in Zanzibar is an incredible experience that left me in awe of the natural beauty and biodiversity of this unique ecosystem.
Our guide was very knowledgeable and provided us with a lot of interesting information about the different species of mangroves that grow in the area, as well as the various animals that call the mangroves home. We saw a variety of crabs, and even some monkeys swinging through the trees above us.
The walk itself was quite easy and took us along a boardwalk that wound its way through the dense mangrove forest. The trees were tall and majestic, with their roots stretching down into the water below, creating a labyrinth of tunnels.
One of the highlights of the walk was spotting the rare red colobus monkeys that are endemic to the area. Our guide was able to point out several of them to us, and we were able to watch them foraging for food in the trees.
Overall, I would highly recommend a visit to the Jozani Forest National Park Mangrove Walk to anyone who loves nature and wants to experience the unique beauty of a mangrove ecosystem. Contra: Man hat an sich keine andere Wahl als mit einer viel zu großen Gruppe (bei uns über 20 Personen) durch den Wald zu gehen, da man alleine mE völlig aufgeschmissen wäre. Es gibt im gesamten Wald keine Wegweiser oder ähnliches.
Was unser Guide dann letztlich über den Wald zu erzählen hatte, haben wir weiter hinten nicht verstanden, weshalb es für uns auch nicht weiter schlimm war, dass er nur gebrochenes Englisch gesprochen hat..
Nach ca 30 Min Marsch durch den Wald wurden wir dann an einen Parkplatz gelotst an dem uns etliche Taxifahrer erwarteten. Vom Guide kam dort die Erklärung, dass der angepriesene Mangrovenwald nicht zu Fuß erreichbar sei. In nem ziemlichen Chaos wurden dann alle Besucher in irgendein Taxi gepfercht. (Selbstredend, dass diese Fahrt natürlich nochmal extra kostet.)
Fazit: Kann man machen, muss man aber defintiv nicht.
translated_content:
Pros: You see monkeys. And quite a lot of them, actually.
Cons: You basically have no choice but to walk through the forest with a far too large group (over 20 people in our case), as you'd be completely lost on your own. There are no signs or anything like that in the entire forest.
We didn't understand what our guide ultimately had to say about the forest, which is why it wasn't a big deal for us that he only spoke broken English.
After about 30 minutes of walking through the forest, we were directed to a parking lot where several taxi drivers were waiting for us. There, the guide explained that the advertised mangrove forest wasn't accessible on foot. In a rather chaotic scene, all the visitors were then crammed into whatever taxis were available. (Naturally, this ride cost extra.)
Conclusion: It's doable, but definitely not a must-do.

Unfortunately, we hardly saw any animals, but there were dik-diks, leopards, forest pigs (we only heard them), oh yeah, and some unpleasant ants… After the jungle, we took a short drive to the mangroves. The tour was great, a good 1.5 hours of walking in the heat. Bring something to drink!

content:
A nice trip through the tropical forest. Ticket (25 k TSh / 12 $) includes entrance fee, guide services and walk through three areas. First is the small forest near the ticket office, where you can see monkeys. Then you enter bigger forest and can see some known trees, like mahogany or eucalyptus. The third part, mangrove forest, of the trip requires you to either walk 2-3 km or take a car (your own or rent something at the parking lot, they charged us 3$ pp). It was my favorite part of the trip, a stroll on the bridges over the roots of trees growing in water. Altogether, trip is an interesting alternative to the beach activities, although do not expect wonders. You just spend 1-2 hours in the forest and learn basics about it and take nice pictures of monkeys.
You can get there by taxi or local bus. I recommend the bus, it costs 1k TSh from Paje (any bus that goes to stone town is fine).

Сама экскурсия не особо длительная. Но обезьяны очень прикольные.

The tour itself isn't particularly long. But the monkeys are really cool.
Probably because they're herbivores, they're not brazen. They don't jump on your head or steal things.
They live right next to the road. But there's a police station there.
I don't recommend going into the forest yourself. According to reviews, there are various stories: some were found and taken to pay, while others took pictures of monkeys in a restaurant and then spent half a day dealing with the police.
Besides the monkeys, there are also mangrove trees and some pools with turtles.

Interessant und auf jeden Fall empfehlenswert. Mein Tipp um auf die vorherigen Bewertungen einzugehen. Bucht nicht über die Reiseveranstalter im Hotel. Bucht einen Privatguide, so habt ihr die Möglichkeit die Zeiten wielange ihr wo Stopps einlegen wollt selbst zu bestimmen. Bei uns hat das bei insgesamt zwei Tagen super geklappt und die 150€ p.P. Nicht zu schaffen)  inkl. Eintritte, Privatguide, privaten Fahrer und Getränken. Nur zu empfehlen. Bei Interesse helfe ich gerne weiter.
Aber nun zum Jozani Forest. Wenn man sich dort ein bisschen Zeit lässt hat man die Möglichkeit die Affen aus nächster Nähe zu beobachten. Ist für Fotografen wirklich zu empfehlen. Auch der Magrovenwald auf der anderen Seite ist mit dem Natursteg sehr sehr schön angelegt und einen Abstecher wert.
translated_content:
Interesting and definitely recommended. My tip, addressing the previous reviews: Don't book through the tour operators at the hotel. Book a private guide. This way, you can decide how long you want to spend at each stop. It worked perfectly for us over two days, and I can't understand the €150 per person mentioned here. For €100, we saw Changuu Island, Stone Town (including the museum), the Spice Farms, the Zaaso Animal Welfare Organization, Jozani Forest, and the Nungwi Aquarium over two full days (it's impossible to do it all in one day). This included entrance fees, a private guide, a private driver, and drinks. Highly recommended. I'm happy to help if you're interested.
Now, about Jozani Forest. If you take your time there, you have the opportunity to observe the monkeys up close. It's really recommended for photographers. The mangrove forest on the other side, with its natural boardwalk, is also beautifully laid out and worth a visit.

full_address:
There's a species of monkey here that, due to its specific diet, which thrives only in this area, exists only in this presumably small patch of rainforest. During the rainy season, the forest may be flooded and inaccessible. A few meters further on (1 to 2 km by car or a park vehicle), you can visit an interesting mangrove forest (white, brown, and black mangrove trees). You get a guide "free of charge" (ours was unmotivated and impatient), who expects a generous tip. Even if he's in a bad mood 😜.
Entrance fee: US$12.
Separately, for an additional US$10 on foot, you can visit and support a sanctuary for water and land turtles (really large animals), along with some pythons, monitor lizards, and fish. It's a conservation project run by a cooperative of 119 families who have learned how to better care for the animals and make a living from them. Because monkeys used to destroy crops and other things (and probably still do), they were killed for it (but aren't anymore). Unfortunately, turtles were and still are also on some people's menus. Since the increasing number of hotels is making suitable beaches for egg-laying scarce, an artificial inland beach, which is still to be created, is intended to promote reproduction and species conservation. The animals are usually released back into the wild after some time and care. However, the realization is slowly taking hold (as in the national parks on the mainland) that intact flora and fauna mean more tourism and more income.

Beware of being scammed! Run for your lives!

The visit is worth it, lasting about an hour and a half, but for those who want a longer tour of the entire forest, it can last up to seven hours. Adult admission is €10 as of July 29, 2019.

The jozani forest, for me i would like to call it pride of Zanzibar its a small forest located in the main island of zanzibar which is known as Unguja Island the most interesting part of this forest is the monkeys, the red colobus mokeys unlike other colobus monkeys theese ones are red coloured with long hair and a cute face, and the most interesting part is the can only be found here in Zanzibar and no where else... So that means if u want to see red colobus monkeys u have to be at jozani forest in Zanzibar... Hey even net geo wild channel and animal planet channel once came here to this place to make a documentary about these creatures.....

content:
Der Wald teilt sich auf in einem Dschungel artigen Wald mit allerlei Getier und einem Mangrovenwald.
Im ersten Abschnitt lassen sich mit etwas Glück ein paar kleine Schlangen und Eichhörnchen entdecken, sowie natürlich die Roten Stummelaffen. Wenn man sich erstmal gefunden hat, lassen Sie sich nicht bei ihrer Beschäftigung stören und in aller Ruhe fotografieren.
Der zweite Teil des Ausflugs führt in einen Mangrovenwald. Nicht besonders spektakulär aber man kann wunderbar die Ruhe genießen.
Jeder muss selbst für sich entscheiden, ob er eine solche Tour braucht. Jedoch ist es eine schöne Abwechslung vom Strandurlaub und verschafft Einblicke in die großartige Natur Sansibars.
translated_content:
The forest is divided into a jungle-like area teeming with wildlife and a mangrove forest.
In the first section, with a bit of luck, you might spot some small snakes and squirrels, as well as, of course, the red colobus monkeys. Once you've found them, don't let them disturb you and take your time photographing them.
The second part of the excursion leads into a mangrove forest. It's not particularly spectacular, but you can enjoy the peace and quiet.
Everyone has to decide for themselves whether they need such a tour. However, it's a nice change of pace from a beach holiday and offers insights into the magnificent natural beauty of Zanzibar.

content: Wir waren im August 2018 im Jozani Forest Park auf Zanzibar. Dort kann man die blauen und roten Kolubus Affen sehen. Die blauen Leben alleine und die roten in der Gemeinschaft. Wir besuchten den kleinen Park mit unserem Reiseführer am Vormittag und haben viele Affen gesehen. Mit etwas  Glück sitzen die roten Affen alle versammelt an einer Stelle und man kann diese hautnah beobachten, wie sie klettern, abhängen am Ast oder genüsslich die Blätter fressen. Man darf diese nicht anfassen oder füttern . Sie tun einem nichts und geniessen es fotografiert zu werden und lassen sich nicht aus der Ruhe bringen.Es gab zu unserer Zeit auch einige kleine Äffchen. Es gibt einen Wald den man durchläuft, wo man den ein oder anderen blau Affen findet. Wir können ein Besuch in diesem Park empfehlen. Kosten pro Person 5 $ Eintritt. Es ist ein Erlebnis so nah an einem Affen zu stehen.
translated_content: We visited Jozani Forest Park in Zanzibar in August 2018. There you can see blue and red koula monkeys. The blue ones live solitary lives, while the red ones live in groups. We visited the small park with our guide in the morning and saw many monkeys. With a bit of luck, the red koula monkeys are all gathered in one spot, and you can observe them up close as they climb, hang from branches, or enjoy eating leaves. You are not allowed to touch or feed them. They won't hurt you and seem to enjoy being photographed, remaining completely undisturbed. There were also some baby monkeys when we were there. There's a forest you walk through where you might spot a blue koula or two. We highly recommend a visit to this park. The entrance fee is $5 per person. It's an amazing experience to be so close to a monkey.

content: Bar e ristorante e bagni collocati all''ingresso, prezzo di 20.000 scellini a testa per l''ingresso(alla data odierna). Di tutta la tenuta viene fatta visitare una piccolissima area dove si viene subito a contatto con le scimmie (Red colobus), la visita dura in base alla guida assegnata, la nostra non aveva una particolare voglia di parlare, la riserva inizia a mostrare i primi segni di inquinamento (molta plastica), da notare i due Baobab secolari davvero maestosi. Dopo le scimmie viene fatta visitare la zona delle mangrovie, forse la più interessante, ecosistema caratteristico perché cambia in base alle maree mostrando la palude nel momento di bassa marea e le mangrovie sommerse durante l''alta.
translated_content: There's a bar, restaurant, and restrooms at the entrance. The entrance fee is 20,000 shillings per person (as of today). Of the entire estate, we're given a tour of a very small area where we immediately come into contact with the red colobus monkeys. The tour lasts depending on the assigned guide; ours wasn't particularly interested in talking. The reserve is starting to show the first signs of pollution (lots of plastic). Note the two truly majestic, centuries-old baobab trees. After the monkeys, we're given a tour of the mangrove area, perhaps the most interesting. This ecosystem is unique because it changes with the tides, revealing the marsh at low tide and the submerged mangroves at high tide.
full_address: Jozani Forest, Mapopwe, Tanzania

content: Экскурсия состоит из трех частей: лес, обезьяны и мангры. Лес огромный и красивый, но увидеть можно только крошечный кусочек. Обезьяны водятся повсюду, обычно высоко в кронах деревьев. Рассмотреть поближе их можно во второй части экскурсии, не в самом лесу, а в невысоком кустарнике через дорогу. Мангры, также как и лес, предлагается посмотреть с краю, там где проложены деревянные дорожки. Организация всего процесса хромает - если приехать в неудачное время, можно сполчаса прождать гида и потом оказаться в группе человек из 10.
translated_content: The tour consists of three parts: the forest, the monkeys, and the mangroves. The forest is vast and beautiful, but you can only see a tiny fragment. Monkeys are everywhere, usually high in the treetops. You can get a closer look at them in the second part of the tour, not in the forest itself, but in the low bushes across the road. The mangroves, like the forest, are viewed from the edge, where wooden paths are laid. The entire experience is poorly organized—if you arrive at the wrong time, you could end up waiting for a guide for half an hour and then end up in a group of only 10 people.

translated_content:
A fantastic excursion! We walked through the forest with a guide. It's incredible what there is to discover. Our guide explained a lot about the plants and trees and the useful properties of the fruits, leaves, etc. This forest is a veritable pharmacy! 😜
Since we were there early in the morning, we soon saw the Zanzibar Red Colobus Monkeys, a species of monkey found only here. After a short drive, we continued with part two of the tour, this time walking along boardwalks through the mangroves. Again, we received very interesting explanations about the importance of this mini-ecosystem for the entire island. It was also good to hear that the nine surrounding villages benefit from the entrance fees.
So, practically a must-see for anyone interested in the sustainability of their trip.

content:
Wir buchten diesen  Ausflug als HotelTour mit Bus und Klimaanlage vom Royal Zanz Beach Resort.
Bus war nicht voll belegt, das war sehr angenehm. Wir hatten über Fisherman Tours (ein erfahrener Veranstalter vor ort) insg 3 BegleitPersonen, Englisch Deutsch Suaheli.
Die Fahrt zu Jozani + Prison island war sehr interessant, man sieht an der Straße entlang die Örtlichen Begebenheiten direkt. Vom Hütten -und Häuserbau bis über die Dalla Dalla Busse der Einheimischen und Tuk Tuk , die Unmengen von Arbeitern und Marktverkäufern fahren .. die Reiseleiter kennen sich sehr gut aus und beantworten die Fragen.
Im Jozani und Mangroven Gebiet sah es für uns aus, wie auf einem anderen Planeten. (es sieht optisch so aus, als diene die Erde als MeerwasserSalzFilter und hätte im Lauf der Jahrhunderte das Leben dort ermöglicht). Es war ein kurzer aber interessanter Ausflug. Die kurze Wanderung über die angelegten Holzstege war recht interessant und abwechslungsreich. Durch den Wald ging es dann auch noch eine Weile.
Auch hier wurde die Vergangenheit kurz erläutert.
Alles in Allem kurz gesagt : für die 70-90 USD / Person ein toller Tagesausflug . Abwechslung zum Hotelalltag.
Highlights :
- Busfahrt
- Affen besuchen sehr nahe (Red Colobus) rote Stummelaffen
- Wanderung über die Holzstege
- Wanderung durch den Waldjungel
MfG und schöne Tage
translated_content:
We booked this excursion as a hotel tour with air-conditioned bus service from the Royal Zanz Beach Resort.
The bus wasn't full, which was very pleasant. We had a total of three guides through Fisherman Tours (an experienced local operator), who spoke English, German, and Swahili.
The drive to Jozani and Prison Island was very interesting; you can see the local life firsthand along the road. From the construction of huts and houses to the dalla-dalla buses of the locals and the tuk-tuks carrying countless workers and market vendors... the tour guides are very knowledgeable and answer all our questions.
In the Jozani and mangrove area, it looked like another planet to us. (It looks as if the earth acts as a saltwater filter, allowing life to develop there over the centuries.) It was a short but interesting excursion. The short hike along the boardwalks was quite interesting and varied. We continued walking through the forest for a while afterward.
The past was briefly explained here as well.
All in all, in short: a great day trip for $70-90 per person. A welcome change from the usual hotel routine.
Highlights:
- Bus ride
- Very close encounter with red colobus monkeys
- Hike along the boardwalks
- Hike through the jungle
Best regards and have a nice day

content: As a nature lover, I loved the forests and the monkeys.  The guides were quite knowledgeable and I heard them explaining details of the forest in a number of different languages.  I liked the idea that a percentage of the proceeds from the park fees go to help the local community.  Why shouldn''t the locals benefit from tourism?  As a resident of Tanzania, I see all too often the tourist dollars being funneled outside of the country with a minimal amount of benefit reaching the local residents.  The park fee subsidizes local farmers and damage to their crops caused by allowing the monkeys to stay in their locality.  Please be advised that there are signs posted on the highway prohibiting photographing the monkeys without paying the park fee.  Do not risk losing your camera.  This is a government law.  Some might feel offended by this... feeling that their freedom is being restricted.  They usually just want something for nothing.  Be happy as you share in the conservation efforts of Jozani Forest.

content:
Visited today and really enjoyed it. At 15,000 TZS per person, the entrance fee is very fair for what you get.
Our guide Omar was excellent – friendly, patient and clearly passionate. He started by explaining why the centre exists and how it supports local farmers and forest conservation, then walked us through the whole butterfly life cycle, showing us what the caterpillars and cocoons actually look like up close. We got to see where the butterflies live and were shown the incubator where the pupae are kept until they emerge.
After the guided part, we had time on our own in the small but beautifully kept garden to watch the butterflies and take photos. Omar stayed nearby the whole time and happily answered any questions we had. To finish, he showed us the chameleons, which was a nice bonus.
The whole visit was peaceful and relaxing – a lovely change of pace from the beach. Highly recommended, especially combined with a trip to Jozani Forest.

content:
This is a fantastic little place to stop. We visited while travelling from east coast of Zanzibar to Stone Town.
We gave Juani Forest a miss after mixed reviews and opted for this instead.
$7 per person entry which goes directly to support local butterfly farmers and the community. A brief but a detailed discussion about the life cycle of butterflies and how they''re farmed here, with lots of items to look at including the most incredible shiny golden chrysalis! You can then wander around the netted garden for as long as you want admiring the plants and butterflies and any other creatures you may find!
There''s also another section outside the butterfly garden where they move the chameleons to (so they don''t eat the butterflies) and we were able to hold a chameleon and watch them change colour.
100% worth a visit!

Spotting the massive coconut crab, the largest land-living crab on earth, was an absolute highlight.
What really impressed me was Chumbe’s dedication to ecotourism, where all income supports their impactful conservation and education initiatives. I was fortunate to meet students and community members on a day trip, learning about the marine protected area, forest reserve, and broader environmental issues. Their commitment to community engagement is inspiring.
To the entire Chumbe team: thank you for such a warm welcome and the meaningful work you do. And for anyone visiting, I highly recommend climbing the lighthouse at golden hour for a breathtaking view of this unique island. Chumbe is truly one of a kind!

This year marked my 17th visit to this island, and I'm still amazed and curious to see what new things the reef has to offer. This year, I managed to document a parrotfish that hadn't previously been found and identified on this reef. For me, that was a very special moment!
It's incomprehensible to me how a visitor who only saw the reef for a maximum of 90 minutes in a single day can claim to know everything about this reef and its health, and then even dare to publish such information! False statements hurt the wrong people!
Chumbe, the island and the reef, is a special place. It's certainly not for people who believe that this island, the moment they visit it, should present itself exactly as they imagine it to be. And if it doesn't live up to their ideal, then of course "others" are to blame.
... People who still have a connection to nature appreciate this island for what it offers all visitors: the chance to discover habitats far removed from mass tourism, habitats that have already been irretrievably lost in many parts of the world. The management of this project invests considerable time and money to ensure that this remains the case for as long as possible. Every visitor contributes to this effort.
It's true that climate change has also left its mark on Chumbe Reef. But for that, "we" (humans) must take responsibility ourselves, not the management of an island that is doing everything possible to preserve the lives of endangered species above and below the water.
I'm already looking forward to my next visit and am curious to see how much further the reef has regenerated in the meantime and what new things await me.

After driving a long distance to get there, I was surprised to be told that the actual entrance fee was USD 15 per person. When I politely asked for an explanation, the staff showed no interest in acknowledging or correcting their mistake. Instead, they accused me of handing the phone to someone who spoke the local language, which was simply untrue.
Everyone can make mistakes, but what truly matters is how those mistakes are handled. Unfortunately, the staff’s attitude was unprofessional, dismissive, and disrespectful. As a visitor, I expected much better customer service.

NIE POLECAM !!!
Nie polecam do odwiedzin. Dla MZUNGU czyli obcokrajowców nie oferuje niczego interesującego za 15$ od osoby. Jest to skromny „park rozrywki” raczej z atrakcjami dla lokalnych dzieci,  jednak zbyt drogo dla nich by mogli z tych atrakcji korzystać.
Byłem tam z lokalnymi 7 dziećmi 26 września 2021. Wszystkie atrakcje  były nieczynne i pozamykane łańcuchami. To było przykre nie tylko dla MZUNGU ale przede wszystkim dla tych 7 lokalnych dzieci, które w ramach wstępu mogły zobaczyć bardzo skromne mini Zoo i skorzystać z paru huśtawek.
Jestem bardzo zawiedziony ZANZIBAR PARK, który po 4 latach odwiedziłem ponownie. Wcześniej był o wiele tańszy i w swym programie oferował nieco więcej.
Tak więc NIE POLECAM!!!
translated_content:
I DO NOT RECOMMEND!!!
I do not recommend visiting. For MZUNGU, meaning foreigners, it offers nothing interesting for $15 per person. It's a modest "amusement park," with attractions for local children, but it's too expensive for them to enjoy.
I was there with seven local children on September 26, 2021. All the attractions were closed and chained up. This was upsetting not only for the MZUNGU, but especially for the seven local children, who, as part of their admission fee, were allowed to see a very modest mini zoo and use a few swings.
I am very disappointed with ZANZIBAR PARK, which I revisited after four years. It was much cheaper before and offered a bit more.
So, I DO NOT RECOMMEND!!!

Все закрыто, включая детскую комнату. Катание на лошадях и верблюдах с 16 или 16:30 - на сайте указано - спору нет. А как же все остальное?!! Зверушек мало. Быстро всех посмотрели и решили искупаться в небольшом бассейне. С нас опять попытались содрать по 500 руб с человека за купание (15000 tz). Якобы наши билеты только для парка, а бассейн - отдельно. После долгих споров и пререканий на кассе нам предложили искупаться беслатно. Сделали одолжение, спасибо. Но желания и настроения уже не было. Тем более, что бассейн далеко от входа.
Жалеем о потраченном времени. Возможно, после 16 получше. Проверять не будем.
translated_content:
We read good reviews and decided to visit this park with the kids. We arrived at 10:00 a.m. Our first disappointment awaited us at the entrance: the 5,000 entrance fee is only for Tanzanian residents. Although the website doesn't mention this at all. They told us to pay 15,000 TZ (480 rubles) per person. Fine. Judging by the price list, this price includes absolutely everything. The park itself is in a sad state. It seems like they rarely clean up after the animals. The walking paths are basically cleaned. There are swings and slides for children. They are old and poorly maintained. From 10:00 a.m. to 12:00 a.m., not a single attraction was working. Everything was closed, including the children's play area. Horse and camel rides start at 4:00 or 4:30 p.m. - the website says so - no doubt about it. But what about everything else?!! There are only a few animals. We quickly looked at everything and decided to take a dip in the small pool. They tried to charge us 500 rubles per person for swimming again (15,000 tz). They claimed our tickets were only for the park, and the pool was separate. After much arguing and bickering at the ticket counter, they offered us a free swim. They did us a favor, thank you. But we were no longer in the mood or in the mood. Especially since the pool is far from the entrance.
We regret the waste of time. Perhaps it's better after 4 pm. We won't check.

content:
My wife and I had such high expectations of this ‘trip’ but unfortunately the staff and organization seem to be the biggest downfall for our experience. When booking my wife did email to let the staff know that we would want picture opportunities together because let’s be honest the main attraction to this place is the photo/video opportunities, my wife even mentioned that we would be happy to pay extra for this. We were told there would be staff to help with this and it would be at no extra cost.
At no point do they inform you that there are NO opportunities to eat throughout the day, you are offered water and prosecco but no food, we were collected from our hotel at 12pm & didn’t arrive back to the hotel until 8:30pm, ideally if they had told us this when booking we could have arranged some form of pack lunch! My wife has health issues which means she has to eat throughout the day little and often, however when we told staff this they still made sure we put our bags into a reception office and just said ‘no sorry we don’t have food here, there isn’t anywhere you can get any food either’
Our group had a total of 21 guests which is way too many, this was discussed throughout the day with other guests and everyone said the same thing, the day is far longer than it needs to be because of the amount of people to animal ratio - 2 bush babies to 21 guests and everyone gets to feed them twice? Then 4 lemurs to 21 guests.. you can imagine the waiting around, we are avid animal lovers and have our own animal rescue rehab farm in the UK so we totally understand the day is controlled inevitably by the animals and how they are feeling but the animals weren’t the problem.
Staff who lead the tour were quite demeaning and rude, not to us as such but others it was quite embarrassing hearing how one man spoke to people. The staff who are in the black shirts (locals) were so pleasant and as helpful as can be.
When it came to the ‘main event’ the images with the beautiful Latifah OBVIOUSLY with myself and my wife being together and it also being our honeymoon we wanted our pictures to be together, with this being such an expensive trip too we wanted to be sure our only images were perfect. After our pictures were taken with the cheetah we then checked them and noticed every picture that was taken was blurry and their finger was infront of the camera, when we mentioned this to staff and asked if there was any chance we could try and just get one more we were told ‘No’
We were then split up for the next encounter so again my wife was allowed another picture but not with myself? I was able to brush the cheetah but not with my wife? It was all very badly organized and honestly not worth the money at all, many other people were told they couldn’t join in due to colours they were wearing? At no point was this sent or mentioned in the email so this other couple didn’t get to have any Involvement in some things which was such a shame.  we felt like we had wasted a day of our holiday from start to finish with this trip. We have done experiences like this all over the world and we haven’t ever had this experience.
Honestly I wouldn’t recommend this trip to anyone, if it was ran by the local men it would have been such a nicer experience and this isn’t due to ‘rules’ at all we completely understand how it works. Just lack of communication and breakdown of the day prior to booking. If it was explained how it ACTUALLY would be, we would have saved our money and not bothered.
However one positive I can add is that the animals are all well taken care of and it is clear how clean enclosures are kept.
response_content:
Dear Marc,
Thank you for recognising how well our animals are cared for. 
That standard is possible because our guests support our work, and because everything at Cheetah’s Rock is organised around one priority: animal welfare.
The practical details of a visit, including group size, suitable clothing and the fact that meals are not provided, are stated on our website. 
When your wife explained that she needed to eat regularly, fruit was offered to her - including bananas. Guests may access their belongings whenever needed and eat at Reception; 
food and bags remain outside the animal areas, both to prevent access to anything potentially harmful and to ensure that none of our smaller residents accidentally finds an unexpected way out.
Photographs are, of course, a wonderful way to preserve an extraordinary encounter, and our team is always happy to help guests capture those memories. As explained before your visit, however, we do not offer professional photography sessions or additional paid photo opportunities. 
What we offer is something rather rarer: the opportunity to sit beside a relaxed, purring cheetah and experience that moment for what it is — while learning about the animal in front of you and supporting its care through your visit.
Clothing colour is relevant only with Beppo, our adult zebra stallion, should something a guest is wearing unsettle him. All other encounters are unaffected.
And one small clarification: everyone on our team wears black shirts — local staff and international zoologists alike. I am immensely proud of the team we have built and of the knowledge, dedication and care they bring to our animals and guests every day.
The excellent condition of our animals that you noticed is precisely the result of these rules, decisions and priorities.
Jenny and the Cheetah’s Rock Team

content:
Cheetah’s Rock was easily one of the things I was most excited about during our time in Zanzibar and I’m so glad we went. I’m always conscious about the ethics of wildlife encounters, so knowing that Cheetah’s Rock is a not-for-profit conservation centre focused on rescue, animal welfare and education made this experience so much more meaningful.
Our guides JJ, Kevin and Mario were absolutely fantastic. Their knowledge and passion for the animals really came across throughout the experience. We didn’t just get to see these incredible animals up close — we learned their individual stories, how they came to be at Cheetah’s Rock, their behaviours and personalities, as well as so much about wildlife and other animals found across the African continent.

content:
We cannot recommend Cheetah''s Rock highly enough!
My sister and I initially booked the Great Wildlife Tour, and we were so impressed that we immediately decided to book the VIP Otter Tour as well. Without a doubt, these were some of the most incredible experiences we have ever had.
One of the things that stood out the most was how much we learned about the animals. Having grown up with many animals ourselves, we are familiar with animal behaviour and care, but Jenny and her team still taught us an incredible amount. Their depth of knowledge and genuine passion for educating visitors, while sharing the unique stories of each animal, made the experience truly special.
The VIP Otter Tour is a private experience where, if the otters choose to interact, you even have the opportunity to play with them. During the Great Wildlife Tour, we met many different species, observed them up close, and, in some cases, interacted with them. At no point did it feel like the animals were being forced to perform for tourists.
What impressed us the most was that the welfare of every single animal always comes first. It is obvious that Jenny and her team are deeply passionate about what they do. The tours help fund the sanctuary and provide care for rescued animals, but every interaction is carefully considered and only takes place when it also benefits the animals.
For example, playing with the otters provides them with important enrichment and stimulation. Other interactions help animals become more comfortable with handling by veterinarians or caretakers, reducing stress when medical treatment is needed. Every animal is treated as an individual, and the team carefully considers whether an animal actually wants to interact with visitors. If an animal prefers not to participate, it is simply left alone. The animals always have the choice to walk away.
It is also clear how much trust exists between Jenny, her team, and the animals. You can immediately see that the animals have had positive experiences with their caretakers. Even during demonstrations, such as with the zebra, it was obvious that everything was based on trust rather than force, and the animals could leave the interaction whenever they wanted.
Beyond the tours themselves, the work this sanctuary does is truly inspiring. Many of the animals have been rescued from heartbreaking situations, saved from death, or given a second chance after suffering terrible circumstances. By booking a tour, you are directly supporting this important conservation and rescue work.
The only small criticism we have is not directed at Cheetah’s Rock, but at some of its visitors. Unfortunately, not everyone treats the animals with the care and respect they deserve. The team sometimes has to step in, and in our opinion, anyone who continues to behave disrespectfully should simply be asked to leave. We honestly cannot understand such disrespect towards these amazing animals and work of the team.
All in all: This was truly a once-in-a-lifetime experience, and we are so grateful we had the opportunity to visit. If you are traveling to Zanzibar or Tanzania, we wholeheartedly recommend booking one of these tours. And if you cannot visit, consider supporting this amazing sanctuary with a donation. Jenny and her team are doing extraordinary work, and they deserve every bit of support they can get.
Lara & Alicia

Jenny and the Cheetah’s Rock Team

content:
Zu der Kritik der vorigen Rezension!
Diese Kritik entspricht nicht dem Eindruck, den man vor Ort gewinnt. Die Tierauffangstation wird mit großem Engagement geführt, und es ist nachvollziehbar, dass ein erheblicher Teil der Einnahmen direkt in die Versorgung der Tiere fließt – etwa für Futter, Pflege und medizinische Betreuung.
Ein wichtiger Aspekt ist zudem die Finanzierung: Der Transport der geretteten Tiere wird privat organisiert und getragen, ebenso wie sämtliche laufenden Kosten. Es gibt offenbar keine staatliche Unterstützung. Tierarztleistungen, Materialien und notwendige Medikamente sind mit hohen Ausgaben verbunden, insbesondere wenn bestimmte Mittel erst eingeflogen werden müssen. Vor diesem Hintergrund erscheinen die Einnahmen als notwendige Grundlage für den Betrieb.
Zudem handelt es sich um eine Einrichtung, die Tiere davor bewahrt, getötet zu werden, da sie häufig nicht mehr in die freie Wildbahn entlassen werden dürfen. Die Verantwortung umfasst dabei nicht nur die Tiere selbst, sondern auch das gesamte organisatorische und finanzielle Risiko. Sämtliche Kosten werden eigenständig getragen, einschließlich der Bezahlung des Personals, das täglich unter fachlicher Leitung für die Versorgung der Tiere sorgt.
Auch die Haltungsbedingungen unterscheiden sich von der Darstellung in der Kritik. Die Gehege wirken gepflegt und auf die Bedürfnisse der Tiere ausgerichtet. Dass keine Decken in den Käfigen vorhanden sind, orientiert sich an natürlichen Lebensbedingungen – Tiere liegen in freier Wildbahn ebenfalls auf Erde, Gras oder vergleichbarem Untergrund. Die Gestaltung zielt darauf ab, eine möglichst naturnahe und zugleich sichere Umgebung zu schaffen.
Die Unterbringung dient dem Schutz von Tieren, die häufig nicht (mehr) in der freien Wildbahn überlebensfähig sind. Der Fokus liegt auf Versorgung, Stabilisierung und – sofern möglich – einer späteren Auswilderung.
Auch die angebotenen Besuche lassen sich als Beitrag zur Finanzierung und zur Aufklärung über Tierschutz verstehen. Insgesamt ergibt sich ein deutlich differenzierteres Bild, als es in der ursprünglichen Kritik dargestellt wird.
Abschließend ist es bedauerlich, dass Plattformen wie Google für derartige Bewertungen genutzt werden, ohne dass eine eigene Erfahrung vor Ort vorliegt oder ein fundiertes Verständnis im Umgang mit Tieren erkennbar ist. Bewertungen sollten idealerweise ehrlich, sachlich und respektvoll sein. Dieser Anspruch wird in der vorliegenden Kritik nicht erfüllt.
Nach neun besuchen bei Cheetahs Rock
Es war eines der beeindruckendsten Erlebnisse dem ich beiwohnen durfte. Es ist beeindruckend wie die Tiere dort umsorgt worden. Jeder im Team hat sich es zur Aufgabe gemacht diese seltenen und schönen Kreaturen zu umsorgen, dass es an nichts fehlt. Würde es mehr Leute geben, die dieses tun, würde die, Welt ein wenig besser sein. Jeder Support ist Gold wert.
translated_content:
Regarding the criticism in the previous review!
This criticism does not reflect the impression one gets on-site. The animal shelter is run with great dedication, and it is understandable that a significant portion of the income goes directly into the animals' care – for example, food, grooming, and medical treatment.
Another important aspect is the financing: The transport of the rescued animals is organized and paid for privately, as are all operating costs. There is apparently no government support. Veterinary services, supplies, and necessary medications are expensive, especially when certain items have to be flown in. Against this backdrop, the income appears to be a necessary foundation for the shelter's operation.

Die Antworten auf Bewertungen/Kritik, von Inhaberin Jenny, lesen sich stellenweise wie die Reaktion einer ungewöhnlich schnell verärgerten Betreiberin, weniger wie sachliche Einordnung von Besucherfeedback.
Das Kritik hier schnell als Wunsch nach „Sonderbehandlung“ dargestellt wird, wirkt wenig offen für ehrliches Feedback.
Auch die Aussage, Interaktionen richteten sich nach dem natürlichen Rhythmus der Tiere, wirft Fragen auf.. besonders wenn Tiere gleichzeitig sehr stark inszeniert präsentiert werden.

Unabhängig davon bleibt auch das Erlebnis selbst zumindest erklärungsbedürftig. The responses to reviews/criticisms from owner Jenny sometimes read like the reactions of an unusually quick-tempered operator, rather than an objective assessment of visitor feedback.

The claim that interactions are based on the animals' natural rhythms also raises questions, especially when the animals are simultaneously presented in a highly staged manner.

Terms like "treatments" are used here to describe tourist interactions with animals.
Regardless, the experience itself remains at least questionable. If interactions supposedly follow only the animals' natural rhythms, it seems somewhat contradictory to visitors when fixed program points, clearly timed sequences, and very obviously staged moments are simultaneously part of the tour.
The flow already feels highly regulated, while visitors are mostly rushed from station to station in a short amount of time.
When animals are also clearly part of demonstrations, the question remains: where exactly is the line between experiencing the animals and the staged performance?
All in all, a disappointing experience, quite apart from the way tourists are treated here!
