It was supposed to be a highlight of our Zanzibar trip: a visit to Cheetahs Rock!
Unfortunately, it left me with a very mixed and ultimately rather disappointing impression.
Upon arrival, we were greeted together as part of a larger tourist group.
Item number one on the agenda – payment!
The "adventure" costs $160 USD per person, a price that naturally raises certain expectations.
After payment, we set off, the entire tourist group lined up in a line on horseback, ushered relatively quickly through the individual enclosures.
The process felt more like a tightly organized tour than an experience.
Then came the first impressions of the animals... also quite underwhelming. Small enclosures, a gloomy atmosphere, and the feeling that the animals were noticeably tense.
The lioness repeatedly jumped against the bars as soon as visitors or keepers walked by, baring her teeth. The puma and the striped hyenas also seemed similarly restless and irritable, due to their recent vaccinations, according to those present.
During the tour, the importance of our fingers and belongings was repeatedly emphasized, sometimes obscenely. We were warned not to lose them to the animals. Are animals being systematically "criminalized" here?
Safety is important, of course. However, the sheer volume and dramatic presentation of these points struck us as an attempt to lend the whole experience a thrilling, cinematic feel.
Many of the interactions with the animals, previously advertised online, now appear to be severely restricted, presumably due to the numerous regulations introduced in recent years.
The real highlight these days seems to be the cheetahs.
Another activity involved "toasting" with a glass of sparkling wine in front of the lion "Aslan" while the animal stared down at the visitors sitting outside its enclosure.
A rather unusual activity, presumably intended to create an exclusive atmosphere. For me, it left me wondering whether this was really the moment that was supposed to make an animal encounter unforgettable, and rather with a strange feeling of shame.
When we finally got to the cheetahs, which was actually the main reason for my visit, the biggest disappointment followed.
The animal was placed on a rock, a zookeeper stood beside it and fed it, while the tourists, lined up again, were allowed to come forward briefly to take photos for a few seconds.
When I politely asked if I could quickly change my lens to take another portrait of this majestic animal, the owner, Jenny, appeared herself and explained to me in front of the assembled group of tourists that this wasn't Instagram and I wouldn't get any special treatment.
Her tone was so sharp and patronizing that I briefly wondered whether I was a guest or a nuisance—especially after paying $160.
It was interesting that she seemed to know I record my videos for Instagram. Especially since I use a full-frame camera with a telephoto zoom lens attached. The idea of ​​me being a photographer didn't seem to occur to her at all.
But if you're building a hotspot for social media fans and promoting it, you shouldn't really get upset about it.
To top it all off, Jenny proudly presented her trained zebra. What was really shown was how she demonstrated her trust in the animal by putting a cloth over its eyes, and yet it still obediently walked "at her side." Last hope... nipped in the bud.
Ultimately, the impression remains of a highly organized tourist program with a lot of staging and little opportunity for genuine animal encounters.
In the end, I was left with a nagging feeling of excessive promotion, sensationalized animal behavior, and an experience that, for me, didn't justify the price and could have offered more substance. Just another ordinary day at the zoo. For us, the day at Cheetahs Rock will not be memorable.

content:
Nagyon különleges és egyedülálló élményt nyújt ez a hely. Miközben rengeteget tanulsz a túra alatt, testközelbe kerülsz vadon élő állatokkal. Nem mindennapi élmény!
Nekem megérte a belépő árát, és az itt eltöltött 5 órát.
Mindenképp olvasd el a honlapon az infókat. Kerüld az élénk, mintás, rikító ruhákat, mert emiatt lemaradhatsz pl a zebra etetéséről.
Fontos, ez a hely nem egy állatkert, vagy cirkusz, és nem az emberek szórakoztatása miatt jött létre. Ez egy állat ‘menhely’, sérült, mentett vadon élő állatok befogadására létesült állat ‘otthon’, ahol az idelátogató megtapasztalhatja milyen testközelből egy zebra, gepárd stb. miközben tanul.
A túra nagyon edukatív, rengeteget lehet tanulni. A személyzet nagyon kedves, segítőkész, rengeteget tudnak az állatokról és nagyon érdekesen adják át az infókat. A munkájukat szívvel lélekkel végzik, hogy jobb sorsuk legyen az idekerült állatoknak.
Mindenképp ajánlom, a látogatásoddal te is hozzájárulsz a világ, de legalábbis az itteni állatok sorsának jobbá tételéhez. Köszönjük a munkátok!
translated_content:

Importantly, this place is not a zoo or circus, and was not created for the entertainment of people. This is an animal 'shelter', an animal 'home' established to accommodate injured, rescued wild animals, where visitors can experience what it's like to be up close with a zebra, cheetah, etc. while learning.
The tour is very educational, you can learn a lot. The staff is very kind, helpful, they know a lot about animals and they provide information in a very interesting way. They do their work with all their heart and soul, so that the animals that come here have a better fate.

Dear Malte,
Thank you for visiting Cheetah’s Rock and for contributing to the care of the rescued animals through your tour fee. We appreciate every guest who helps us continue this work.
For future guests, we would like to clarify a few points mentioned in your review:
1.⁠ ⁠Space and enclosures
Cheetah’s Rock is a CITES-recognised rescue centre. Many of the animals in our care come from confiscations or demanding former conditions and require secure, species-appropriate areas with veterinary oversight and structured enrichment.
All interactions take place in controlled environments — for reasons that are both legal and entirely practical.
Zanzibar is a densely populated island. Allowing rescued wildlife to roam freely would not only be unlawful, it would very quickly result in a situation where only the strongest predator remains.
A thought that may sound appealing in theory, but would end rather swiftly in reality, and certainly not in the animals’ best interest.
2.⁠ ⁠Card payment fees
To avoid misunderstandings: Cheetah’s Rock does not receive any portion of the additional card charges.
All extra fees are applied by the external payment provider. As a self-sustaining rescue centre without outside funding, we rely on receiving the full tour amount to provide veterinary care, specialised nutrition, enrichment, and species-appropriate facilities.
Guests may choose between advance payment or paying on-site; depending on the option selected, external providers may apply additional fees.
Thank you again for supporting the animals in our care and for spending your day with us.
Jenny and the Cheetah’s Rock Team

BEWARE: If it feels wrong, it’s because it is. Here are the key elements that the owner won’t tell visitors.
1. CITES (Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species) has absolutely no connection with ethical practices or animal wellbeing. It only control border movement of the animals.
2. ZIPA (Zanzibar Institute of Protected Areas) only ensures the bare minimum standards determined by Zanzibar, which are notably poor.
3. Research has proven time and time again physical interaction with wild animals generates stress and its detrimental to the animals health. Specially in felines where they spend long periods of time alone. This place provides no opportunity for the animal to retreat, a fundamental welfare issue.
Quoting research:
[Poor Welfare Indicators and Husbandry Practices at Lion (Panthera Leo) “Cub-Petting” Facilities, 2022]
[University of Oxford''s Wildlife Conservation Research Unit]
4. The breeding programs combined with lion cub petting and walking are serious red flags of “Canned Hunting” pipelines. Where animals are bred and used while they are “cute” and harmless, later they are sold to private owners for hunting in private land.
In conclusion, while the desire to have a close encounter with a magnificent animal like a lion or cheetah is understandable, the evidence strongly suggests that facilities offering petting of large carnivores are overwhelmingly unethical.

Vielen lieben Dank für die großartige Erfahrung mit den Ottern . Ein kleiner Traum ging in Erfüllung :-).
Wir hatten soo viel Spaß mit allen Ottern . Das süßeste was wir je gemacht haben. Ich hatte eine schlechte Bewertung gerade gelesen wo sich jemand über Kratzer beschwert hat,was mein Mann und ich sehr lächerlich fanden . Otter sind wilde Tiere, die auch kleine krallen haben. Über sowas sollte man sich vorher informieren! Es tat nicht weh,und wir empfanden es auch nicht als unangenehm. Wir hatten auch den Eindruck das es den Tieren wirklich gut geht. Die Otter hatten so viel Spaß mit uns,dass wir es auch immer wieder machen würden. Der einzige negative Punkt ist, es hat aber absolut nichts mit Cheetah''s Rock zu tun, ich bin übersät mit Mückenstiche 😅 bestimmt an die 30-40 stk . Bin aber generell sehr anfällig dafür . The only downside, which has absolutely nothing to do with Cheetah's Rock, is that I'm covered in mosquito bites 😅 probably around 30-40. I'm generally very prone to them, but with the bushes and the water feature, mosquitoes are unavoidable! We give Cheetah's Rock a 10 out of 10! Thank you so much for the amazing pictures and videos :-). It was FANTASTIC ♡. PS: Feel free to post the pictures on Instagram 💐

response_content:
Dear Sandrine,
At Cheetah’s Rock, transparency and open communication are very important to us, so I would like to clarify a few points for you and for future visitors who may read your review.
Our tours are, as clearly stated on our website, always conducted in English. We answer every question openly in English, but please understand that none of our staff members speak French. This may sometimes lead to a language barrier, although we do our best to explain everything in detail.
What you observed with the cheetahs in our care and with Beppo, our zebra stallion, is not a “performance” but a demonstration of positive reinforcement animal handling. Animals in human care cannot simply be left without stimulation – they need physical and mental enrichment. Learning new things is enrichment, it keeps their minds active and builds trust. Thanks to this training, for example, we were able to vaccinate our young zebras calmly by hand, without stress or sedation – something that would be impossible without this foundation of trust.
Beppo in particular is a wonderful ambassador for this approach. His willingness to engage and to demonstrate his intelligence allows us to share with visitors how communication and respect between humans and animals can grow. 
This is very different from “animal rights” ideology, which often ends with animals being euthanized when they cannot be released into the wild. 
At Cheetah’s Rock, our focus is animal welfare: giving each individual a safe life, meaningful enrichment, and the best possible care.
Many of our guests tell us that seeing these methods firsthand was one of the most valuable and moving parts of their journey – because it shows what true animal welfare means in practice.
Best regards,
Cheetah’s Rock

response_content:
Hallo, Frau Kothe.
Sie haben eine schlechte Bewertung geschrieben, obwohl Sie uns nicht besuchen konnten - weil Besuche ohne Buchung im Voraus nicht möglich sind.
Was uns dabei wirklich traurig stimmt: 
Solche Bewertungen – auch wenn sie nur aus einem Moment der Enttäuschung entstehen - können echten Schaden anrichten ; nicht bei uns, sondern bei den Tieren, für die wir kämpfen. 
Wie aus unserer Website, unserem Google-Profil und allen offiziellen Quellen klar hervorgeht, ist eine Buchung notwendig (pre-booking necessary).
Überall dort stehen auch unsere Tour-Tage und -Zeiten, Preise für die Touren und vieles mehr. 
Bitte sehen sie nochmal nach und entscheiden Sie selbst, ob Sie Ihre Bewertung so stehen lassen möchten oder fairerweise lieber löschen. 
Da ich allerdings Ihre Frustration und die der anderen Menschen verstehe, die aus demselben Grund eine 1-Stern-Bewertung geschrieben haben, wäre es sehr hilfreich für uns, wenn Sie uns wissen lassen könnten, wer Ihnen die Fehl-Information gegeben hat, dass man Cheetah‘s Rock ohne Buchung besuchen kann. 
(Nur die Klinik für Wildtiere ist 24/7 geöffnet.) 
Dies würde in der Zukunft viel Ärger auf beiden Seiten vermeiden. Bitte kontaktieren Sie uns dazu direkt über unsere offizielle Website (Button hier auf Google zum direkten anklicken). Dafür bedanken wir uns im Vorraus.
Wir bedauern sehr, dass Ihr Besuch vorerst nicht geklappt hat und hoffen, Sie doch noch in Ihrem Urlaub bei Cheetah‘s Rock persönlich begrüßen zu dürfen.

Danach wurden wir von einem Maasai zu einem unglaublich schönen Flecken Erde gebracht. Arnoldis on the Cliff Bar and Bites. Wunderschön und sehr lecker.

Anschließend ging es bei Cheetah''s Rock für 4 Stunden weiter mit den anderen geretteten Tieren. Meist sehr erschreckend wenn man erfährt, warum diese Tiere aufgenommen werden mussten.
Schön, dass es solch einen Platz und solche Menschen gibt, die sich so sehr um die Tiere bemühen.
Keines der Tiere wurde gezwungen zu uns zu kommen. Die die kommen wollten kamen und die einen Affen kamen nicht so zu mir, dann war das eben so. Natürlich bekommt man Futter um die Tiere anzulocken, aber es ist nicht so, dass man die Tiere hungern lässt, damit sie kommen. Alle sind sehr gut genährt. Auch werden nicht unendlich viele Besucher zu den Tieren gelassen. Bei den Ottern zum Beispiel waren wir nur zu zweit und es wird nicht täglich gemacht.
Man merkt, dass der höchste Stellenwert das Wohlergehen der Tiere hat, trotzallem können sie ohne Besucher den Tieren nicht mehr helfen.
Für mich war es einer der schönsten Tage in meinem Leben und ich würde es jedem empfehlen. Wenn ich könnte, würde ich 100 Sterne vergeben.

response_content:
Hello Olivia,
Since you have not yet personally visited Cheetah’s Rock, a CITES-recognized rescue and conservation center, we would like to suggest the following:
1. Book an Educational Tour
We invite you to join one of our educational tours to experience firsthand what we do. During the tour:
• You’ll gain insight into our mission and get answers to all your scientific questions from our highly qualified in-house zoologists.
• Learn about the journey of each animal in our care—whether they can one day be released into their natural habitat or, for specific reasons, cannot be.
• Discover the detailed efforts we undertake in collaboration with the State Veterinarian to rehabilitate and release animals whenever possible.
• Hear success stories of animals already released into their natural habitat and the extensive work involved in making it happen.
Feel free to “bombard” our expert staff with your questions. If you still have doubts after your visit, we will gladly put you in direct contact with the State Veterinarian, one of the leading authorities in wildlife conservation here.
By visiting us, you directly support our project, which relies solely on contributions from animal lovers. Your visit helps ensure the well-being of the animals in our care and supports vital animal and environmental protection efforts in Zanzibar.
2. Help an Animal in Need
We would like to give you the opportunity to actively and directly help an animal that, unfortunately, can never be released into its homeland due to legal reasons:
Meet “Judy,” Our Latest Rescue. Judy is a yellow baboon who was discovered by an animal lover in Zanzibar’s hinterland, chained to a tree at a garbage dump. Authorities determined that she had endured this miserable life for eight years after being poached as a baby from the mainland. She survived without protection from the weather, scavenging for food wherever she could, and even learned to open bottles and set them upright to get something to drink.
When Judy was rescued, she immediately hugged us and didn’t want to let go. Her iron shackle was removed, her health was checked, and she was vaccinated. Judy is currently in quarantine while we finish building an enclosure for her, which she will move into next week.
Sadly, Judy cannot be legally released into the wild, either on Zanzibar or mainland Tanzania.
During our 4-hour tour, you’ll learn about individual rehabilitation cases and the challenges involved. Currently, there are no rehabilitation programs for the species we care for anywhere in Africa.
Contrary to popular belief, “lions released into the wild” are often bred for trophy hunting, which remains a significant source of income in Africa, including Tanzania. The truth behind such programs is far from the publicized image of conservation efforts. All details and supporting evidence are shared during the tour.
As the only monkey of her kind on Zanzibar, social interaction is essential for Judy’s well-being. She would be delighted to have you visit, and we believe you wouldn’t want to deny her the joy of a personal cuddle.
All our animal-loving sponsors receive a sponsorship certificate as a token of appreciation. If you cannot visit Judy in person, we would also be happy to send you a short video by email.
We hope you like these two offers.
For bookings or sponsorships, please email us directly at info@cheetahsrock.org.
Sponsors receive a certificate by email without a “price tag.” The amount you choose to contribute to the well-being of “your” animal is entirely up to you.
After your visit and personal experience, we would greatly appreciate a review. Until then, we politely ask that you remove your current review. If, after visiting, you still feel we deserve only one star for our work, we would be genuinely surprised.
Thank you for considering this opportunity to experience and support Cheetah’s Rock.
With animal-loving greetings,
Jenny and the Cheetah’s Rock Team

content:

These animals are so incredibly cared for, all of the training they are given is not for entertainment but enrichment and ensures easier, less stressful administration of medical needs. The care that the owner and her wonderful team have, including Charlie & JJ for these animals is so evident.
For my Mum''s birthday I purchased the otter experience. It was quite simply incredible. Our guide and keeper was Charlie, who was not only lovely, but so informative and he loved those otters so much, and it was evident that they adored him right back. He is the father of otters!!
As a full family we did the full tour today, something that we will never forget. Being able to stroke a cheetah, have lemurs and monkeys bounce onto your shoulders, bush babies crawl into your lap and even meet their newest resident Zebra for a neck scratch..... wow!!
It is so clear how cared for these animals are, they run on only positive reinforcements (mainly food) and each of the interactions are always on the animals terms (the primates have to choose to jump on you!) The rest are free to leave from the people if they wish and return to their enclosures.
You hear so many horror stories as an animal lover of drugged animals, declawed cats etc and Cheetahs Rock couldn''t be further from this. It is truly a place where the animals are cherished and rescued from often awful situations, working with all the relevant authorities to ensure rare species conservation, rescue lions from apartment buildings when kept as pets etc.....
If you''re on the fence, do it. As a proud animal lover with a massive interest in animal welfare, I can say it was one of the most amazing things I''ve ever done. Well done Jenny and team; and thank you for all that you do.

Wir waren gestern dort und es war einfach fantastisch. Wir durften interaktiv sein mit dem Tieren und haben viele Informationen bekommen von den Tierhüter. Alle waren super freundlich und haben versucht jeden mit zu integrieren. Die Tieren werden super behandelt und bekommen immer frisches Futter. DIe Besitzerin wird definitiv nicht reich davon außer ihre Herz . Aber auch sie und die angestellten müssen leben, so bitte keine Verurteilungen hier rein schreiben wenn deine Augen geschlossen sind und das war nett ausgedrückt.
translated_content:

Everyone was incredibly friendly and tried to include everyone. The animals are treated wonderfully and always get fresh food. You can really tell that they love their animals; none of them were pushy about donations or extra money. It was worth every penny we paid. And for people who don't have the money for a safari, it's a great alternative to see the animals.
As for the bad reviews, I can't understand them because it's not a so-called circus or a rip-off. Most of the money goes towards the animals' welfare. content: Very kind and nice People. But no Idea why they call it a rescue Center? About the Lions .. the adult lioness squints, a genetic defect, so do the children. They have 6 Lions there and I found 4 with this eye disease. There is no reason to breed in a rescue center.  Someone said white lions can''t survive in the wild, I saw one adult male with his pride. Anyway the cages and the open space for the Animals are to small. Many People in the Group was happy, but these People never saw animals in the wild. it''s a kind of zoo. If it is a rescue center they would be released some of this animals in the wild.
response_content:
Dear Kirsten,
Thank you for your compliments to our staff for caring so passionately and devotedly for the health and well-being of the wild animals entrusted to our care here at Cheetah''s Rock. 
White lions are an endangered kind. 
Their eyes are healthy but may look unfamiliar to you.
Supporting genetically diverse population increase among sheltered wild animals is important to enable their survival on our planet. 
We are a CITES certified and ZIPA-approved rescue and conservation center. The wildlife authorities here fully support our breeding and rescue activities. Aslan and his partner Savannah are genetically different.
Our goal is for our guests to meet and interact with the wild animals entrusted to our care here at Cheetah''s Rock.
We strongly believe that only if you get to know, respect, and – hopefully - love them, will you care about their survival against habitat destruction and poaching, amongst other threats. That''s why we open our gates to you. People of good will are very welcome here.
For very specific reasons explained on your tour, the wild animals sheltered at Cheetah’s Rock could not be released into the wild. This would mean their imminent death. Surely, you couldn’t approve of this, could you? 
Their enclosures are as natural and generous as possible. They can live, play, and interact with each other there at their leisure. Our resident zoologists and our veterinarians pay close attention to all their well-being. They love meeting our guests as it enriches their social lives.
Your review saddens us and contains quite a few erroneous assumptions. 
Only the white lioness Savannah and her son Timba have an eye condition not rare among their subspecies. It is called pseudo-strabism, is natural and caused by a broad flat bridge of the nose and pronounced epicanthal folds for their eyes which allow the skin on the inner part of the eye lids to extend over and cover the inner part of the eye. It’s natural and is presumed to protect their eyes from dust particles. It is absolutely different from squinting.
Our white lions here at Cheetah’s Rock are Panthera Leo melanochaita. It’s the same subspecies as the tawny South African lion. Aslan and his partner Savannah are not related at all genetically. That is why them having offspring is so valuable for the continuation of their highly endangered line.
Genuine white lions like those living and enjoying their lives here at Cheetah’s Rock possess a recessive leucistic gene, resulting in a partial loss of pigmentation. This genetic condition causes pigment to be visible in their eyes, paw pads, and lips. It’s all perfectly natural.
We are very proud that Timba and his sister Vati are the first genuine white Timbavati lions born in East Africa. It is a conservation success.  As their particular genes responsible for their genuine white color are recessive, if they interbreed with them in an area where tawny lions occur, their recessive white gene that needs to be inherited from both parents’ side will become repressed:  no more white lions in the next generation then.
Wishing you’d realize how such a groundless review such as yours harms, rather than promotes wildlife conservation. This cannot be what you want or intended. Please read our response carefully and rethink your lines, thank you.
Kind regards
Jenny and the Cheetah‘s Rock team

Wir waren gestern bei Cheetah‘s Rock und wir sind überwältigt.
Das war das absolute Highlight unseres Urlaubs.
Es ist schön zu sehen, dass es auch noch Menschen wie bei Cheetah‘s Rock gibt, denen es nicht nur um den Kommerz geht.
Es wird sehr respektvoll und liebevoll mit den Tieren umgegangen. Genau dieser respektvolle und liebevolle Umgang führt meiner Meinung nach dazu, dass man den Tieren so nahe kommen kann wie nirgendwo sonst. Das Team vor Ort leistet eine hervorragende Arbeit und nötigt mir den höchsten Respekt ab!
Wir sind regelrecht geflasht! Ich liebe die Natur und die Tiere und am liebsten erkundige ich das „zufällig“ und lasse die Tiere in Ruhe. Einfach sehen, sich darüber freuen etwas gesehen zu haben und dann weiter gehen. Unter anderem bei den Buschbabies war es schön zu beobachten, als sich ein Tier zurück gezogen hat, dass man es dann auch wirklich in Ruhe gelassen hat. Hier können die Tiere noch selbst entscheiden ob und wie intensiv sie interagieren möchten.
Mario hat sehr proffessionell und humorvoll diese Expedition geleitet. Allen Mitarbeitern merkt man an, dass sie hohen Respekt vor den Tieren haben. Schön zu sehen, dass es noch Orte gibt, an denen man mit den Tieren umgeht wie sie es verdient haben.
Da nimmt man sich gerne die unzähligen Mückenstiche in Kauf.
Irgendwann wollte ich gar keine Fotos mehr machen,  weil ich so fasziniert von allem war und nur beobachten wollte.
Einziger „negativer“ Punkt:
Nach diesem Erlebnis bereuen wir, dass wir nicht die Combined Tour gebucht haben ;-).
Alles Gute an Jenny, Mario und alle Mitarbeiter von Cheetah''s Rock für dieses außergewöhnliche Erlebnis und die tolle Arbeit die hier geleistet wird!
Liebe Grüße
Markus & Christina Wollmann
translated_content:
We visited Cheetah's Rock yesterday and we are overwhelmed.
It was the absolute highlight of our vacation.
It's wonderful to see that there are still people like those at Cheetah's Rock who aren't just in it for the money.
The animals are treated with such respect and love. In my opinion, it's precisely this respectful and loving approach that allows you to get closer to the animals than anywhere else. The team on site does an outstanding job and commands my utmost respect!
We are absolutely blown away! I love nature and animals, and I prefer to explore them "by chance" and leave them in peace. Just observe, enjoy the experience, and then move on. With the bushbabies, for example, it was lovely to see that when one of them retreated, it was truly left alone. Here, the animals can still decide for themselves whether and how intensely they want to interact.
Mario led this expedition with great professionalism and humor. It's clear that all the staff have a deep respect for the animals. It's wonderful to see that there are still places where animals are treated the way they deserve.
You gladly put up with the countless mosquito bites.
At some point, I didn't even want to take any more photos because I was so fascinated by everything and just wanted to observe.
The only "negative" point:
After this experience, we regret not booking the combined tour ;-).
All the best to Jenny, Mario, and all the staff at Cheetah's Rock for this extraordinary experience and the fantastic work they do here!

translated_content:
It was a great tour. It's just a shame Jenny wasn't there, as she understandably had to take care of the puma cubs.
Unfortunately, I have to deduct one star because we couldn't take our bags or backpacks all the way to the enclosures. This meant we were without food for hours, since our bags were locked away at registration. My wife, for example, is diabetic, and her blood pressure plummeted. That's not what I call taking precautions.
Six years ago, we were allowed to take our bags right up to the enclosures.
response_content:
Dear Ralf,
Thank you for your review. We have also seen the review you posted in TripAdvisor. We''re glad that you have shared your experience with us and to hear that you enjoyed the experience and had a great time with the wild animals entrusted to our care. We apologize for any inconvenience caused by our policy of not allowing guests to bring backpacks into the enclosure. 
Rucksacks are large backpacks that can hold many items. We understand that rucksacks are convenient and useful for carrying many items. However, we do not allow rucksacks and other backpacks to the enclosure because they may pose a great threat to small animals. Some animals may play with the rucksacks and go inside them, which can result in injuries or suffocation. The animals in our care are clever and can even open them and eat what they are not supposed to eat. Bigger animals might find your rucksack attractive as a toy, eat on them and in the worst case die from an obstruction. Please understand that the well-being of our animals is our utmost priority and also our guests. 
We understand that this may have affected your comfort and well-being, especially if you have a medical condition like diabetes. We wish you had communicated with our staff during your visit, as they would have been happy to assist you and provide you with other ways to bring what you need for your wife during the tour. I know that in the safety briefing they advise you to store your things but they always offer you to take your items and leave them right in front of the entrance of each single enclosure. Our staff always try their best to help our guests and make their visit more comfortable and enjoyable.  We appreciate your feedback and we will use it to improve our services in the future. Thank you for your visit!
All the best,
Jenny and the Cheetah’s Rock Team

content:
We were at Cheetah''s Rock in November.
Unfortunately, our mood is quite negative and clouded when we think back on it.
We had the option at the time to book a combo tour to visit the two baby lions in the morning. The entrance fee itself for cheetah''s rock is actually already expensive enough, but we had to pay an extra of 250€ for the combo Tour (so in total for two people almost 600€). To top it all off, one of the employees took pictures of my partner and me with the baby lions with his cell phone and we still haven''t received any of those photos. For 250€ extra it would have been quite nice to get at least one picture.
Therefore, unfortunately, a rather negative experience, as we were very much looking forward to the photos.
response_content:
Dear Antonia,
As we informed in the email confirmation, we encourage our guests to bring their own cameras or phones to capture their memories with the animals. We don’t charge anything for pictures. The staff who took pictures of you with his own cell phone was doing it as a personal favour and not as part of our service.
We apologise for the inconvenience caused by not receiving these photos with the baby lions.
We understand how important these memories are for you, unfortunately, due to a technical issue, the photos on our staff member’s camera were lost and cannot be retrieved anymore. We understand how disappointing this must be for you, especially that you were expecting it too much. 
We, of course, would be the happiest if you have received the photos as you informed us previously in the email that you had full of joy in the tour and had a wonderful time with the lion cubs, however, it has gone beyond our control due to the personal phone of our staff got damaged and the datas were unretrievable. 
We ask for your understanding and hope that future visitors rely on their own camera devices.
We hope you can still appreciate the wonderful moments you had with the wild animals entrusted in our care, especially the lion cubs. They are now quite big and I personally think that you have enough reasons to cherish the moment you touched them, fed them, played with them as this was a very limited and privileged time. 
Timba and Vati are the first real white lions born in East Africa and they are doing well thanks to our dear guests. Please keep in mind that we don’t receive any monetary support from our government. 
Do you still think your review is fair?
We always strive to provide our dear guests with an unforgettable and educational encounter with the wild animals entrusted in our care.
Best regards
Jenny and the Cheetah’s Rock Team

Als ich mich nach Ausflüge auf Sansibar erkundigt habe, kam ich sofort auf Cheetah´s Rock. Diesen Ausflug musste ich unbedingt machen, da Geparde meine absoluten Lieblingstiere sind und man sie auch noch streicheln kann! Während der Tour lernt man die verschiedenen Tiere kennen und warum sich dort sind. Teilweise sind das traurige und furchtbare Geschichten. Auch die Eigentümerin Jenny hat sich kurz Zeit genommen, obwohl sie zu unserem Aufenthalt sich um die Löwenbaby kümmern musste.
Zwei kleine Kritikpunkte habe ich allerdings trotzdem. Ich empfand die Gruppenstärke mit 38 Personen deutlich zu groß und unserer Fahrer ist sehr verrückt gefahren ist und hat einfach so fremde Leute noch mitgenommen.
translated_content:
When I was looking for excursions in Zanzibar, Cheetah's Rock immediately came up. I absolutely had to do this trip, as cheetahs are my all-time favorite animals, and you can even pet them! During the tour, you learn about the different animals and why they're there. Some of the stories are sad and terrible. The owner, Jenny, even took a few minutes to talk to us, even though she had to take care of the lion cubs during our visit.
I do have two minor criticisms, though. I felt the group size of 38 people was far too large, and our driver drove very recklessly and picked up strangers without any warning.
response_content:
Lieber Dennis.
Herzlichen Dank für Ihre tolle Beschreibung, was man bei Cheetah‘s Rock erwarten darf.
Sie haben Recht: oft kommen Tiere aus fürchterlichen Verhältnissen zu uns.
Nicht alle sind mit dabei bei den Touren, da wir etliche davon in unsrer Klinik/Quarantäne haben.
Sollte eine Entlassung rechtlich erlaubt sein und auch für das jeweilige Tier Sinn machen, versuchen wir dies gewissenhaft.
Für die anderen Tiere, für die dies nicht gilt, oder die in Arterhaltungs-Zuchtprogrammen sind, versuchen wir so gut wie möglich, ein artgerechtes und schönes Leben zu ermöglichen.
Dazu gehört der Kontakt zu tierlieben Menschen, wie Euch. Dieser stellt eine Bereicherung für deren tägliches Leben dar.
Ja, wir dürfen uns freuen: Timba und Vati, zwei echte weiße Löwen haben am 3. Juni das Licht der Welt erblickt und sind somit die ersten in Ost-Afrika geborenen Timbavati-Löwen, die in der Natur leider bereits als ausgestorben gelten. Damit sind die beiden ein Meilenstein in der Erhaltung.
Wir sind sehr froh, dass nun wieder Urlauber den Weg zu uns finden, nachdem wir für lange Zeit wegen der Covid-Krise auf Spenden angewiesen waren (und dies leider noch einige Zeit sein werden).
Wir haben kein kommerzielles Interesse und bekommen keinerlei finanzielle Unterstützung von unserer Regierung oder NGO’s. Das gesamte Projekt wird Durch tierliebe Besucher ermöglicht.
Unsere Gruppengrösse mit Max. 37 Personen ist so bemessen, dass der Eintrittsbeitrag überschaubar bleibt und es den Tieren in unserer Obhut an nichts fehlt.
Ich habe gerade nachgesehen und Sie haben Recht: an ihrem Besuchstag, dem 19. Juni hat sich ein zusätzlicher Gast „eingeschlichen“. Das passiert selten, aber ärgert mich natürlich.
Eine Gruppe bucht und dann steigen einfach weitere ins Taxi ein. Bei der Ankunft wird dann versucht, alles zu überprüfen; Gäste Buch, disclaimer, Bezahlung . Wir haben in dem Fall den „Übeltäter“ leider erst später “erwischt” und zum Glück hat er bezahlt und sich auch entschuldigt. Er hat es nicht böse gemeint und dachte, man kann hier einfach herein marschieren.

response_content:
Liebe Christine,
Vielen Dank für Ihr Feedback.
Wir freuen uns sehr, dass Sie Ihre Combo-Tour bei Cheetah''s Rock genossen haben.
In der Tat sind Sie herzlich eingeladen, Fotos von und mit all den wilden Tieren zu machen, denen Sie auf Ihrer Tour begegnen.  Es ist etwas ganz Besonderes, diese besonderen Momente festzuhalten, oder?
Wir haben (wie wohl die meisten) unter dieser Krise sehr gelitten und müssen dies leider weiterhin tun.
Um so mehr hatten wir uns sehr gefreut, dass wir an dem Tag Ihres Besuchs endlich und zum ersten und einzigen Mal wieder seit Beginn der Reise-Erschwernisse eine volle Gruppe hatten.
Dies war den Tieren in unserer Obhut leider weder davor noch nach Ihrem Besuch vergönnt.
Ich hätte mich sehr gefreut, wenn Sie dies mit uns hätten feiern wollen.
Wir haben keinerlei kommerzielles Interesse und unsere Preise sind so berechnet, dass wir an allen Tour-Tagen volle Touren haben sollten. Ansonsten müssten wir den Preis erhöhen.
Wie wir jetzt leider erkennen mussten, war es überlebensnotwendig für die Tiere, die bei uns ein sicheres Zuhause gefunden haben, dass wir daneben auch eine Reserve bilden konnten und der Futter-Container mit Fleisch gefüllt war. Dank dieses Protokolls haben die Tiere von der Krise nichts Nachteiliges mitbekommen müssen:
Wir können weiter alle Mitarbeiter in deren Wohl beschäftigen und wir konnten selbst einen der besten Wildtierärzte der Welt einfliegen (Dr. Peter Caldwell/Old Chapel Clinic/South Africa) da es Aslan nicht gut ging. Dies ist unsere Verantwortung und dieser kommen wir nach. Zum Glück hat Aslan sich gut erholt und allen anderen hier geht es dank der Unterstützung unserer tierlieben Gäste sehr gut.
Aslan darf seit seiner Erkrankung nicht mehr von Gästen gefüttert werden, da er im Moment noch 10 kg Hackfleisch pro Tag bekommt, um wieder vollständig „der Alte“ zu sein.
Unsere Hoffnung ist es, die Liebe zu den wilden Tieren in den Herzen unserer lieben Besucher zu verankern. Aus diesem Grund ist die Tour zwar auf 37 Gäste begrenzt, aber einige Tage sind ausgebuchter als andere.
Unsere ansässigen Zoologen bieten jedoch jedem Gast an jedem Tourtag einen vollständigen persönlichen Service.
Unsere Dankes-E-Mail wurde persönlich erstellt mit dem Gruppenfoto und dem Gruppen-Video Ihres Besuchs-Tages, um Ihnen eine kleine Extra-Freude zu machen.
Wir haben den Text leider vor kurzem nicht angepasst, was mir sehr leid tut und nun auch geändert wurde. Aber alle darin erwähnten Tiere sind Ihnen begegnet!
Wir haben neben Maktoum und seinem Bruder Sharqi nun auch zwei Gepardinnen, Latifa und Fatima, die aus anderen Erhaltungszentren zu uns kamen. Mit einem(einer) der Geparden (Gepardinnen) konnten Sie sicherlich sehr schöne Bilder machen.
Mehr Büro-Arbeit würde weniger Zuwendung an die Tiere mit sich bringen.
Ich bin mir sicher, als Tierfreunde haben Sie Verständnis dafür, dass wir dem Tierwohl unsere größte Priorität widmen.
Für eine noch persönlichere Antwort können Sie uns jederzeit gerne eine E-Mail senden, die wir Ihnen sehr gerne beantworten.
Mit tierlieben Grüssen
Jenny und das Cheetah’s Rock Team

content:
This was an excellent experience that I would highly recommend if you have some free time in Zanzibar. First, I want to say that this is a TRUE animal sanctuary through and through (based on the research I did before visiting and also everything I observed while there.) I have visited other rescues in other parts of the world that because of political or economic pressure, have made certain compromises to stay open and be able to maintain operations, but at some expense to their animals. In the situations they are in, they reason that the animals are at least better off there than where they were before (and usually they are), but they have to make their location more lucrative in order to stay afloat. At Cheetah’s Rock, I didn’t witness any such compromise. Their policies always appeared to put animal welfare and visitor safety over gimmick-y tourist attractions (which is much rarer than you would think!), while still maintaining an enjoyable and educational experience for visitors. For example, once lions reach maturity (they are much more aggressive than cheetahs when fully grown), they no longer allow photos with visitors- which is the safest and most humane thing! —
For a more detailed account:
A round trip driver to and from your hotel (for most areas on the island) is included in the price. Our driver was on time, courteous, and got me excited for the visit. Upon arrival, our guide, Shane, was very welcoming and told us what we could expect, briefed us on safety procedures, and was very up front about any risks with specific animals and experiences. It was raining when we arrived, so we started under a covered area, where we met an adorable zebra, Chaka. We were told how staff only use positive reinforcement to build trust in the animals, which not only allow visitors to interact, but more importantly, allow vets to treat the animals without using tranquilizing drugs for routine check-ups, which is much healthier. Then we met a gorgeous puma (who was in heat!) and were told her heartbreaking story before being rescued. We then got to go into an enclosure with some lemurs, who we could feed as they sat on our shoulders, and one of the rarest species in the world, Ploughshare Tortoises!! We also visited a psyches blue monkey and two playful vervets. One of my favorite encounters was with the bush babies! The are super interested in you- sniffing you, preening your hair and giving you lots of love. Then, we were served champagne and refreshments before meeting Aslan the lion! He stays in his enclosure for safety, BUT, volunteers who would rise to the challenges can start by making eye contact, leading to a race up and down the grounds. I volunteered and it was so cool to connect with this lion and get him excited to race, switching back and changing direction while maintaining eye contact. We later saw some beautiful and very rare golden tabby tigers. Finally, of course, we were able to pose with the cheetahs. There were two separate cheetah encounters, both allowing photo opportunities.
The only advice I would give is that someone in your group take your pictures (allowed only for the first cheetah encounter). I was a solo traveler so relied on the staff to take pictures and unfortunately did not get a single usable picture with the cheetahs (almost all were blurry or the cheetah was cut out of the frame). But, the couple that was in my car took their own photos and were very satisfied with theirs (and were a little more pushy with getting photo time). If I went again, I would just have another guest take my pictures☺️. On the second cheetah encounter, our group was a bit time pressured and because of the rain, the sunlight was gone, but we were still able to get very close to an even bigger cheetah and learn about why some were named after the royal family in Dubai. We later saw the adorable otters when passing outside their “night house”.
Thank you Cheetah’s Rock for maintaining your integrity and staying true to your mission❤️❤️

content:
We started our experience at Cheetah''s Rock on the first day with the VIP Otter Experience. It was such a wonderful and amazing experience to feed the little Otter pirates and play in the water with these lively and joyful animals, which were full of energy. They made us smile the full time, we immediately fell in love with Bloody Mary, Cpt. Hook, Cpt. Blackbeard and Cpt. Jack Sparrow. There won’t be any other way than to fully enjoy this encounter. We are recommending the program to everyone. A big thank you as well for Leaveil and Stephan who made us feel very comfortable. They did a fantastic job, they were very kind, friendly, also took pictures about us and the animals and could always answer our questions. They ensured that the animals were always looked after while we (and they) played with them. This created a very pleasant atmosphere.
The Great Wildlife Experience took place on the next day. The tour starts with a welcome coconut water and a mandatory briefing. From the beginning you could see with what dedication, love and passion the employees in Cheetah‘s Rock look after the animals. Their well-being always comes first and is their top priority. They are making no profits out of the tours, all the money goes directly to the animals and helps the team sustain their operations. They are not getting any support from the government, that’s why the entrance fee for such an experience is more than justified. We learned a lot about their vision and goals and about the current situation concerning the flora and fauna in Zanzibar. That’s why their conservation work is even more important. From the staff we learned a lot about the animals at Cheetah‘s Rock. About their species but especially about their individual, mostly very sad back story. The most of the animals are rescued and adopted and due to ongoing physical impairments they will never be released to the wild as it would mean their certain death. At Cheetah‘s Rock they can live a happy, sheltered life in a large and spacious enclosure, which is adapted to their natural habitat. With so many different wild animals living in one place it is of course necessary to have fence between the different enclosures as a safety restraint. The resident Zoologist Stephan had a great deal of knowledge and could answer all the visitor questions in detail. The same applies for Leaveil and the rest of the employees, who led the group through the afternoon in a well-structured manner.
One of the highlights of course was the interaction with the different animals. This was again an experience for a lifetime. For example the soccer play with the zebra stallion Chaka, or having the opportunity to sit beside the cheetah Maktoum and touch him. Or feeding the bush babies, lemurs or monkeys treats while they are jumping from shoulder to shoulder, or helping the white lion Aslan having his 10kg meat per day, while having a refreshment for yourself with sparkling wine or water. It is very nice to see what a great deal of trust there is between the trainers and the animals, which is transferred to the visitors. For example the zebra stallion Chaka is trained to loose its fear of people and to build trust in order to get medical care. That is very important because at Cheetah‘s Rock the animals are not declawed, defanged, drugged in order to treat them nor forced to do anything by force. The interaction with the trainer or the visitors also enriches their lives so that they do not get bored.
We definitely recommend visiting Cheetah‘s Rock and if it’s possible to book both available programs. You do not only get educated very well, you also get the opportunity to get very close to a lot of wild animals, to touch and feed them, which leaves you with a breathtaking feeling. At Cheetah‘s Rock they mediate perfect consciousness for wildlife conservation. Your visit will not only enrich your, but also the animals life. A big thank you to the staff for making it an unforgettable experience and providing us two of the best days of our lives.
Kinga & Benedikt

Aus unsere Sicht ein Muss für jeden Zanzibar-Besucher!

content:
It all goes down to your expectations and why you’re here.
If you’re here because of your love for animals, then you came to the right place. If you’re here because of the good cause of protecting endangered animals, then you’re definitely in the right place. But if you’re here to have sufficient time interacting one-on-one with the big cats, then you’ll likely be disappointed.
Here’s the itinerary:
1)) you arrive and get welcomed with fresh coconut water.
2)) you wait for everybody else to arrive, approximately 30 in total
3)) you get briefed for an hour about safety procedures, their mission, global climate etc. by an enthusiast that you’d enjoy listening to.
4)) you start with a Zebra interaction (feeding, playing with and petting) that takes about an hour, feels childish but yet entertaining.
5)) you move to Bush Monkeys interaction then to Lemur (so-called Lima Monkey), then to Dik-Dik, then to a rare specie of tortoises and peacocks. You get to see also a gorgeous rescued Cougar in a cage.  That’s another 2 hours of feeding and petting.
6)) here comes the long waited gorgeous majestic 5 years old white lion. Of course you get to learn about it and see it from behind the cage. You get to feed it from behind the cage too.
7)) then you’re walked and briefed from behind the cage while they feed two cubs a Liger and a Tiger. Both are breathtakingly beautiful.
8)) this is followed by a photo shoot with two beautiful Cheetahs inside their enclosure but without any interaction more than petting its back while being photographed for few seconds, for the next in turn to do the same.
9)) lastly you’re surprised by meeting two young cubs (lion and tiger) who got walked on a leash separately to get close to the audience to pet their back as they swiftly walk past them.
Personally I feel like every one-on-one interaction is rushed due to the large number of the audience from start to finish. And especially when it comes to the big cats, I feel I left Cheetah’s Rock longing for more than what I got. I was told there’s a VIP experience that provides that, but personally I didn’t know about it, and even if I did I’d not have known what to expect from the original one verses the VIP one. Therefore I hope my review helps future visitors to decide.
response_content:
Dear Hassaan,
Thank you for stating that Cheetah''s Rock is a wonderful place for animal lovers to meet, and interact with, our wild animals. Your photos give future visitors a good idea of what can be experienced at Cheetah''s Rock.
We try to strike a careful balance between enabling as many of our dear guests to come on the tour, while still keeping it close and personal. Interaction with the wild animals, including the big cats, is never rushed, but appropriate for each big cat you meet.
Just a little comment that we don''t have any Liger, but lion and lionesses, and Golden Tabby Bengal Tiger and Tigress. You met her as a surprise at the end of the tour just as you describe.
Thank you for keeping an open mind about our work and for describing in detail some of the important aspects of our tour.
All the best
Jenny and the Cheetah’s Rock Team

content:
Auf meinen Wunsch haben wir während unserer Flitterwochen auf Zanzibar auch Cheetahs Rock besucht. Statt eines fröhlichen Ausflugs hatten wir aber während all der traurigen Geschichten von misshandelten, getöteten und wer-weiß-was noch für Geschichten schon nach kurzer Zeit keinen Spaß mehr an der Tour. :-(
Dir Gruppe war so riesig (beinahe 40 Personen) das fand ich als Tierfreund eigentlich unzumutbar. Das Zebra wurde behandelt wie im Zirkus und musste Kunststücke aufführen. Ich habe keineswegs das Gefühl, dass die Tiere schlecht behandelt werden, aber naja, ich hatte dennoch kein gutes Gefühl dabei. Uns als Besuchern wurde eher das Gefühl gegeben, man solle nicht hier sein, sondern sie machen die Touren nur um Geld einzunehmen: basta. Tierleben kommt vor Menschenwohl. Das wurde mehr als einmal betont. Ich hatte mir den Traum erfüllen wollen, einmal einen Gepard zu berühren. Leider hatte ich Pech und wurde (zum Glück nur leicht!) von einem, der beiden herumlaufenden Leoparden am Knie angeknabbert. Ich war so in Panik, ich wusste nicht, ob ich was sagen durfte, ohne das Tier aufzuhetzen. Zum Glück hat er von mir abgelassen. Das war genug für einen Tag. Der Tag war sehr anstrengend, Highlight waren die Lemuren und Buschbabys. Die durfte man immerhin streicheln. Wenn dies aufgrund der vielen Besucher auch sehr chaotisch war. Ich würde es niemandem empfehlen dorthin zu gehen. Spendet lieber das Geld, da ist den Tieren mehr mit geholfen.
translated_content: At my request, we also visited Cheetah's Rock during our honeymoon in Zanzibar. However, instead of a joyful excursion, we quickly lost all enjoyment of the tour due to all the sad stories of abuse, murder, and who knows what else. :-( The group was so huge (almost 40 people) that, as an animal lover, I found it unacceptable. The zebra was treated like it was in a circus and had to perform tricks. I don't feel the animals were mistreated at all, but well, I still didn't feel good about it. We visitors were given the impression that we shouldn't be there, that they only run the tours to make money: period. Animal welfare comes before human well-being. This was emphasized more than once. I had wanted to fulfill my dream of touching a cheetah. Unfortunately, I was unlucky and was (luckily only lightly!) nipped on the knee by one of the two leopards roaming around. I panicked so much, I didn't know if I could say anything without provoking the animal. Luckily, it left me alone. That was enough for one day. The day was very tiring; the highlight was the lemurs and bush babies. At least you were allowed to pet them, even if it was very chaotic due to the large number of visitors. I would I wouldn't recommend anyone go there. It's better to donate the money; that will help the animals more.

column25: #cheetahsrock #cheetahsrockzanzibar Jenny's mission, which created this place, is summed up in the first photo at the reception: "Animals have a voice. If you ignore their suffering, I'll remind you. If you don't understand them, I'll translate for you. If you can't hear them, I'll be their voice. You can silence them, but you can never silence me as long as I live." An incredible place, where animals are saved from human cruelty, zoos, black market trade, and poachers. Jenny, along with her son, Stephan, and other wonderful people, explain the story of each animal. You can interact with them with the necessary precautions because the animals are not sedated or drugged, and the first priority is respect for them. They don't have "cages," but enclosures with enormous spaces where they can move freely. Unfortunately, they can't be released back into the wild because they wouldn't survive. Here, they're trying to preserve the species and help them reproduce, animals like Aslan the white lion and his "future wife," Savannah, who are at risk of extinction due to human stupidity. They don't receive any funding, so with our visit, we contribute to their cause, in addition to having a unique experience. Jenny is moved when she talks about the atrocities she has to witness; you can see her love for her mission and her animals, and this goes for all her staff. If you go to Zanzibar, don't forget this place. Thank you, Jenny, for everything you do. ❤

response_content:
Dear Katie,
Thank you for your big praise of our work for our wild animals that you feel is truly amazing. We do offer our guests after arrival a fresh coconut at our reception and a glass of sparkling wine or mineral water half way of the tour. If you become really thirsty during the tour, a staff member on the ground can
escort you to the reception where we always have mineral water in our office.
The reason why we ask all guests not to wear mosquito repellant is that many of our wild animals will be in close contact with you. As they rub their fur against your skin, they would take on some of the repellant. Later, when they lick their fur to clean it, the poison would enter their system. That is why we advise guests if they are very sensitive to mosquitos to wear long-sleeve shirts, long pants with socks tucked into them. This minimizes the danger of getting bitten - and keeps the wild animals free from inadvertently poisoning themselves after cuddling with you. Thank you for your understanding.
All the best
Jenny and the Cheetah’s Rock Team

content: Это контактный зоопарк, заходишь в клетки, садишься, к тебе в клетку впускают ручных животных, их можно кормить (дают чем), можно потрогать, пофотать. What I didn't like: there were a lot of people, and the presenter talks a lot, A LOT, A LOT! It just got tiresome. It's worth a one-time visit! Overall, Forodhani Gardens is not just about food — it’s about the experience. The combination of great local flavors, a lively atmosphere, and a scenic seaside location makes it a must-visit when you’re in Stone Town.

content:
Forodhani Gardens is one of the most vibrant and memorable places to visit in Stone Town, Zanzibar. Located along the seafront, this public garden transforms every evening into a lively night food market that attracts both locals and tourists. As the sun sets over the Indian Ocean, the area fills with the aroma of grilled seafood, spices, and freshly prepared street food.
One of the most popular dishes is the famous Zanzibar pizza, a unique stuffed flatbread that can be made sweet or savory. Visitors can also enjoy mishkaki grilled meat skewers, samosas, urojo soup, and a variety of freshly squeezed fruit juices. The food is affordable, and there are many options to choose from, making it a great place to sample local flavors.
The atmosphere at Forodhani is energetic and social. Vendors call out to customers, friends gather to eat together, and children play nearby. The ocean breeze and beautiful sunset views add to the experience. Although it can become crowded and busy at night, the lively environment is part of its charm.
Overall, Forodhani Gardens offers an authentic taste of Zanzibar’s culture, cuisine, and community life.

Фородхани-парк в Стоун-Тауне — место, где оживает вечер. Днем там жарко и тихо, но с заходом солнца всё меняется. Из ниоткуда появляются прилавки, дым от мангалов висит в воздухе, пахнет морепродуктами, специями и соками.
Главное — не спешить. Просто бродить, выбирать, что попробовать. Кальмары, осьминоги, креветки, пицца по-занзибарски, свежий сок из сахарного тростника. Люди вокруг улыбаются, торгуются, шутят. Атмосфера лёгкая, теплая, немного хаотичная, но по-своему уютная.
Если хочешь почувствовать настоящий Стоун-Таун — иди туда вечером. Это не просто еда, это кусок жизни острова.

Forodhani Park in Stone Town is where the evening comes to life. It's hot and quiet during the day, but everything changes as the sun sets. Stalls appear out of nowhere, smoke from barbecues hangs in the air, and the smell of seafood, spices, and juices fills the air.
The key is to take your time. Just wander around, choosing what to try. Squid, octopus, shrimp, Zanzibar pizza, fresh sugarcane juice. People are smiling, bargaining, and joking. The atmosphere is light, warm, a little chaotic, but cozy in its own way.
If you want to experience the real Stone Town, go there in the evening. It's not just food; it's a slice of island life.

content:
Los Jardines de Forodhani (también conocidos como Jardines del Jubileo y, más recientemente, como Parque Forodhani ) [ 1 ] son ​​un pequeño parque en la histórica ciudad de Stone Town , Zanzíbar , Tanzania . Se encuentran a lo largo del paseo marítimo principal de Stone Town, justo frente a sus edificios más famosos: la Casa de las Maravillas y el Fuerte Viejo.
Los jardines se llenan especialmente después del atardecer, cuando turistas y lugareños se reúnen en un popular mercado callejero de comida en la plaza principal, para cenar y disfrutar de las delicias de la cocina swahili y zanzibarí, como mariscos a la parrilla , samoosas , yuca y batatas .
El 31 de julio de 2009, el Aga Khan celebró la ceremonia de colocación de la primera piedra para inaugurar un parque revitalizado.
La rehabilitación estuvo a cargo del Aga Khan Trust for Culture (AKTC) con un coste de 3 millones de dólares (3.900 millones de chelines), frente a las estimaciones iniciales de 2,4 millones de dólares (más de 3.000 millones de chelines).
La remodelación incluyó la restauración de las pasarelas peatonales, el paisajismo, la modernización de la infraestructura, la incorporación de iluminación, el sistema de alcantarillado y los servicios públicos, y la rehabilitación del malecón frente al parque
translated_content:
The Forodhani Gardens (also known as the Jubilee Gardens and, more recently, as Forodhani Park) [1] are a small park in the historic city of Stone Town, Zanzibar, Tanzania. They are located along Stone Town's main waterfront, directly opposite its most famous buildings: the House of Wonders and the Old Fort.
The gardens are especially busy after sunset, when tourists and locals gather at a popular street food market in the main square to dine and enjoy the delights of Swahili and Zanzibari cuisine, such as grilled seafood, samoosas, cassava, and sweet potatoes.
On July 31, 2009, the Aga Khan held a groundbreaking ceremony to inaugurate a revitalized park.
The rehabilitation was undertaken by the Aga Khan Trust for Culture (AKTC) at a cost of $3 million (3.9 billion shillings), compared to initial estimates of $2.4 million (over 3 billion shillings).
The renovation included the restoration of pedestrian walkways, landscaping, infrastructure modernization, the addition of lighting, a new sewage system and utilities, and the rehabilitation of the waterfront promenade in front of the park.

content:
Nestled in the heart of Stone Town, The Forodhani Hotel offers an authentic and charming experience for travelers seeking cultural immersion in Zanzibar. Its prime location, directly across from the famous Forodhani Gardens and a short stroll from the seafront, makes it ideal for exploring the island’s vibrant history, food, and local life.
The rooms are simple yet comfortable, equipped with air conditioning, clean bathrooms, and traditional Swahili décor that reflects the heritage of the island. Some rooms offer sea views, enhancing the coastal atmosphere of your stay. The rooftop terrace is a hidden gem – perfect for catching sunsets or enjoying breakfast with a view.
The staff are friendly, helpful, and welcoming, always ready to assist with directions, tours, or special requests. While it’s not a luxury hotel, Forodhani provides excellent value for money and is ideal for travelers who prioritize location, cultural charm, and warm hospitality.
Overall, The Forodhani Hotel is a great choice for those who want to feel the pulse of Stone Town, enjoy local flavors, and stay within walking distance of major attractions like the Old Fort, House of Wonders, and bustling night markets.
Highly recommended for budget-conscious explorers!

translated_content: Fish market on the promenade in the capital of Zanzibar - Stone Town. It's worth going here in the evening when all the stalls offer different types of seafood. Pay attention to the prices and bargain. At first they caught me with the price for two skewers, one chicken and one shrimp. The chef asked for 20 dollars. Then I found out that one skewer costs from 7000 shillings which is about 3 dollars. So I overshot quite a bit, but in general, for example, freshly squeezed sugar juice costs 1000 shillings, a small tasty kebab in your hand costs 2500 shillings. I recommend this place with an empty stomach, everyone will find their own nutella pancakes, sea monsters, fresh fruit juices and much more.

content:
The Heart of Zanzibar’s Street Food Scene
Forodhani Gardens is a must-visit spot in Stone Town, Zanzibar, especially in the evening when the lively night food market comes to life. Located along the scenic waterfront, it’s the perfect place to experience local culture, delicious Swahili cuisine, and a vibrant atmosphere.
The highlight here is the fresh seafood grills, where you can try everything from lobster and prawns to octopus and tuna skewers. Don’t miss the famous Zanzibar pizza, a unique street food snack, or the refreshing sugarcane juice.
Beyond the food, the gardens offer stunning sunset views over the Indian Ocean, with local musicians and performers adding to the charm. It’s safe, welcoming, and a great spot to relax after exploring Stone Town’s historic streets.
If you’re in Zanzibar, Forodhani Gardens is the perfect place to taste the island’s flavors and soak in the local vibe! 🌴🌊🍢 #ForodhaniGardens #ZanzibarFood #StoneTown

row_id: Overall, it's a fantastic place, but... unfortunately, the local crooks decided to pull off a massive culinary scam here! I'm giving it one star because the park itself should have received five stars, but the event that takes place here every evening, the outdoor grilled food (I specifically say "food" because it can't be called food) is the biggest Zanzibar disaster imaginable! They're ripping tourists off with prices around $10 for a tiny skewer that finally lands on your plate without a skewer, meaning you don't even know if it's what you ordered, because the taste leaves much to be desired. Of course, you order first, then the local guides you to a place where you can eat in peace, and when you ask about the price, you receive evasive answers and the assurance that "you'll pay later." Unfortunately, after devouring the questionable quality of the grilled food, you're met with a bucket of cold water in the form of a bill equivalent to a ten-course dinner at a luxury restaurant. We argued about the price and paid much less, which doesn't mean it's acceptable considering the quality and location. I'm not one to write negative reviews, but I HAD to do so here to warn others. content:
Good collection of foods and amusements. However, I''m expecting more cleanliness. The same hot oil on a pan is used for frying various foods (veg and non-veg). The local people''s food habits and preparation styles are probably like that. I saw lots of people enjoying themselves. Jumping on the ocean during the evening is really a very dangerous play and probably the trademark of this play. People are highly jovial, friendly, and welcoming. They never mind if you don''t take any food from them after enjoying the preparation or spending time in front of their stall. I am here with my family and spending two evenings in this place—a perfect place for spending the evening and rejuvenating yourself. We have not taken any food from this park as we want to keep us away from non-veg items.

content:
Out of all the experiences in Zanzibar, this one was my favourite.
It was my first time zip-lining, and no better place to do it than in the land of your descendants.
I was with my family, and we ran into the director whilst we were there. They shared what it took to bring this experience to life in Zanzibar and what their visions are going forward. Greatly appreciate them sharing their insights.
The members of the team who took us through the forest were also so friendly and informative. One of my family members was imploring them to make it known that “this is the world’s LONGEST single span zip line in East Africa”.
It was incredibly beautiful to see a part of Zanzibar from above, but walking through it was also curative.
There are several trails, some of which are a little difficult, but the plants and animals will make you overlook this and propel you to challenge yourself.
I would do it all over again.
There were quite a few things under construction, e.g. restaurant, zip line end, etc., when I was there, so hopefully when I return, it’ll be good to see the new additions and enhancements.
Please DO NOT build the viewpoint, I personally don’t think it’s necessary. From where we were standing, it was a sufficient view (less is more in this case).

content:
Very nice location in the middle of the beach and good friendly and laid back school manager and teachers. Joao did a great job and was patient with us. Prices are steep though. Had lots of fun and great experience overall.
One thing I’d like to point out is that the school or rather the instructors should ensure that if you pay for two hours’ tuition, you actually get two hours of active instruction. We actually started lessons late on a regular basis – partly due to preparations, choosing the right kite and walking to the training spot, or simply because everything moved at a slower pace and last time I checked we literally started the lesson with a 15 min delay (which is totally fine, as it’s all ‘pole pole’ and ofc preparations are also part of the learning), but we’d then finish early and were, so to speak, already out of the water before the end of the two hours,  meaning you effectively only had 1.5 hours of lessons (sometimes it felt like just one hour). I understand that other people might have a lesson session afterwards, but in future it should be planned a bit more efficiently.

content:
Cours dans un très bel environnement. Jordy, l''instructeur était super : pédagogue, patient, encourageant. Les conditions sont réunies pour apprendre le kite dans de bonnes conditions.
Par contre, j''ai eu des problèmes avec les pratiques douteuses du propriétaire de l''école :
- le matériel était en très mauvais état
- - j''ai reçu plusieurs messages pour me demander de payer plus, car j''avais réservé et payé des cours semi privés. Ils n''ont mis aucun autre élève dans mes cours... et ont attendu la fin pour me demander de payer un supplément car j''étais seule lors des cours.
- ils ne veulent pas compléter mon IKO (apparemment je dois payer un supplément de 20 €... ou payer le fameux supplément du dessus et les 20€ sont offerts)
- j''ai reçu plusieurs messages pour me demander de revoir ma note (j''avais mis 4 étoiles initialement - avant les demandes de facturation supplémentaires)
Moniteur : top
École : à fuir
translated_content:
Lessons in a beautiful setting. Jordy, the instructor, was great: patient, encouraging, and a good teacher. The conditions are perfect for learning kitesurfing.
However, I had some issues with the school owner's questionable practices:
- The equipment was in very poor condition.
- I received several messages asking me to pay more because I had booked and paid for semi-private lessons. They didn't add any other students to my lessons... and waited until the end to ask me to pay extra because I was alone during the lessons.
- They refuse to complete my IKO (apparently I have to pay an additional €20... or pay the aforementioned additional fee and the €20 is waived).
- I received several messages asking me to revise my rating (I initially gave 4 stars - before the requests for additional charges).
Instructor: Excellent
School: Avoid at all costs
response_content:
Thank you for taking the time to share your feedback. We’re happy to hear that you enjoyed the location and that you had a very good experience with your instructor.
Regarding the points you mentioned, we would like to clarify a few important details:
Your booking was made through a tour agency, which is fully aware that semi-private lessons are only possible when two people book together. Unfortunately, this was a booking mistake on their side. Despite this, we did not charge you any extra and honored the private lesson price for your first course, even though you were alone.
The additional hours you decided to take were done as private lessons, and this was clearly communicated to you in advance. The extra charge requested was only for those additional private hours which at the end you didn''t pay .
Concerning the IKO card, the €20 fee is not charged by our school, but by IKO itself. This is a standard and very common practice worldwide, and many schools apply the same fee.
We would also like to clarify that we never asked you to change or rewrite your review. Your instructor simply asked if everything was okay after the lessons, which is part of our normal follow-up with students.
Regarding the equipment: we use Duotone gear only, which is one of the leading brands in kitesurfing. Our equipment is modern, regularly renewed, and among the newest models available, as safety and performance are a top priority for us.
We always aim to be transparent and fair, and we regret that this situation left you with a negative impression despite our efforts to accommodate the booking error that was not made by us.
We wish you all the best for your future kiteboarding experiences.
Cheers,
Baris and Stephanie
Kite Centre Zanzibar

content:
Unbiased, honest review after spending 7 days here: Kite Center Zanzibar is hands down THE BEST KITESURFING CENTER in all of Paje! 😊 WE ABSOLUTELY LOVED SPENDING OUR DAYS HERE!
My friends and I came to Zanzibar on a 7-day holiday to do kitesurfing. We did a lot of research before hand and decided we will be using Kite Center Zanzibar as our preferred choice throughout our stay. Little did we know, this was the best decision we have made throughout this trip! Even after arriving to Zanzibar, on our first day we went to check out multiple schools on the beach (B4, Aquaholics, and several others). However, none were as friendly and accommodating as the team over at Kite Center Zanzibar.
We were first greeted by Stephanie! Who is super friendly, always smiling and easy going - an absolute pleasure to deal with! She explained to us all details about the spot, entry point to the lagoon, location of the reef, areas with seaweed farms (a place you should not go to during low tide), and all other aspects of where to ride in the lagoon. She also gave us a walk around the center and where all facilities were. We later met Baris whom we were also dealing with on daily basis and he was very kind and friendly with all our requests and inquiries. The crew on the ground helping us out (especially Saeed) were super kind and looking out for us all the time!
My friend and I know how to kite so we brought our gears with us. We rented a locker for the entirety of the week and it was brand new and clean. Felt very safe keeping our gear there.
Our 3rd friend is new to kitesurfing so he took the beginner course with their team members and absolutely loved it. They have very clean, well maintained equipment for students (walkie talkie, helmets, vests, etc). My other friend also took a 1-hour advanced lesson with Coach Mohammed to learn transition and he managed to do it from the first trial!! Absolutely brilliant! 😁
I personally rented a 17m kite on the days with low wind and it was in great condition!
Honestly, this was our first time in Zanzibar and it was such an unforgettable experience, mainly because we spent a great deal of time (most of our mornings) at Kite Center Zanzibar with Baris, Stephanie and the rest of the team!! We loved it so much that we wanted to extend a few more days but we had to return home for work :( - Next time inshAllah!

🏄‍♂️🪁 Three Weeks of Kite Fun:
During my extended stay in June 2024, I rented kite equipment from Kite Centre Zanzibar, and let me tell you—it was three weeks of pure kitesurfing euphoria! 🤩 The gear? All Duotone branded, top-notch quality, and in impeccable condition. 🙌
🤝 Friendly Faces Everywhere:
Baris, Steffi, and the whole staff were like a kitesurfing dream team. Super friendly, fun, and always ready to provide tips on how to nail my next jump! 🏄‍♂️🚀 Thanks for everything!
🌊 Double the Fun:
Paje, oh Paje! This place is a kitesurfer’s paradise. The winds in late June were on point, and you get to kite on not one, but often two totally different waters on the same day 🌊 The flat lagoon is perfect for beginners, while the choppy water (thanks, tides!) adds an extra thrill for advanced riders.
🏝️Stunning lagoon views and great location:
Imagine kiting with a stunning view, the lagoon vista is straight-up magical. Also right next door is Mr. Kahawa, where you can refuel your energy levels after those intense sessions ☕ while enjoying the views - believe you won’t ever get enough of it (and yes I already miss it!) 🌅 And if you’re lucky you might even see some cute monkeys around 🐒
💰 Quality Comes at a Price 💰 Yes, the prices lean toward the higher end, but honestly, it’s worth every of your hard earned Shillings. When you’re soaring through the air, harnessing the wind, you’ll know why. 🚀
So, grab your board, catch the breeze, and let Kitecenter Zanzibar elevate your kitesurfing game! 🌬️🏝️

content: Het begon met dat wij bij het kite centre aankwamen en hier niemand met onze eerste lesdag rekening had gehouden. Er moest dus nog iemand per direct opgetrommeld worden zodat we konden starten met een relatief dure cursus (na het later vragen om prijzen bij locals en zoeken bij kitescholen in NL). We hadden nog nooit gekite en hebben geen enkele theoretische uitleg gehad of iemand die even waarschuwde over het heftige verbrandingsgevaar hier (en dat terwijl de eigenaren Nederlands zijn). Heel erg vervelend want daarna moest ik nog 2 dagen het water in. Nu, 2 maanden later, zijn die heftige verbrandingen door de zon nog steeds zichtbaar (en ja, ik smeerde wel zonnebrand en had een t-shirt aan). Niemand dacht op geen enkel moment mee. Dat bleek ook toen ik noodgedwongen een shirt met lange mouwen bij hen in de winkel moest kopen voor €60,-. Zelfs toen wilden ze me niet even netjes helpen in de winkel zoals gebruikelijk in een winkel. Zeker zo''n winkel bij een duikschool. Na bijna 1 week in Paje kwamen we de eigenaren regelmatig tegen en terwijl wij ''hoi'' zeiden kwam er bij hen geen woord uit. Ik zie verder weinig slechte reviews dus mogelijk hadden wij gewoon pech met verschillende zaken. Een slechte week met tegenvallers gehad misschien? We hebben met niemand meer gesproken en gewoon stilletjes onze kite cursus afgemaakt. Deze was verder prima en ook de spullen waren goed.
translated_content: It started with us arriving at the kite centre and finding that no one there had taken our first day of lessons into account. So, someone had to be rounded up immediately so we could start a relatively expensive course (after later asking locals for prices and searching at kite schools in the Netherlands). We had never kited before and received no theoretical explanation whatsoever, nor did anyone warn us about the severe risk of sunburn here (even though the owners are Dutch). It was very annoying, because I still had to go into the water for another two days after that. Now, two months later, those severe sunburns are still visible (and yes, I did apply sunscreen and wore a t-shirt). No one was willing to help at any point. This also became apparent when I was forced to buy a long-sleeved shirt in their shop for €60. Even then, they wouldn't help me properly in the shop, as is customary in a store. Especially a shop like this at a dive school. After almost a week in Paje, we ran into the owners regularly, and while we said 'hi,' they didn't say a word. I see few bad reviews otherwise, so perhaps we just had bad luck with various things. Maybe we had a bad week with setbacks? We didn't speak to anyone anymore and just quietly finished our kite course. That was fine otherwise, and the equipment was good too.
