content:
Rekl bych ze pomerne SCAM od Cedoku co nam to prodal. Maji byt zastavky na krasne piscite plazi, na šnorchlování, u hvezdic, modra laguna a obed na ostrove kde jde nejvetsi baobab strom.
Ve vysledku z hotelu 1:30 busem, pak priserna spinava cesta lesem plna odpadku nez dojdete na plaz. Dalsi skoro hodinove cekani na nalodeni a brodeni se v melcine (kde jsou jezkove) az k lodi, protože na clun uz bylo malo vody.
Plaveni na lodi prijemne, tam snad neni co zkazit. Prvni zastavka snorchlovani, kde lod zaparkovala u dalsich 10 a pruvodce řekl Jump a hotovo, vic ze nestatal, neukazal. K videni par rybek, zbytky koralu a kdyz zrovna necerila jina lod vodu, dalo se potapet. Kdo zna treba rude more, tady toho je zlomek. Ale prijemne, plavani.
Zastavka 2: písečný blob, ktery vypada hezky pri přílivu, ale byl odliv, takze kilometr mrtvych koralu a hromadka písku. Na ni desitky docasnych pristresku kde cestovky nabizi ovoce. A pres 300+ turistu co nechape na co se tam maji divat. Na hotelu je lepsi pisek (bily), tady zluty. A pochopitelne odpadky, takze plavajici kus ananasu, ci melounu, bezna vec. Rychle jsme se jako posadka lodi sesla a chteli jsme se nalodit a odjet, krom davu tam neni nic.
Zastavka 3: misto na potapeni za hvezdicemi. Asi si pletou pojem starfish (hvezdice) a jellyfish (meduza). Protoze hvezdici nasel pruvodce jednu malou a zato meduz ze neslo plavat. Osobne jsem hevzdici nenasel na dne zadnou. Ale ano, kus koralu se sasankou a  klaunem ockatym (nemo) bylo fajn. Kdyz jsme pruvodci vysvětlovali ze u hotelu mame desitky hvezdic ruznych velikosti, vic nez tu jednu nenašel. Ono když je vyndavaji ven z more, nedivim se, ze umreli uz.
Zastavka 4: ostrov se stromem baobab a obedem. Spoiler alert: 500 let stary strom spadnul a na korenech puvodniho roste nový. U stromu jsou pochopitelne desitky lidi, takze ho sotva vidíte. Na ostrove je hromada stánku a snazi se vam neco vnutit.
Obed je jedine co bylo fajn, pokud ovšem jite morske plody. Jina varianta nebyla. Ale zena si humra pochvalovala.
Zastavka 5: modra laguna. Viz samostatna recenze. Zajimavy prirodni ukaz, laguna vymletá v koralech, mangovniky co maji koreny do vody. Nevideli jsme, byl uz priliv. Jinak laguna kde zastaví 30+ lodi a turisty zenou do vody. Do vody kde kdyz je priliv, priveze to vsechen bordel a z lodi cítíte vuni benzinu. Nikdo z nasi posadky se tam neodvazil skocit a jeli jsme raději domu.
Kdyz to shrnu: hvezdice najdete kousek od restaurace The Rock na sever, na plazi najdete nekoho kdo vas tam ochotne odveze, nebo tam jde doplavat. Pisek je lepsi na vychodni strane pobrezi. Na potapeni je lepsi rude moře.
Z vytelu co jsme kdy na vsech dovolenych meli, je toto prvni kde davam 1 hvězdu, protoze 0 dat nejde. Vyhozene penize 75$/os.
translated_content:
I would say it was a complete SCAM from Cedok who sold it to us. They have stops at beautiful sandy beaches, snorkeling, starfish, the blue lagoon and lunch on an island where the biggest baobab tree is.
As a result, from the hotel at 1:30 by bus, then a terrible dirt road through the forest full of garbage before you get to the beach. Another almost hour of waiting to board and wading in the shallows (where there are sea urchins) to the boat, because there was little water for the boat.
Swimming on the boat was pleasant, there is probably nothing to spoil there. The first stop was snorkeling, where the boat parked with 10 others and the guide said Jump and that's it, because he wasn't standing, he didn't show. There were a few fish to see, the remains of coral and if another boat wasn't splashing water, you could dive. Who knows the Red Sea, there is a fraction of it here. But pleasant, swimming.
Stop 2: a sandy blob that looks nice at high tide, but it was low tide, so a kilometer of dead coral and a pile of sand. On it, dozens of temporary shelters where tour companies offer fruit. And over 300+ tourists who don't understand what they are supposed to be looking at there. The hotel has better sand (white), here yellow. And of course garbage, so a floating piece of pineapple or watermelon, a common thing. We quickly sat down as the crew of the boat and wanted to board and leave, except for the crowd there is nothing there.
Stop 3: a place to dive for starfish. I guess they confuse the terms starfish and jellyfish. Because the guide found one small starfish, but the jellyfish was not swimmable. Personally, I didn't find any starfish on the bottom. But yes, a piece of coral with an anemone and a clownfish (nemo) was nice. When we explained to the guide that there are dozens of starfish of different sizes near the hotel, he didn't find more than one. When they take them out of the sea, I'm not surprised that they've already died.
Stop 4: island with a baobab tree and lunch. Spoiler alert: a 500-year-old tree fell and a new one originally grows on its roots. Understandably, there are dozens of people near the tree, so you can barely see it. There are a lot of stalls on the island and they try to force something on you.
Lunch is the only thing that was nice, if you eat seafood. There was no other option. But the woman praised the lobster.
Stop 5: blue lagoon. See separate review. Interesting natural spectacle, lagoon ground in corals, mango trees with roots in the water. We didn't see it, it was already high tide. Otherwise a lagoon where 30+ boats stop and tourists rush into the water. Into the water where when the tide is high, it brings all the mess and you can smell gasoline from the boat. None of our crew dared to jump in there and we went home instead.
To sum it up: you can find starfish a short distance from The Rock restaurant to the north, on the beach you can find someone who will gladly take you there, or go swimming there. The sand is better on the east side of the coast. For diving, the Red Sea is better.
Of all the hotels we've ever had on all our vacations, this is the first one where I give 1 star, because 0 is not possible. Waste of money 75$/person.

content:
The Safari Blue Original offers an incredible experience, especially for those who haven’t participated in one before. It’s a notable upgrade from the standard tours offered by other providers, providing a unique adventure that is hard to replicate.
However, there are a few areas that need improvement. One significant concern is the crew''s handling of wildlife interactions. During our tour, some guests dove down to grab starfish and sea sponges for their entertainment, and the crew seemed to turn a blind eye to this behavior. It’s important for the crew to set clear expectations regarding wildlife interactions to ensure that all guests treat the marine environment with respect.
Additionally, I felt that the cooking crew on the island could be more attentive and respectful, particularly towards local tourists. I noticed that my friends, who were foreigners, received more attentive service than I did. While I understand that local tourists may be fewer in number, it’s essential for the staff to treat all guests equally and with respect to create a welcoming environment for everyone.
I hope my feedback will be taken into consideration to enhance your services, especially for local tourists who travel from the mainland to enjoy this beautiful experience. Furthermore, it would be great to see more gluten-free options on the menu, as well as a variety of cooked vegetables, as there were none available during our visit.
Overall, I believe that with a few adjustments, Safari Blue can provide an even more exceptional experience for all its guests.

content:
I selected this company after reading a lot of bad reviews of other ''blue safaris''. So we paid more hoping for a better trip. The organisation and service were good, not too crowded on the boat, drinks and fruits served during the trip. The attractions, not so much. We didn''t go to see the dolphins, the first stop was on a sand bank which was nice but full of people at that time (20 or so other boats). It would be better to stop there on the way back when it was almost empty. The first snorkeling point was disappointing, unclear water, damaged coral and very little fish. The second spot was better but not spectacular. At least the water was clearer and we saw several kinds of fish. Unfortunately it started raining so we moved to the next location. The lagoon was nice at high tide. The boat goes inside and you can swim in calm water. We stayed there for a short time, I would prefer more. Then there is lunch which was served on the other side of the island. There was sea food and chicken and some vegetables. Not a fancy fish but I believe all was fresh. Again there were drinks, including beer, and then some fruits, and a small coffee with amarula liqueur. The visit to the baobab tree was a 2 minute walk, a chance to take a photo (it is really a large tree) and go back. There are some stalls with souvenirs and clothes but you can just pass them by. I think we spent maybe 2h there including lunch. I''m not sure if there is anything more to explore on the island, if you eat quickly and skip ''baobab attraction'' you can probably walk around - the guide did not mention such a possibility. The way back was smooth. The wind was too weak to set the sail unfortunately.
To summarise, you can spend the whole day on the water, see some attractions and swim. Do not count on snorkeling as the best in the world (maybe when the company started their business in 1996 the reef was in better shape). It is enjoyable but quite expensive. Remember that due to the tides and weather your experience may be different.

content:
This experience was truly exceptional, and I highly recommend it.
First, the logistics were seamless; I was conveniently picked up from and dropped off back in Nungwi. The team was incredibly well-organized. Upon arrival at the main meeting point, don’t be concerned by the number of people you see. The team efficiently divides everyone into smaller groups (ours had 16 people, and it never felt crowded), each assigned to separate boats.
The sandbank was breathtaking—unlike anything I’ve ever seen. We were fortunate to visit during a very low tide around the full moon. We were also incredibly lucky to spot dolphins and even swim with them, which was undoubtedly the highlight of the trip. The snorkeling experience was fantastic—long enough to savor and truly immerse yourself in the beauty of the underwater world.
Lunch exceeded expectations. It was served buffet-style on a charming island, and I enjoyed fresh grilled fish, beans, lentils, and rice. There was also chicken and meat for those interested. The local fruits were abundant, and the crew thoughtfully explained each one in detail. The lunch area seemed to be privately managed by the company, and it featured sunbeds, perfect for relaxing after the meal. If you''re interested in souvenirs, there are plenty of small local shops nearby.
One lovely surprise was when the crew sailed the boat after lunch instead of using the engine—a peaceful and delightful touch. Drinks were provided onboard (soda, water, and beer), along with fresh fruit and a local sweet treat.
As for concerns about crowding, I personally didn’t feel it was an issue. Perhaps we were lucky with the timing, but if it was the case, we’re all tourists contributing to the scene being crowded, and I think that’s just part of the experience.

content: A great day out spent with extremely friendly and professional staff that look after you from start to finish. Communication was fantastic throughout, with multiple WhatsApp messages throughout the booking process and we were collected on time from our hotel at the exact meeting time. Don’t be put off when you arrive, as the beach is covered with hundreds of people from different resorts and it gets a little bit chaotic with not much organisation. However once you get on your boat it is smooth sailing. The boats are comfortable and spacious, with alcohol, soft drinks and water provided. Throughout the day snacks are also given, including fruits, homemade peanut butter chocolate bites and other treats. Initially you visit a small sand raised island for photos before beginning the snorkelling. You are taken to two snorkelling areas. Both were sadly a little disappointing. The first was too murky to see anything, and where the waters were clear there was nothing to see but dead coral. The second site you could see a reef but little marine life. Perhaps it is luck of the draw, and on other days will be better, but for a  snorkelling excursion it was a little poor on this occasion. The blue lagoon you are taken to after is beautiful. On the main island, lunch makes up for the snorkelling, and really made our day. You are seated on long 20 seater tables by your boat name and called up table by table for lunch to be served to you. The bbq included lobster, chicken, fish, calamari and prawns. With rice, bread, cornflour cakes and sauces to accompany. Beer is included and there is also a bar where you can purchase additional alcohol. You get two hours on the island. Enough time to enjoy lunch and explore, with lots of shops nearby. This is the cheapest place for souvenirs and paintings. With items like fridge magnets just $2 and paintings in the range of $30. You will not find cheaper anywhere else in Zanzibar. The final treat came when you return to the mainland, and instead of using the motor, the staff put up the sail and you sail back. It is a really incredible experience. Overall a great day out and we would book again, it just needs to find a few better sites for the snorkelling!
full_address: The Safari Blue, Zanzibar, Fumba Village, Zanzibar, Tanzania

content:
Safari Blue Zanzibar
Onze ervaring met deze trip was helaas verre van wat de verkopers ons vooraf hadden voorgesteld.
De prijs-kwaliteitverhouding was ronduit teleurstellend. Voor 2 personen betaalden we samen 90 dollar, wat achteraf veel te hoog bleek. Na een busrit van een uur kwamen we aan bij een locatie waar we met zo’n 20 personen op een boot stapten voor nog een uur durende boottocht. Eenmaal aangekomen op een zandbank kregen we een fruitontbijt, maar we waren niet de enigen: er lagen ongeveer 25 boten, waardoor de zandbank overvol was met toeristen. Verder was er op en rond de zandbank niets te doen.
Na een pauze van 45 minuten gingen we verder naar de snorkelplek, een tocht van 20 minuten. Hier lagen ongeveer 20 boten en werd iedereen tegelijkertijd in het water gedropt. De schippers voerden de vissen, maar van een echte snorkeltour was geen sprake. Het was veel te druk, en we botsten constant tegen andere toeristen aan. We hebben uiteindelijk maar 10 minuten gesnorkeld en zijn daarna weer terug de boot op gegaan.
Vervolgens maakten we een korte boottocht naar een lunchplek, waar we een uur pauze hadden. De lunch was goed verzorgd en er was voldoende eten voor iedereen.
Na de lunch gingen we nog naar een mangrovebos, waar we slechts 10 minuten konden zwemmen. Door de vloed was het mangrovebos nauwelijks te zien, waardoor ook dit weinig indruk maakte.
Daarna volgde een boottocht van 1,5 uur en nog een busrit van een uur terug naar het hotel.
Kortom, hoewel de trip vooraf prachtig werd beschreven en de foto’s veelbelovend waren, bleek het in werkelijkheid een zeer commerciële aangelegenheid. Je betaalt veel te veel voor een ervaring die weinig biedt.
GEEN AANRADER!
translated_content:
Safari Blue Zanzibar
Unfortunately, our experience with this trip was far from what the vendors had promised us beforehand.
The value for money was downright disappointing. For two people, we paid a total of 90 dollars, which turned out to be much too high in hindsight. After a one-hour bus ride, we arrived at a location where we boarded a boat with about 20 people for another hour-long boat trip. Once we arrived at a sandbank, we were served a fruit breakfast, but we were not the only ones: there were about 25 boats, meaning the sandbank was overcrowded with tourists. Furthermore, there was nothing to do on or around the sandbank.
After a 45-minute break, we continued to the snorkeling spot, a 20-minute journey. There were about 20 boats here, and everyone was dropped into the water at the same time. The skippers fed the fish, but it was far from a real snorkeling tour. It was much too crowded, and we constantly bumped into other tourists. In the end, we only snorkeled for 10 minutes and then went back onto the boat.
Next, we took a short boat trip to a lunch spot, where we had an hour break. The lunch was well catered for, and there was plenty of food for everyone.
After lunch, we went to a mangrove forest, where we were only able to swim for 10 minutes. Due to the tide, the mangrove forest was barely visible, so this also made little impression.
This was followed by a 1.5-hour boat trip and another hour-long bus ride back to the hotel.
In short, although the trip was beautifully described beforehand and the photos were promising, in reality, it turned out to be a very commercial affair. You pay far too much for an experience that offers very little.
NOT RECOMMENDED!

content:
Was underwhelming.The safari consists of a swim, snorkelling, another light swim in a lagoon, and then lunch.
The first swim was on a tiny sand spit with probably 140 other people.  The swim itself was nice. The water was lovely and warm, and the provided fresh fruit was also pleasant.  It would have been good to have some better shelter from the sun.
The snorkelling was a complete waste of time, maybe because the water was choppy. Having life jackets might have made a difference, but it is hard to know as none were provided. We ended up seeing maybe 3 small fish.
The swim in the lagoon was nice but nothing to write home about. And the lunch at another spot was fine. A major concern was that the step ladder into and out of the boat was extremely slippery as it was metal, with no tread added. Several people had trouble getting in and out, made worse by the turbulent waters.

content:
My favorite excursion of Zanzibar. Thank you to the crew of the Stahamili Tuu!
I went on a half-day trip that included visiting a beautiful mangrove lagoon, a sandbank that disappears and reappears with the tide, snorkeling, and barbecue lunch, and fruit sampling at Kwale Island. The crew was so helpful throughout the trip, helping me with my snorkel and life jacket when I was having trouble swimming. The assistant captain was very kind to guide me through snorkeling, as well as help my mom on the uneven beach when walking back to the dhow.
Snacks and drinks were available throughout the trip. One of the snacks was aged coconut and cinnamon-y chocolate - I wish I had remembered to ask for the name and recipe!
Unfortunately we didn''t get to go swimming at the mangrove lagoon because the tide was going out - apparently, if we had stayed much longer, the dhow may have gotten stuck. We did not get to see any dolphins, but that is based on luck and did not diminish the experience.
Tip: bring a towel, as it can get chilly when you''ve just come out of the water and the dhow is moving.

translated_content:
It's a beautiful, fun, full-day excursion. There are four stops: the first for fruit, the second for snorkeling (1 hour) – they feed the fish, and you see quite a few, with beautiful colors. The third stop is for lunch (white rice, French fries, salad, and some grilled seafood). The food is decent, but not amazing either. The fourth stop is at a saltwater lagoon where you can swim for ten minutes. We also saw a dolphin.
It cost us $30 without transportation, since we had a rental car, and we booked through the hotel cook, but I think it's usually much more expensive.
It's worth going.

content:
Safari Blue turned out to be in my personal top things to do in Zanzibar. Actually, I’m not the person who would enjoy boat trip, but believe me I did!
So, there was a group of people, we got into the boat and off we went in the search of adventures.
We came to the first snorkeling place over some reef and spent time there. After the snorkeling the boat crew gave us some fruit, and we went to the second reef and snorkeled there for a while. After that we were proposed coconuts. And we went to the lagoon with an amazing crystal clear water and mangrove trees around, and snorkeled and swam there for a while.
After that we were taken to the island where we had lunch. We ate lobsters, shrimps, fish, rice and sauces. Also the fruit was proposed as desert.
After lunch we wandered around the island, saw a huge baobab tree, and an even huger another baobab tree. Took some pictures, walked a bit. Also there is a small market for those who would like to buy some souvenirs. After the lunch and walk we got back to the boat and went to the sandy island. That’s the small island which is covered in water in high tide. But while there’s low tide, the soft sand is looking out of the water and invites you to step on it. The island is just a few meters wide and maybe around twenty meters long. At least, that was the size when we were there. By the way, the boat crew took us there when there were no other people, so we could take some nice pictures looking like we are in a total solitude.
After that we got back into the boat and opened the sail and sailed back. And that was amazing! Even for such a naughty non-lover of the boats as me. I did enjoy and for sure I’ll keep this trip in my memory.

content: I would describe this as a glorified snokling event. First thing was the loading onto the dhow boat was nothing short of ridiculous. We had to wade through muddy waters where a smaller boat would pick you up to bring you to the dhow boat which was about 20 meters away. I understand that the low tides make it hard for the boats to enter the shallow waters. But if you have been doing this business since 1996 you should seriously consider constructing a small jetty that will overcome all these problems. Next, in the dhow boat we had 15 guests and 3 crew. We were sitting packed like sardines for the entire boat ride.  The sand bank: not sure why we stopped here as there is nothing to do especially if you stay at a beachfront hotel. Snokling: this was the only fun thing except that I got bitten by some invisible jelly fish and was stinging all over my body, but the boatmen didn''t seem to care or explain how I got the sting. Nice thig was that the other guests were offering medication and creams to alleviate my distress. Mangrove lagoon  swim: a little enclave that is nice for some picture taking. Lunch: food was good, buffet style n free flow of beers. Overall, I felt sorry for most of the guests in my boat as they didn''t seem too comfortable snokling and mostly stayed on the boat throughout. Next, the guide claimed that there was a 85% chance that we would see dolphines, but alas we didn''t see any. I suspect the dolphins only come to that area at certain times of the year, so do you research before taking this trip. So overall my take was that I would have engaged a local operater to take me snokling near my hotel instead of spending the entire day with blue safari. One star is given for the snokling experience and the 2nd star is given for lunch.

This trip is a very interesting, beautiful, adventurous full-day trip.
It includes three locations, a beautiful sandbank, where the group arrives from the Fumba pier. Here you can snorkel, then they serve local fruits, pineapple, coconut, red and yellow (lady fingers) bananas, mango.
Then we sailed to another island, where a large fish awaited us, with rice, fried potatoes and we got a very tasty sauce on the rice.
Lunch included grilled squid, crabs, tuna and lobster. The seafood was delicious.
After lunch, we went to a lagoon, where we walked in waist-deep water among the wonderful rocks, and then we visited a giant baobab tree.

One thing to watch out for is that on the way back everyone will be soaked from the waves, so you need a towel, and what is not extra, you have to frequently apply body lotion with a sun protection factor of 50, which is not really enough, because we forgot about it anyway.

They offered assistance whenever asked. This is a trip for people who know where they're going and what to expect.
Remember, you're sailing on the same boats you see in the photos (these aren't luxury yachts). There will be no cocktails served with palm trees. It might be windy, there will be waves, and the boat will rock. (It's safe, but you have to like that kind of atmosphere.)
The trip plan looks something like this:
- snorkeling (Lots of beautiful fish that brush up against you while swimming. The spot where you'll be swimming may have many other boats moored nearby (peak season), so you'll snorkel—sometimes in the waves—between them.
- "Disappearing Island"—sandy, surrounded by beautiful water. Very picturesque.
- lagoon (very beautiful). No fish there, but beautiful trees. You can swim. It's beautiful!!!
- Delicious lunch on the next island. The locals really go the extra mile. You'll also see a baobab tree there.
I recommend this trip. I had a great time. The guys on the boat are really knowledgeable and know what they're doing.
It was wonderful. I hope to go on a trip like this again someday.

content:
Safari Blue Beach Tour
Zanzibar’s most talked about sea adventure Sail away to sandbanks around the magnificent island of Unguja, Zanzibar. sailing, snorkeling, sunbathing on a Traditional Zanzibar DhowExplore the mangrove lagoon
Safari blue trip in Zanzibar is one among the best sea adventures in the Zanzibar island, not only sailing along with the traditional dhow but also you can have snorkeling, swim, and relaxing on a white sandy beach on a sandbank. In addition, all, there is plenty of seafood that are all waiting for you to be tested,
The dhow departs from the fumba beach at 09:00 and we get back around 17:00, with your Tour guide, you will explore the mangrove lagoon hidden inside the Kwale island.
Swimming into the protected mangrove forest at high tide is an unforgettable experience. This mangrove lagoon is famously known as a natural swimming pool.
The 200-year baobab tree is another attraction you just come and climb it and get a great view from the top! If you are lucky you can find massive coconut crabs living inside its hollow trunk.
Menai bay conservation society has several naturally occurring sandbanks with safe swimming and from there you can enjoy great snorkeling, relax under the shade and enjoy fresh coconuts and local snacks in paradise while you are surrounded by turquoise waters.

content:
We had an amazing time with this trip (but we also had luck and were the first group at every spot).
In the morning you get your equipment and go on one of the traditional dhows. We were around 20 people which made the boat really full. But we were catered for with drinks and fruits. First you go to a Sandbank and can take nice pictures. It is a Sandbank so don''t expect too much.
Then it goes to the first snorkeling spot which was amazing. So many corals and colored fish. We had one hour of snorkeling which was plenty enough. Then we went to one of the islands and had full lunch with chicken, lobster, kingprawns and delicious condiments. Highlight here was the fruit tasting, because the guide gave us like 10 different fruit to taste.
After that you can climb the Baobab tree or go shopping in the beachfront. The Baobab is really crowded when a lot of people come at the same time. Still impressive, though.
Second time snorkeling was at a spot where the coral reefs were almost dead. Sad to see the destruction but still we could look at some fish and anemones.
In the end we drove to a little bay with coral rocks.
Piece of advice: definitely bring reef shoes!
All in all a nice trip worth the money. However there are so many boats out there, sometimes snorkeling all in the same spot so you have to be prepared for that. Also you start snorkeling right of the boat and although the crew seemed knowledgeable we were not confident that they had every person in eyesight, e.g. would notice if someone was going under.

content: Don''t waste your time or money. We turned up to the boat station to find about 20 boats moored up, all doing the same tour. It was raining and the conditions were frankly dangerous. Low visibility and choppy water. They still decided to run the tour. We were stuffed onto a boat with 15 other people, all put under some tarp whilst waiting for the rain to pass. Once the rain did clear, we were taken to a mangrove forest only to be told that portion of the trip isn''t possible as the tide was low, something the boat captain would''ve known before doing the tour. We were then taken to a sandbank where we ate fruit with about 100 other tourists who had been dropped off there. There is nothing to do there so you spend most of the time just sitting in the sand waiting for the tour operators to put everyone back on the boat. It also isn''t a good swimming spot as there are sharp pieces of debris under the water. We were then taken on a 40 minute snorkelling trip which was 50 yards away from the sandbank. They also decided to feed the fish from the boat which upsets their natural habitat. We then had lunch which, to be fair, was quite nice. We saw no dolphins on the trip either. This is something they tell you that you will see. When speaking to a local, he said dolphins don''t live in this area due to the amount of boat activity. In total, we paid $65 each to have an alright lunch as none of the other activities really lived up to expectations. We feel like we were mislead over the trip. They promise you the earth so if you do decide to go, go with no expectations at all.

You get on the boat and they take you to an area with about 20 other boats, where you can barely move around the boat for fear of being run over.
There's practically nothing to see while snorkeling, and they even threw food to the fish to attract them, disrupting their habitat and food supply. It's a disgrace.

We were tossed around like crazy, everyone was vomiting, my terrified 12-year-old daughter begged us to go back, but it was no use!! content:
First off: we're giving one star for the pretty fish while snorkeling and one star for the overall beautiful scenery. The rest was unfortunately a complete disappointment...
It started with arriving at the starting point by taxi to find 20 other taxis already waiting. Simultaneously, a "traditional" dance performance, seemingly rehearsed for the tourists' entertainment, was taking place, and we were able to purchase some worn-out snorkeling gear.
Then we took an overcrowded boat to the sandbank. The sandbank itself was actually quite nice, and fruit was being handed out. However, the amount was limited, so you constantly had to stand in line to get some. Given the size of the group, this wasn't surprising.
Afterwards, we went snorkeling (50 meters from the sandbank, but we were taken there by boat). We saw some beautiful fish for 15 minutes, which, of course, were being fed. Environmentally, this was probably a complete disaster, with the boat anchors scraping across the coral... but that's another story.
Now came the "highlight," and we were taken to an island. There, besides countless vendor stalls, we first had lunch. It was like being processed like a school cafeteria.
Afterwards, we were "allowed" 30 minutes to relax on the beach among the vendor stalls until the boat departed again.
Then we went to a lagoon with mangroves, where we were allowed to jump in the water briefly. After that, we returned to the starting point.
In conclusion: We booked the tour through our accommodation for $40 per person. Others had even paid more. For us, it wasn't even worth $40.

content:
C’est une activité plutôt fun à faire, mon avis reste mitigé sur l’excursion car le temps n’était pas avec nous. Je pense que la météo est un facteur qui joue beaucoup autant pour le moral que pour la beauté de la nature. (La mer transparente sous un ciel bleu est forcément moins paradisiaque sous la pluie).
Vous partez le matin à bord d’un dow (voilier local à Zanzibar), direction une île de sable blanc pour aller nager et manger des fruits frais (un taxi vient vous chercher à votre logement). Un arrêt snorkeling est prévu, avant de rejoindre l’île principale où vous mangerez un enorme barbecue de poissons accompagné de riz (la nourriture était super bonne)
Après avoir mangé, vous pourrez faire le tour d’un marché de souvenirs, ainsi que découvrir le Baobab, un des plus anciens arbres du monde (et aussi un des plus grands!). Vous pourrez aussi vous détendre sur la plage si le marché ne vous intéresse pas 🙂 .
translated_content:
It's a pretty fun activity, but my opinion of the excursion is mixed because the weather wasn't on our side. I think the weather plays a big role, both in terms of mood and the beauty of nature. (The crystal-clear sea under a blue sky is definitely less idyllic in the rain).
You leave in the morning aboard a dow (a local sailboat in Zanzibar), heading to a white sand island to swim and eat fresh fruit (a taxi picks you up from your accommodation). A snorkeling stop is planned before reaching the main island where you'll enjoy a huge fish barbecue with rice (the food was delicious!). After eating, you can browse a souvenir market and discover the Baobab, one of the oldest trees in the world (and also one of the largest!). You can also relax on the beach if the market doesn't interest you.

content:
Contratamos las excursión con un local, nos costo la pareja 85€, luego nos dijo un local que máximo 70€ la pareja deberíamos pagar.
El origen puede ser diferente según la parte de la isla donde estés pero final siempre acabas en los mismos lugares. La excursión consiste:
1. Barquito a tope de gente turista con sus guías hacia un banco de arena.
2. El banco si llegas pronto genial, en Cádiz contrario es un banco de gente. Te dan frutal deliciosa.
3. Te vas dirección a las isla final y por el camino paras a hacer snorkeling.
4. Llegas a una turística isla donde comes arroz, patatas y mariscos (muy buena comida). En la isla puedes dar un paseo para ver sus carísimas tiendas y un árbol precioso.
translated_content:
We booked the excursion with a local; it cost €85 for the couple. Later, another local told us the maximum we should pay was €70 per couple.
The starting point can vary depending on the part of the island you're on, but you always end up in the same places. The excursion consists of:
1. A small boat packed with tourists and their guides heads to a sandbank.
2. If you arrive early, the sandbank is great; otherwise, it's a crowded place. They give you delicious fruit.
3. You head towards the final island and stop along the way for snorkeling.
4. You arrive at a tourist island where you eat rice, potatoes, and seafood (very good food). On the island, you can take a walk to see its very expensive shops and a beautiful tree.

content:
Non andate!!!!
Si paga troppo per stare mezz’ora sul banco di sabia con altri mille turisti a mangiare della frutta.
La laguna blu non si vedeva perché, come dicono loro, sfortunatamente la marea era bassa, ma si parte sempre alla mattina presto quindi va de “fortuna”. In banco di sabia era estremamente pieno di gente e abbiamo visitato posti simile a Zanzibar dove la sabbia era più bianca e il mare più bello.
Momento snorkeling? Due corali a due passi dal banco di sabia, quindi non ti sposti neanche.
Momento pranzo è imbarazzante, tutto insieme un caos assoluto e gli uccelli hanno anche fatto i bisogni dentro la nostra birra. Birra che tra l’altro costa tantissimo!
Meno male che abbiamo fatto il tour privato e abbiamo potuto scappare dalla trappola prima del previsto.
Se volete banco di sabia e snorkeling bello potete andare a Mnemba o Pungume.
translated_content:
Don't go!!!!
It's too much to spend half an hour on the sandbank with a thousand other tourists eating fruit.
The Blue Lagoon wasn't visible because, as they say, unfortunately the tide was low, but we always leave early in the morning, so it's a matter of luck. The sandbank was extremely crowded, and we've visited similar places in Zanzibar where the sand was whiter and the sea more beautiful.
Snorkeling time? Two coral reefs just steps from the sandbank, so you don't even have to move.
Lunchtime was embarrassing, everything was absolute chaos, and the birds even did their business in our beer. Beer, which is incredibly expensive, by the way!
Luckily we took the private tour and were able to escape the trap earlier than expected.
If you want a sandbank and great snorkeling, you can go to Mnemba or Pungume.

content: Nous avons passé une très bonne journée. Première étapes : sur un banc de sable, nous avons manger des fruits frais. Deuxième étapes : snorkelling incroyable. Nous nous sommes crus dans un aquarium. Les poissons et les coraux sont magnifiques. Troisième étapes de ce tour en bateau : repas sur une île. Nous avons été servi comme des rois (homards, pieuvre, crevette, thon, riz, frites et salade). Puis détour pour admirer un sublime baobab. Des boutiques sont juste à côté. Cependant, cela ne vaut pas le coup. Les tarifs sont excessifs. Quatrième étapes : piscine naturelle au milieu des mangroves. L''eau est incroyablement chaude. A deux, la journée nous a coûté 60 € (taxi et repas compris). En discutant avec d''autres personnes, certains ont été facturé 150, et d''autres 40. Ne fait pas confiance aux personnes qui vous abordent sur la plage en vous promettant des tarifs exceptionnelles. Souvent, ils partent avec l''argent et vous vous devez de repayer.
translated_content: We had a wonderful day. First stop: we ate fresh fruit on a sandbar. Second stop: incredible snorkeling. We felt like we were in an aquarium. The fish and coral were magnificent. Third stop on this boat tour: lunch on an island. We were treated like royalty (lobster, octopus, shrimp, tuna, rice, fries, and salad). Then a detour to admire a magnificent baobab tree. There are shops right next to it. However, it's not worth it. The prices are exorbitant. Fourth stop: a natural pool in the middle of the mangroves. The water is incredibly warm. For two people, the day cost us €60 (taxi and lunch included). Talking to other people, some were charged €150, and others €40. Don't trust people who approach you on the beach promising exceptional prices. Often, they run off with the money, and you have to pay again.

content: Nice sea adventure with Safari Blue on their traditional Dhow boats. Please note, there are no bathrooms on the boat, so use their facilities before you board. Booking on their website was seamless. Communication via WhatsApp was fast and supportive. Our boat captain and guides were polite and helpful from the second we arrived. We went to several snorkeling sights, all had interesting biodiversity. We saw dolphins along the way and stopped on an island for a wonderfully prepared buffet lunch and fruit tasting. Our guides were nice to allow us the option and opt to visit to the sandbank after lunch so it was less crowded, and it was the perfect idea. We stopped at the Blue Lagoon for a quick swim, although wish it was longer as it was so relaxing and beautiful. One thing that would have made the trip more comfortable is having a boat ladder with higher handrails for easier embarkment. But the trip back under sail was the most relaxing ending to a overall nice experience.

content:
TL;DR - Bad experience.
It was unfortunate that we requested not to swim in coral reefs as that damages them however we still ended up going to a coral reef and told we could swim here. We also visited the giant tortoises... it says in the entrance “do not feed the tortoises” yet they give us food to feed them. The babies are locked in a 6x8 cage. The entire area is full of poop and the tortoises do not get to roam free at all. They’re captive and do not have the ability to escape the hands of tourism except probably at night time. It was extremely sad to see that people not only cage them but some people will pay a ton of money just for an instagram pic. One girl I saw was trying to hold the tortoise back to get a “good pic” and nobody stopped her although the tortoise was clearly trying to avoid her. We decided to skip out on the dolphins as some others we met along the trip mentioned how they cornered the dolphins and left their propellers on to herd them in a circle. Just hearing that made me cringe and I couldn’t do it. While snorkeling I was having trouble with my goggles and the captain nor the other workers even offered assistance. I didnt even get to swim. The snorkeling also only lasted about 15 minutes... we spent most of our day on the beach catching rays. If I wanted to spend time on the beach I’d go to Cancun. I wanted to experience something different but Sadly most of my experience was seeing greed. The beaches are beautiful, the water is great, the animals are lovely. The food was awesome as well. However my rating isn’t on just this, it’s also on Safari Blue & the greed surrounding tourism. My group and I were very discouraged and we decided to skip out on the last day. I hope whoever reads this, please do some research! Many groups pose as conservationists only to take advantage of you and the animal.

content: Blue Safari was the highlight of our trip to Zanzibar! We headed out on a boat fully stocked with drinks and fresh coconut and did guided snorkeling. This was my first time snorkeling and I was in awe! There were so many types of fish and sea life - manta rays, puffer fish, starfish, sea cucumbers, we even saw Nemo and Dory! Then we hopped back on the boat and got back in the water a short time later to snorkel around independently. We headed to a satellite island where we had a delicious meal of rice, veggies, fish and chicken with soft drinks and beer. We did a tasting of all sorts of local fruits. We saw a huge Baobab tree and did a little shopping at some of the souvenir huts. Then we got back on the boat and our final stop was a mangrove lagoon. We went back to the main island and arrived around 4pm. Our trip had about 12 other tourists from many countries and it was really cool to get to chat with them. Our guides were very knowledgeable and friendly. The trip was only $65/person and we paid for our own transport from Stone Town. I would HIGHLY recommend this trip, I will never forget it!

Retour à la voile du bateau.

Return to the boat by sail.
I recommend shopping around to find different guides, as prices can vary significantly.

Enjoy every moment.

translated_content: We booked the Blue Safari with the well-known Marbella, influenced by what we'd seen online, and our recommendation is that if possible, you book directly with local people. I would have appreciated it if he had notified us that he wouldn't be there or expected; instead, he simply called at the last minute to ask how things were going and remind us what we had to pay the guide on duty. Furthermore, he never advised us on the best times for certain activities (for example, swimming with dolphins). We could have gone in the afternoon directly from the hotel, but instead, they took us in the morning, along with everyone else, and at a time when the place was practically a flea market. Knowing we were so close, we could have gone earlier or later. And this is just one example. Finally, I must mention that the price is very high for the poor quality offered. Again, if you want to do something special, hire them directly in the area. They might not speak Spanish, but I don't think that's important, right?

content:
I had very high expectations and unfortunately they weren’t met fully.
The morning was semi chaotic with MANY boats departing. Boat was ok but ours had no shade - should be a must on a boat when there’s clear skies and UV 11. First snorkeling was ok regarding time and such, the snorkeling wasn’t good, although that’s not a fault of Safari Blue. The snorkels wasn’t good, had no stop filter. One more short snorkel, close to the other place - same to see.
And that was it. No sailing in areas with a chance to see dolphins - they didn’t even mention how/where to look.
The tour seemed more concerned with food and drinks (I’m guessing that’s one reason people liked it so much...?). The food was good and plenty.
Directly back to shore after that. So, too little snorkel (approx 45 min total), too little dolphins. Short visit to laguna and an island. All in all not good enough value for the price (which is very expensive! - 90 usd per person incl transfer).
Despite what others say, this (and snorkeling) in Zanzibar is not a must. Have you tried snorkeling before you will probably be disappointed, and should maybe come for the food and the sailing instead...

content:
The Hamamni Persian Baths is located in a historical building of Stone Town, Zanzibar. The name Hamamni is also used to refer to the neighbourhood where the building is located.
The Baths were built between 1870 and 1888 for sultan Barghash bin Said for use as public baths, and maintained this function until 1920. They are referred to as 'Persian'" because their construction was commissioned to Shirazi architects.[1] The word '"Hamamni'" means '"the place of the baths'".

content: Экскурсия интерактивная, познавательная, проходит динамично и весело. Понравится любому возрасту. Мы приехали на машине с детьми. Сотрудник нас сразу встретил у машины, познакомились, обсудили цену, помогли перейти через дорогу, озвучили вводную информацию  и перешли к экскурсии.Нам очень повезло с Адамом, успевал ответить и на наши вопросы, и детские комментарии. Попробовали все: и на вкус, и послушали ароматы - начиная от перца, алое, корицы, имбиря, лемонграсса и тд. Дети так вошли во вкус и каждый раз перемещаясь к новому кусту, либо дереву, задавали шутливый вопрос гиду - ням - ням или только слушаем аромат -этот вопрос стал коронным и перешел в разряд шутки, которую отлично поддержал Адам - от этого стала веселее и интереснее и нам, и детям . Очень много полезного узнали для здоровья и познавательного, например, что ваниль является растением - паразитом, и если он крепится к какому - то дереву, то плодоносящее дерево перестает плодоносить, а лемонграсс хорошо отпугивает комаров и многое другое. На каком  - то моменте мы подошли к следующему дереву и вуаля Адам за считанные секунды взобрался на него и собрал нам какие - то вкусные плоды ( столько интересного было, что уже забыла какой). Мы стали возвращаться и думали , ну всё нас уже ничем не удивить. И тут останавливаемся у кокосовой пальмы и парнишка ловко на стопы ног закидывает что- то из серии бечевки и так обхватывая, пальму начинает молниеносно карабкаться по пальме. Тут мы открыли рты и только охали и ахали от предвосхищения, как сорвет кокос - так и оказалось. Это был полный восторг увидеть , как через секунды кокос уже оказался на земле. А перед этим этот ловкий парнишка сплел девчонкам и нам короны из листьев пальм , а Адам дополнил этот брак очками из пальмового листа. Естественно мы шли довольные, делились впечатлениями  и настроились на выход . Но и на этом экскурсия еще подошла к логичному завершению. Теперь нас пригласили на дегустацию фруктов - кокосового молока, его мякоти, ананаса и местного мандарина. Все было вкусным и сочным - одним словом объедение. И в заключении нам предложили масла, мыло и специи. Мы не удержались, да и не хотелось удерживаться -сделать себе приятное в виде подарков и продолжить приятное послевкусие от экскурсии.      Отзыв получился объемным, да с подобной  шикарной программой  одним - двумя предложениями ее прелесть не передать. Всем рекомендасьон!)))
translated_content: The tour was interactive, educational, dynamic, and fun. It's perfect for all ages. We arrived by car with the kids. A staff member met us right at the car, introduced ourselves, discussed the price, helped us cross the road, gave us some introductory information, and then started the tour. We were very lucky with Adam; he was quick to answer our questions and the kids' comments. We sampled everything: tasted and smelled the aromas—from pepper, aloe, cinnamon, ginger, lemongrass, and more. The kids really got into it, and every time they moved to a new bush or tree, they'd ask the guide a playful question: "Yum, yum, or are we just smelling the aroma?" This question became a running joke, which Adam picked up perfectly, making things even more fun and engaging for both us and the kids. We learned a lot of useful health and educational information, for example, that vanilla is a parasitic plant, and if it attaches itself to a tree, the fruit-bearing tree stops bearing fruit, and lemongrass is a good mosquito repellent, among other things. At one point, we approached the next tree, and voila, Adam had climbed it in a matter of seconds and collected some delicious fruit for us (there were so many interesting ones that I've already forgotten which ones). We started to turn back, thinking, well, nothing can surprise us anymore. Then we stopped by a coconut palm, and a young man deftly threw some kind of string over his feet and, clasping the palm in that way, began to climb the tree at lightning speed. Our mouths dropped open and we oohed and aahed in anticipation as he plucked the coconut—and there it was. It was a complete delight to see how, seconds later, the coconut was already on the ground. Before that, this clever young man had woven palm leaf crowns for the girls and us, and Adam had completed the arrangement with palm leaf glasses. Naturally, we were delighted, sharing our impressions and getting ready to leave. But even here, the tour had come to a logical conclusion. Now we were invited to a fruit tasting – coconut milk, coconut pulp, pineapple, and local tangerine. Everything was delicious and juicy – ​​simply delicious. And at the end, we were offered oils, soap, and spices. We couldn't resist, and we didn't want to – we wanted to treat ourselves to gifts and continue the pleasant aftertaste of the tour. This review turned out to be extensive, but with such a luxurious program, it's impossible to convey its charm in just one or two sentences. Highly recommended!)))

Booking with Siso was very easy - quick response, communicates well, flexible with times, organised transport on our behalf and this was very reasonably priced too.
The day  began with the Cooking class - very informal, largely watched the staff prepare our lunch and briefly helped with the preparation. Lovely to watch the authentic way of cooking - making fresh coconut milk, grinding spices/foods with various size pestle and mortar, cooking over coal.
Spice tour - led by Khamis. Clearly experienced, knowledgeable, fun, relaxed and speaks English very well. Lovely to see the various foods grown on their farm and learn about these. Enjoyed coconut drink on the way.
Lunch was lovely - nothing beats homemade food! Felt very hospitable, cosy, homely. Perfect way to end a lovely day.
Opportunity to buy some items - not pressurised to buy, reasonable prices.
Highly recommend booking with Siso directly for the best price which also means tips to the staff can be given a little more generously.

Mixed results:
On the one hand, a friendly and attentive guide (who spoke a little French), a fairly wide range of species presented (pineapple, cinnamon, coffee, ginger, cloves, lemongrass, aloe, among others), and an amusing coconut picker who was also a good singer.
A well-narrated tour lasting just under an hour.
On the other hand, the fact that we weren't shown the true culture, the organization of the harvest, or the parts harvested (it felt more like a sampling than anything else)...
And
the financial aspect.
While the tour price is reasonable ($10 for two people plus tips for the guide and the "picker," totaling around $23), we were in a rental car, without a driver to pay.
The products offered at the end of the tour are very expensive (you'd be better off buying them at the Stone Town market; you'll also enjoy a nice visit), and the "owner" seems much more concerned with your wallet than your appearance.
It's worth seeing for personal enrichment, to see these plants in their natural environment and presentation (not in plastic packaging), but in my opinion, it's not the island's main attraction.
Since this was the only "farm" we visited in Zanzibar, I can't compare it to others...

content:
We visited the farm few days ago with a couple of friends. We booked in advance for a cooking class too.
We arrived at the farm at 9h30.
It was AMAZING !!!
First, we were warmly welcoming by Siso and the rest of the team. Then, we stayed with Ridhwan, the cooking chef. He teached us all the steps to cook Pilau with tuna fish. This experience was really funny and interesting even if it was a little bit long (maybe 2 hours), but normal, sometimes cooking takes time.
During the Pilau finished to cook, we went to visit the farm with Khamis. He is very friendly and funny, we learned and laughed a lot.
The farm is big and it was really pleasant to walk around. We tasted different fruits and spices. Khamis really takes time to explain and respond to all our questions. The tour takes around 1h30.
At the end of the tour, we ate Pilau with the staff. It was de-li-cious ! It was very satisfying and nice to eat all together.
After a plate of fruits and a little photo shoot, we''ve been to the spice shop and buy a lot of spices for cooking Pilau again and again.
This is really something to do if you come in Zanzibar.
But careful, there is a lot of spice farm around. One of them has a sign very similar to Kidichi Spice farm but it''s not the right place if you want to live this experience.
I highly recommend this one !

ביקור מומלץ בחוות התבלינים. סגרנו במלון על נהג ומדריך שיהיה איתנו כל היום ויחזיר אותנו בסוף הטיול למלון. התחלנו בחוות התבלינים. ליווה אותנו גם מדריך מהחווה שהסביר על צמח וצמח ותוך כדי כך גם עשה לנו קישוטי כתר ופרחים. המדריך שלנו תרגם לנו לאנגלית מתובלת במילים עבריות. לסיום, המדריך המקומי גם טיפס והוריד לנו אגוז קוקוס לטעימה. הסיור בחווה תחת צל העצים היה נחמד אבל מרוב תבלינים והסבר על תכונותיהם הבריאות הכל התערבב לי בראש...

A recommended visit to the spice farm. We booked a driver and guide at the hotel who would be with us all day and would return us to the hotel at the end of the trip. We started at the spice farm. The tour of the farm under the shade of the trees was nice, but with so many spices and explanations about their health properties, everything got mixed up in my head...
Overall, being in Zanzibar and not visiting the spice farm we won't really know if it was worth it.

content:
Bilal is a kind, ambitious, and hardworking young man who clearly cares deeply about the community he lives in. He taught himself English and now supports himself through this small guiding business he built on his own.
My husband and I went on a tour with him that included a visit to a spice farm and his home village, Kisongoni. There was no car transfer included (we didn’t need one) — we used our own car and also gave him a ride. We paid $40 per person for the experience.
Bilal guided us through the village and explained how people live there and how they build their homes. He even took us into several local houses so we could see firsthand how families live. He bought small items for the children and laundry detergent, which he distributed to the families.
The experience was moving, and at times quite emotional. Even if you try to prepare yourself by reading or watching videos online, nothing really compares to seeing the reality with your own eyes. The local people are warm and welcoming, and the children were full of joy when receiving the small gifts.
A small suggestion: if you’re able to bring anything with you — like notebooks, coloring books, crayons, small backpacks, children''s clothes, detergent, or rice — these things are truly appreciated and very much needed.
Overall, I wholeheartedly recommend Bilal as a guide. This experience is not just a tour — it’s a powerful reminder of humanity, generosity, and perspective. And supporting someone like Bilal, who works hard and gives back to his community, makes it all the more meaningful.

content:
Cet endroit se dit « éthique » car soi disant propre et peu de tortues présentes, voulant certainement se démarquer de l’autre cave déjà présente à Kizimkazi, mais l’enfer est le même pour les animaux.
Une tortue en un jour peut parcourir des centaines de kilomètres dans l’océan. Est ce le cas ici ?
Les tortues ont été capturé dans l’océan (en bonne santé) puis mises dans cette piscine pour se faire de l’argent …
J’ai demandé en commentaire sur leur Instagram d’où venait ces tortues ... mon commentaire a été supprimé, ce qui veut tout dire.
Ces tortues n’ont rien à faire ici. Il n’y a pas de « sanctuaire », ni d’endroit où les soigner, cet endroit n’est pas éthique,  c’est une prison de plus.
Ne participez pas à ça, ne financez pas ça.
Si vous aimez vraiment les tortues, n’allez pas les voir ici.
translated_content:
This place calls itself "ethical" because it's supposedly clean and has few turtles, undoubtedly trying to differentiate itself from the other cave already present in Kizimkazi, but the hell it is for the animals is the same.
A turtle can travel hundreds of kilometers in the ocean in a single day. Is that the case here?
The turtles were captured in the ocean (healthy) and then put in this pool to make money…
I asked in a comment on their Instagram where these turtles came from… my comment was deleted, which says it all.
These turtles don't belong here. There's no "sanctuary," no place to care for them; this place isn't ethical, it's just another prison.
Don't participate in this, don't fund this.
If you truly love turtles, don't go see them here.
full_address: Pango La Kasa, jambiani, Tanzania

content:
Warning - this is adventure territory!
Bwejuu Mangroves are an absolute must - the highlight of our holiday so far.
We didn''t book in advance and arrived at low tide. The guys were still happy to take us out because even though low tide means having to walk through the mangrove tunnels, we then had an amazing time snorkeling and saw hundreds of vibrant, colourful fish. Our guides were very knowledgeable about the flora and fauna, and made sure we got the maximum from our trip. The experience was rounded off with a very welcome fresh fruit platter. We also took our tuktuk driver along for the whole expedition - also a first for him and definitely not the day he was expecting!
So, if you want to canoe from start to finish, go at high tide. If you want the earthy experience complete with snorkeling and pretty fish, low tide might be better. Good footwear (water shoes) is an absolute must.
full_address: Bwejuu Mangrove Tunnel Kayak, Dongwe, Bwejuu 0000, Tanzania

content: A really fun day, probably best to call and book in advance to get the best advice. If it is high tide, you can get the canoe experience through the tunnels of the mangrove.. But the water is deeper and murky. We went low tide and walked in through the canals. There are rocks under the water, so shoes are advised. Then we canoed in the main river, which was great fun and spectacular. There are lots of fish and crabs to see. We took our own snorkels and masks and were the first to snorkel there. You see lots and lots of fish, angel fish, trumpet fish and many that are unique to thee mangrove. Apparently if you do the sunset timing you are likely to see bush babies and monkeys. The guides and owner are great fun. It''s a new venture so still being slowly completed, at three end of our day we finished with fresh fruits on the tree top view point. Highly recommended. You can take a tuk tuk here for not much and it''s about $25pp. All in all a great experience.

content:
A differenza di chi ha visto erbacce a me è stato spiegato, dalle sagge e tranquille parole, in perfetto inglese, portandomi in un posto dove apparentemente, tutto poteva sembrare, buttato lì così. In realtà, con Mohamed ci sono stata 45 minuti, finché mi ha spiegato che tutte le piante che vedevo intorno, erano medicali...e quindi la farmacia naturale di quella zona. Ho soggiornato per 5 giorni all interno della foresta ed è stato magico. Alla tramonto si usciva tra le mangrovie e ti si paravano davanti dei panorami surreali ...stormi di uccelli mentre scendeva il sole, al suono dei granchi, che schioccavano le chele.
Ho mangiato con loro e ho vissuto tra loro, ed è stata la migliore esperienza che potevo fare, per conoscere la vera Zanzibar.  Se amate la vita da Resort, lasciate stare. Non fa per tutti. Chi cerca di vivere in mezzo alla natura, conoscere la gente, visitare lei piantagioni o una scuola,con una sapiente guida, che vi farà conoscere un eco sistema funzionante, si rivolga direttamente a Mohamed del Zala Park e si faccia fare una proposta di programma, come ho fatto io...vi garantisco che non Ve ne pentirete.
Habari
translated_content:
Unlike those who saw weeds, I was told, by wise and calm words, in perfect English, taking me to a place where seemingly everything could have been thrown together. In reality, I spent 45 minutes with Mohamed, until he explained that all the plants I saw around me were medicinal... and therefore the natural pharmacy of that area. I stayed for five days inside the forest and it was magical. At sunset, we emerged into the mangroves and surreal views appeared before you... flocks of birds as the sun set, to the sound of crabs snapping their claws.
I ate with them and lived among them, and it was the best experience I could have had to get to know the real Zanzibar. If you love resort life, leave it alone. It's not for everyone. If you're looking to experience nature, meet the people, visit plantations or a school, with a knowledgeable guide who will introduce you to a functioning ecosystem, contact Mohamed of Zala Park directly and ask for a program proposal, as I did... I guarantee you won't regret it.
Habari

content:
⭐⭐⭐ 3 von 5 Sternen – tolle Tour, aber mit einigen Verbesserungsmöglichkeiten
Meine Freundin und ich haben am 06.09.2026 am Morgen an der Quadtour teilgenommen. Insgesamt hatten wir eine gute Zeit, allerdings gibt es aus unserer Sicht einige Punkte, die verbessert werden könnten.
Wir wurden mit leichter Verspätung direkt bei unserem Hotel abgeholt. Beim Veranstalter angekommen, gab es zunächst ein gutes und verständliches Briefing zur Bedienung der Quads. Jeder Teilnehmer musste das Quad selbst starten, etwa 4 Meter vorwärtsfahren, den Rückwärtsgang einlegen und wieder zurückfahren sowie das Quad anschließend ausschalten. Dadurch konnte man sich vor Beginn der eigentlichen Tour bereits etwas mit dem Fahrzeug vertraut machen.
Anschließend bekamen wir einen Helm. Dieser wirkte allerdings etwas unhygienisch, da er offensichtlich bereits von vielen Personen getragen wurde. Eine Einweg-Sturmhaube bzw. Hygienehaube wäre hier aus unserer Sicht wünschenswert.
Danach ging die eigentliche Tour los. Wir waren insgesamt etwa 10–12 Quads unterwegs. Die gesamte Tour dauerte rund 4 Stunden, davon waren etwa 2 Stunden reine Fahrzeit. Die Strecke führte über unterschiedliche Untergründe und durch verschiedene Gegenden. Insgesamt gab es drei Stopps: einmal an einem Strand, einmal in einem einheimischen Dorf und ein weiteres Mal an einem Strand bzw. Hafen. Dadurch bekam man neben dem Quadfahren auch einen kleinen Einblick in die Umgebung und das Leben auf Sansibar.
Unser Quad hatte bereits zu Beginn eine leuchtende Reserve-Tankanzeige. Während der Fahrt schaltete es sich beim Fahren über holprige und steinige Passagen einige Male von selbst aus. Ob dies tatsächlich mit dem niedrigen Tankstand zusammenhing, können wir nicht beurteilen – aufgrund der Situation wäre ein Zusammenhang jedoch durchaus denkbar. Hier wäre es sinnvoll, vor Beginn der Tour sicherzustellen, dass alle Quads ausreichend betankt und technisch in einwandfreiem Zustand sind.
Wichtig: Zieht unbedingt Kleidung an, die schmutzig werden darf! 😄
Wir waren nach der Tour wirklich von oben bis unten mit feinem braunem Staub und Sand bedeckt. Wir empfehlen daher ausdrücklich eine lange Hose und ein langärmeliges Oberteil sowie möglichst Kleidung, die anschließend problemlos gewaschen werden kann.
Preislich fanden wir die Tour sehr fair. Regulär hätten wir 58 € für zwei Personen bezahlt. Dank eines Rabattcodes (Tripadvisor) haben wir letztendlich nur 41 € für uns beide und ein Quad bezahlt. Für diesen Preis war das Erlebnis für uns angemessen und das Preis-Leistungs-Verhältnis insgesamt gut.
Fazit: Die Quadtour war abwechslungsreich und hat grundsätzlich Spass gemacht. Besonders die verschiedenen Strecken und Stopps haben uns gefallen. Allerdings gibt es aus unserer Sicht Verbesserungspotenzial bei der Hygiene der Helme sowie beim technischen Zustand und der Betankung der Quads.
Daher vergeben wir 3 von 5 Sternen. Mit besser gewarteten und ausreichend betankten Quads sowie hygienischeren Helmen wäre aus unserer Sicht eine deutlich bessere Bewertung möglich.
translated_content:
⭐⭐⭐ 3 out of 5 stars – Great tour, but with some room for improvement
My girlfriend and I participated in the quad tour on the morning of September 6, 2026. Overall, we had a good time, but in our opinion, there are a few things that could be improved.
We were picked up directly from our hotel with a slight delay. Upon arriving at the tour operator's location, we received a good and easy-to-understand briefing on how to operate the quads. Each participant had to start the quad themselves, drive forward about 4 meters, engage reverse, drive back, and then turn the quad off. This allowed us to familiarize ourselves with the vehicle before the actual tour began.
Afterward, we were given helmets. However, these seemed somewhat unhygienic, as they had obviously been worn by many people. A disposable balaclava or hygienic cap would have been preferable.
The actual tour then began. There were about 10-12 quads in total. The entire tour lasted about 4 hours, of which approximately 2 hours were actual driving time. The route led over varied terrain and through different areas. There were three stops in total: one at a beach, one in a local village, and another at a beach or harbor. This gave us a glimpse into the surroundings and life on Zanzibar, in addition to the quad biking.
Our quad bike's low fuel warning light was already illuminated at the start. During the ride, it switched itself off several times while driving over bumpy and rocky sections. We can't say for sure whether this was actually related to the low fuel level – but given the circumstances, a connection is certainly plausible. It would be advisable to ensure that all quad bikes are adequately fueled and in perfect working order before the tour begins.
Important: Be sure to wear clothes that you don't mind getting dirty! 😄 We were literally covered from head to toe in fine brown dust and sand after the tour. We therefore strongly recommend wearing long trousers and a long-sleeved top, as well as clothing that can be easily washed afterwards.
We found the tour to be very reasonably priced. The regular price would have been €58 for two people. Thanks to a discount code (Tripadvisor), we ultimately only paid €41 for both of us and a quad bike. For this price, the experience was satisfactory, and the overall value for money was good.
In conclusion: The quad bike tour was varied and generally enjoyable. We particularly liked the different routes and stops. However, in our opinion, there is room for improvement regarding the hygiene of the helmets, as well as the technical condition and refueling of the quad bikes.
Therefore, we give it 3 out of 5 stars. With better-maintained and adequately fueled quad bikes and more hygienic helmets, a significantly higher rating would be possible, in our view.

content:
Это было очень познавательно, весело, интересно.
Мы взяли тур на квадрациклах. Мы сами вели, нас не везли и это для нас важно.
Сначала мы ехали по дороге мимо деревень. Затем посетили можно сказать дикий пляж. А потом по лесу поехали в деревню,  где увидели быт людей. И это скажу я Вам сильное впечатление. Мало мебели, вода и электричество не у всех. Мы купили сладкое и мешок риса и наш гид раздал это все людям и детям. Было очень тепло на душе, что есть у нас была такая возможность.
Далее мы поехали на Кендва пляж, поели ананас.
Все было невероятно круто. Благодарю.  Здорово все организованно и продуманно. Все рассказывается честно. Например, мы думали, сладости это прям класс. Но на самом деле знаете, что нужно людям и детям там? Рис. И я очень рада, что у нас было достаточно налички купить и сладости (50.000 занзибарских шилингов) и 50кг риса (170.0000 занзибарских шилингов). Мы потом докупили ещё коробку сладостей за 50К, потому что не хватило.
Пусть у всех нас все будет хорошо. А ребятам спасибо за поучительную экскурсию.
translated_content:
It was very educational, fun, and interesting.
We took a quad bike tour. We drove ourselves, no one drove us, and that's important to us.
First, we drove along a road past villages. Then we visited a practically wild beach. Then we drove through the forest to a village, where we saw people's daily lives. And I can tell you, it was a very impressive experience. There was little furniture, and not everyone had water or electricity. We bought some sweets and a bag of rice, and our guide distributed them to the people and children. It was a wonderful feeling that we had this opportunity.
Then we went to Kendwa Beach and ate pineapple.
Everything was incredibly cool. Thank you. Everything was wonderfully organized and well thought out. Everything was explained honestly. For example, we thought the sweets would be great. But you know what the people and children there really need? Rice. And I'm so glad we had enough cash to buy both sweets (50,000 Zanzibar shillings) and 50 kg of rice (170,000 Zanzibar shillings). We later bought another box of sweets for 50,000 Zanzibar shillings because we didn't have enough.
May all be well with us. And thanks to the guys for the educational excursion.

content:
If you love adventure, speed, and a good dose of dust on your face, then the Payo Quad Bike tour in Zanzibar is an absolute must-do! It’s one of those activities that gives you both an adrenaline rush and a genuine feel of local life.
The experience runs from 2 p.m. to about 6 p.m., and it includes visits to three key locations  the first beach, a local village, and another scenic beach where the tour wraps up with fresh fruits for everyone.
Before hitting the trail, the team gives a brief 15-minute training session on how to operate the quad bikes  simple, practical, and great for beginners. Each quad bike can carry two people (a driver and a passenger), and the machines are solid four-wheel, off-road beasts with good suspension and braking.
Safety is taken very seriously. Everyone is given a helmet, and the group moves in a single file to avoid accidents. There’s a lead instructor in front and a supervisor at the back, making sure no one gets lost or left behind. The pace changes along the way  sometimes fast enough to get your heart racing, other times slower so everyone can catch up and enjoy the view.
The ride starts off on a smooth, open road where you feel the wind and take in the scenery. Then comes the real fun the off-road stretch. During my ride, the trail was extremely dusty, so much that visibility was low even with glasses and a helmet! But honestly, that’s part of what made it so thrilling  it’s raw, messy fun.
The village stop was another highlight. Locals, especially the children, came out to welcome us with songs and dances, including the lively “Jambo Jambo” tune that instantly puts you in a good mood. We interacted with them, shared sweets and biscuits, and got a brief explanation of their culture and way of life. It was warm, genuine, and memorable.
The final stop was another beachside location where we relaxed, enjoyed fresh tropical fruits, and admired the view of the ocean. You could see boats floating nearby and even watch locals working on traditional wooden boat-making a fascinating sight.
The journey back took us through both the village and city roads, giving us one last wave of excitement and scenery.
Overall, the Paiu Quad Bike Adventure is a must-try for anyone visiting Zanzibar. It’s exciting, immersive, and incredibly well-organized. Between the thrill of the ride, the warmth of the local community, and the beauty of the stops, it’s an experience that deserves a solid 10/10.

content:
Il quad è stato molto divertente.
Metto 4 stelle perché sono arrivati a prenderci con grande ritardo. Ci avevano detto alle 13:50, ma alle 14:20 non vedendo nessuno ho mandato il mio fidanzato a chiedere all’ufficio (dove non sapevano neanche della nostra prenotazione nonostante avessimo già pagato il 50%).
Alle fine sono arrivati con circa un’oretta di ritardo giustificandosi per “il traffico” (il posto distava circa 5 minuti di macchina).
Sappiamo che a Zanzibar sono tutti “pole pole” ma quando viene dato un orario di pick up è importante rispettarlo.
Soprattutto dal momento che i costi sono come quelli europei (abbiamo pagato 110 dollari x 1 quad), ci si aspetta puntualità.
A parte questo, il quad è stato divertente, ci hanno fatto visitare un villaggio locale ed è stato molto emozionante. Ti portano a comprare dolci e caramelle da dare ai bambini, ma ricordatevi che queste sostanze non forniscono nutrimento e calorie utili.. anzi sono pure dannose per i denti !! Abbiamo comprato un pacco da 50kg di riso, che costava un po’ di più, ma abbiamo visto che effettivamente è stata consegnata alle varie famiglie che si sono messe in fila per ricevere ognuna la sua porzione.
Do 4/5 perché davvero spero che possano migliorare sull’organizzazione.
translated_content:
The quad was a lot of fun.
I gave it 4 stars because they were very late picking us up. They told us to pick us up at 1:50 PM, but at 2:20 PM, seeing no one, I sent my boyfriend to the office (where they didn't even know we had booked, even though we had already paid 50%).
In the end, they arrived about an hour late, citing "traffic" (the location was about a 5-minute drive away).
We know everyone in Zanzibar is "pole pole," but when you're given a pick-up time, it's important to respect it.
Especially since the prices are similar to those in Europe (we paid $110 for one quad), punctuality is expected.
Aside from that, the quad was fun; they took us to a local village, which was very exciting. They take you to buy sweets and candies to give to the children, but remember that these substances don't provide any useful nutrients or calories... in fact, they're even bad for your teeth! We bought a 50kg package of rice, which cost a little more, but we saw that it was actually delivered to the various families who lined up to receive their portion.
I give it a 4/5 because I really hope they can improve their organization.

content:

Last week my husband and I had the pleasure of cooking with the Mamas of Zanzibar. It was an unforgettable experience - both for its authenticity as well as the warmth and love that the mamas bought to the cooking experience!
The day began with shopping for traditional ingredients at the local markets - coconuts, fruits, fresh fish and vegetables - followed by a hands on lesson in cleaning and preparing the ingredients, which also included making coconut milk from scratch - a messy but worthwhile experience :)
After a delicious breakfast, we marinated the vegetables and fish and were taught step by step how to cook each of the nine dishes that were to be our lunch for the day! My husband and I learnt a great deal about the carefully balanced flavours that make up Zanzibar cuisine and by the end of the day felt ready to cook our own dishes!
We also had the opportunity to learn about local Zanzibarian culture and tradition, as well as the changing attitudes towards gender norms and religious practices. The mamas were patient, kind and incredibly generous with their knowledge and we hope to return again soon!

content:
Wenn du alleine bis zum Ende des Riffs gehen möchtest, also dort wo die Wellen brechen ... vergiss es! Ich habe es versucht und sehr viel riskiert und musste vielleicht 30 Meter vor dem Ziel kapitulieren.
Es war wie in einem Labyrinth mit steigendem Schwierigkeitsgrad. Anfangs gehst du bei Ebbe noch durchs seichte Meer und den Sand. Dann werden es immer mehr Seeigel, da und dort sieht man auch Muränen oder Fische in den Korallen. Einen Weg zu finden zwischen den Seeigeln, wo man teilweise nur noch knapp eine Fusslänge Platz findet zum stehen ... schwierig und riskant. Und über die Korallen sollst du nicht gehen. Einerseits zerstört man diese und wenn eine Koralle einbricht, dann könnte sie dir die Beine bis auf die Knochen zerschneiden.
Wenn du dorthin möchtest, schnappe dir einen Guide oder jemand, der dich mit dem Boot dahin bringt. Ich begegnete dort zum Glück zwei einheimischen Fischern, welche mich zu Fuss aus dem Riff zurück zum Hotel gelotst haben.
translated_content:
If you want to walk all the way to the end of the reef on your own, where the waves break... forget it! I tried it, took a huge risk, and had to give up maybe 30 meters from the end.
It was like a labyrinth with increasing difficulty. At first, you walk through shallow water and sand at low tide. Then there are more and more sea urchins, and here and there you also see moray eels or fish among the coral. Finding a way through the sea urchins, where sometimes you only have about a foot's width of space to stand... difficult and risky. And you shouldn't walk on the coral. For one thing, you'll damage it, and if a piece of coral breaks, it could slice your legs down to the bone.
If you want to go there, get a guide or someone to take you by boat. Luckily, I met two local fishermen there who guided me on foot from the reef back to the hotel.

content:
Бродил по Стоун-Тауну и наткнулся на собор Святого Иосифа — тот самый с двумя башнями, которые видно издалека, если идти от рынка к морю.
Внутрь не заходил, но даже снаружи чувствуется сила места. Каменные стены, немного потемневшие от солнца и соли, и запах океана, который тянет с улицы прямо к воротам.
Стоишь у входа, и сразу представляешь, как его строили: конец XIX века, жара, французские миссионеры закладывают первый камень, вокруг ещё песчаные улочки и гул портового города. А теперь — всё тот же собор, те же башни, и над ними чайки, как тогда.
Мне хотелось зайти, но в тот день двери были закрыты. Так и остался стоять на улице, слушал, как изнутри доносится гул органа и детские голоса.
В этом есть что-то сильное — будто история не закончилась, просто живёт дальше, тихо, внутри этих стен.
translated_content:
I was wandering around Stone Town and came across St. Joseph's Cathedral—the one with the two towers visible from afar, walking from the market toward the sea.
I didn't go inside, but even from the outside, you can sense the power of the place. Stone walls, slightly darkened by sun and salt, and the scent of the ocean wafting from the street right to the gates.
Standing at the entrance, you can immediately imagine how it was built: the late 19th century, the heat, French missionaries laying the foundation stone, surrounded by sandy streets and the hum of a port city. And now—the same cathedral, the same towers, and seagulls above them, just like then.
I wanted to go inside, but the doors were closed that day. So I stood outside, listening to the hum of the organ and children's voices coming from within.
There's something powerful about it—as if history hasn't ended, but lives on, quietly, within these walls.
