content:
St. Joseph''s Cathedral, located in Stone Town, Zanzibar, is a significant historical and architectural landmark. Constructed by French missionaries between 1893 and 1898, the cathedral''s design was inspired by the Marseille Cathedral in France, evident in its prominent twin spires that dominate Stone Town''s skyline.
The cathedral''s interior once featured paintings depicting scenes from the Old Testament. However, these artworks were unfortunately destroyed during a restoration in 2014. The building materials, including tiles and stained glass windows, were imported from France, reflecting the European influence on its construction.
Situated in the Baghani area off Kenyatta Road, the cathedral remains an active place of worship for the local Catholic community, hosting several masses each Sunday and occasionally on weekdays. Its twin spires are easily visible from various vantage points in Stone Town and from the ocean, making it a notable feature of the city''s landscape.
In the narrow churchyard, there used to be a tall palm tree, which appeared in most pictures of the church; the tree was cut down sometime in the 2000s.
As one of the most important historical buildings in Stone Town, St. Joseph''s Cathedral attracts numerous visitors and continues to be a testament to Zanzibar''s rich cultural and religious heritage.

content:
St. Joseph’s Cathedral is an essential landmark to visit when in Stonetown. The cathedral’s interior boasts a remarkable design that vividly portrays the ancient history as described in the Holy Book, with a clear representation of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.
The location of St. Joseph’s right next to an old mosque is a profound testament to the harmonious coexistence of Christian and Islamic faiths in Zanzibar. This proximity highlights the unique cultural and religious tapestry of Stonetown.
I visited the cathedral on a Sunday, and while the worship times listed at the entrance may not always be accurate, it’s important to note that masses are held in both English and Swahili. Sunday services typically begin at 9 a.m., and weekday services start at 6 a.m., although these times can vary.
Visiting St. Joseph’s Cathedral offers not just a glimpse into the architectural beauty and spiritual heritage of Zanzibar, but also a deeper understanding of the island’s diverse and inclusive community.

content:
Is an important historical building located in the Baghani area of Stone Town, Zanzibar. It was built by French missionaries between 1893 and 1898, and the plans were drawn by the same French architect who designed the cathedral in Marseilles, France. The defining characteristic of the cathedral are its twin spires (similar to those of Marseille’s church) which are prominent elements of the Stone Town’s skyline and can be easily spotted from a distance off the coast. The cathedral interior is painted with murals from the Old Testament. The tiles and stained glass windows were all imported from France. The cathedral is in regular use by Stone Town’s Catholic community. There are several masses held each Sunday and occasionally on weekdays.
Ablution facilities need a little work and it can get a little crowded during peak times but a must see when in Stone Town.

He picks you up from your hotel in his comfortable taxi.

content:
Я разочарован. Обратились к Маго, почитав о нем отзывы в гугл. Отзывы лучше некуда. И вначале так и было. Несколько дней пользовались его услугами, ездили в Джозани, несколько раз в Стоунтаун – ответственный, общительный, все как в отзывах (цены у него средние).  С самого начала вели с ним разговор о поездке в Танзанию, в Арушу на Сафари. На два дня и одну ночь.
Договорились что это будут парки Тарангири и Нгорогоро, цена на человека включая перелет в обе стороны 520 долларов. На двоих 1040. Эта сумма им лично была написана на бумажке. И стоимость обсуждалась ежедневно. 500 долларов он попросил вперед (на авиабилеты). Остальную часть он сказал заплатить встречающей стороне в Аруше. Перед вылетом я еще раз уточнил, что должен оставшиеся 540 долларов заплатить человеку, который нас встретит? Маго это подтвердил. К этому моменту я всецело доверял Маго и у меня мысли даже не было, что этот человек может обмануть.
Но! Когда мы прилетели в Арушу, встречающий нас человек стал требовать 900 долларов (на 400 больше!), более того по его словам сафари  запланировано в парк Маньяра, а не Нгоронгоро. Естественно при себе 400 долларов у меня не было. Обратный билет через два дня и мы с женой стоим посреди Аруши, наше сафари стало большой неприятностью.  Тут же мы позвонили Маго и он,  стал обвинять во всем меня, что я глухой, что он с самого начала говорил, что цена на двоих 1400 долларов и что я все не так понял и что я должен заплатить.  А ведь цену в 520 долларов на человека (включая перелет) мы обсуждали с ним неоднократно. Как у него 520 с человека на двоих превратилось в 1400 я не знаю. Но из его слов я понял одно, что дурак я и виноват во всем я.
Потом уже, почитав интернет, я понял, что это распространенная практика на Занзибаре, говорить меньше, чтобы клиент точно купил (а Маго знал, что у нас бюджет 1000 и если бы он изначально сказал 1400 мы бы просто не полетели). В общем, сафари вышло совсем не таким, как мы ожидали – с решением кучи проблем. Врать не хорошо, Маго! Я разочарован. Обращаться к Маго не рекомендую.
translated_content:
I'm disappointed. We contacted Mago after reading reviews on Google. The reviews couldn't be better. And that was the case at first. We used his services for a few days, went to Jozani, and a few times to Stone Town – he's responsible, communicative, and everything he said he did (his prices are average). From the very beginning, we talked about a trip to Tanzania, to Arusha for a safari. It was two days and one night.
We agreed on Tarangiri and Ngorogoro National Parks, and the price per person, including roundtrip airfare, was $520. For two, it was $1,040. He personally wrote this amount down on a piece of paper. And the price was discussed daily. He asked for $500 upfront (for airfare). He said to pay the rest to the person who would meet us in Arusha. Before departure, I reiterated that I should pay the remaining $540 to the person who would meet us. Mago confirmed this. By this point, I trusted Mago completely and it never even crossed my mind that this man could cheat.
But! When we arrived in Arusha, the man meeting us started demanding $900 ($400 more!), and he even said the safari was scheduled for Manyara National Park, not Ngorongoro. Naturally, I didn't have $400 on me. With a return ticket in two days, and my wife and I standing in the middle of Arusha, our safari had become a major bummer. We immediately called Mago, and he started accusing me of being deaf, saying he'd said $1,400 for two from the start, and that I'd misunderstood and that I should pay. We'd discussed the price of $520 per person (including airfare) with him several times. How he'd turned $520 per person for two into $1,400, I don't know. But from his words, I understood one thing: I was the fool and it was all my fault.
Later, after reading online, I realized it's common practice in Zanzibar to say less to ensure the client buys (and Mago knew our budget was 1,000, and if he'd initially said 1,400, we simply wouldn't have flown). Overall, the safari turned out completely different from what we expected—with a ton of problems to solve. Lying is not nice, Mago! I'm disappointed. I don't recommend using Mago.
response_content: Misunderstanding of Price But thank you
full_address: Magozanzibar Tours, Matemwe, Zanzibar, Tanzania

Partiti in 5 con una barchetta locale dalla spiaggia di Michamvi del Bahati Sunset Bungalow, abbiamo visitato dopo 40 minuti di traversata,  questa area molto ricca di pesci (quasi tutti quelli che si possono trovare nel Mar Rosso ) e coralli che ancora mantengono un pò di colore.

Super consigliato!!

Undoubtedly a thousand times better than Mnemba, which is much more barren and overcrowded with tourists!
With the luck of full sun, visibility was perfect and the water crystal clear.
The tour concluded with a visit to The Rock, a stop at the sandbar, and a final swim in the starfish area.
Highly recommended!

content:
Die Blue Lagoon wurde überall als Traumtour angepriesen: Sandbank, Früchte, Schnorcheln, BBQ mit Meeresfrüchten. GetYourGuide voll mit Top-Bewertungen. Klingt paradiesisch – war es leider ganz und gar nicht.
Los ging’s damit, dass wir vom Guide am Strand einfach an den Kapitän „übergeben“ wurden. Wegen Ebbe mussten hunderte Touristen zu den Booten laufen – eine wahre Völkerwanderung. Unser Kapitän entschied sich dann spontan, uns einfach stehen zu lassen, weil andere Guides meinten, wir sollen warten. Spoiler: Niemand kam zurück.
Nach 1,5 Stunden wurden wir zufällig von einem anderen Guide entdeckt und kurzerhand einer italienischen Gruppe „dazugesteckt“.
Dann ging es mit einem kleinen Ruderboot zu einem komplett überfüllten Dhow. Die Leute dort wollten uns verständlicherweise nicht mehr reinlassen. Besonders absurd: Ein Pärchen hatte eine private Tour für zwei Personen gebucht – und stand trotzdem mit uns auf diesem überfüllten Boot. Organisation auf höchstem Niveau.
Also wieder umsteigen: vom Ruderboot auf ein kleines Motorboot, das uns zu einer Sandbank brachte. Kein Schatten, extrem viele Touristen, kurz ein paar Früchte (ja, die gab es), aber die Stimmung war längst im Keller. Aufenthalt: ca. 30 Minuten. Die Sandbank war so voll, dass man sich fragte, wie da überhaupt noch ein weiteres Boot anlegen soll.
Danach wollten wir eigentlich zum BBQ. Problem: Wir hatten kein Boot mehr.
Also warteten wir 2 Stunden in der prallen Sonne (Sonnencreme dringend empfohlen, die Sonne in Sansibar meint es ernst). Dadurch blieben uns fürs Schnorcheln stolze 10 Minuten, weil die Wartezeit natürlich von der Aktivität abgezogen wurde.
Das BBQ fand auf einer Insel statt, die ausschließlich auf Massentourismus ausgelegt ist: Märkte mit billigem Krimskrams, Menschenmassen und ein Essensbereich, bei dem man eher Angst vor einer Lebensmittelvergiftung bekommt als Vorfreude auf Meeresfrüchte. Von Hummer, Thunfisch oder Calamari keine Spur – für uns gab es sicherheitshalber Pommes. Immerhin die waren schwer zu verderben.
Als der Kapitän später unsere Schnorchelausrüstung abholte, kam der erlösende Moment:
„Oh shit – das sind die Leute, die ich verloren habe.“
Kein Witz. Danach wurde hektisch jemand gesucht, der Englisch spricht, man entschuldigte sich halbherzig, wir mussten die nette Gruppe verlassen und wurden erneut irgendwo untergebracht, weil dieses Boot größer war.
Zum Abschluss noch ein kurzer Stopp in einer Bucht zum Reinspringen – sehr kurz – und dann endlich zurück.
Fazit:
Diese Tour ist perfekt organisiert, wenn das Ziel ist, Touristen möglichst lange warten zu lassen, sie mehrfach umzubooten und ihnen jede Illusion von einem entspannten Ausflug zu nehmen. Absolute Massenabfertigung, keinerlei Planung, null Romantik, null Entspannung.
Wer echtes Sansibar erleben möchte: Finger weg.
Wer Chaosurlaub mag: Viel Spaß.
translated_content:
The Blue Lagoon was touted everywhere as a dream tour: sandbank, fruit, snorkeling, seafood BBQ. GetYourGuide was full of top ratings. Sounds like paradise – unfortunately, it was anything but.
It started with our guide simply "handing us off" to the captain on the beach. Because of the low tide, hundreds of tourists had to walk to the boats – a veritable mass migration. Our captain then spontaneously decided to just leave us standing there, because other guides told us to wait. Spoiler alert: Nobody came back.
After 1.5 hours, we were spotted by chance by another guide and promptly "added" to an Italian group.
Then we were taken in a small rowboat to a completely overcrowded dhow. Understandably, the people there didn't want to let us on. Particularly absurd: A couple had booked a private tour for two – and yet they were still stuck on this overcrowded boat with us. Organization at its finest.
So, another transfer: from the rowboat to a small motorboat that took us to a sandbank. No shade, tons of tourists, a quick bite of fruit (yes, they had some), but the mood had long since soured. We stayed for about 30 minutes. The sandbank was so crowded that we wondered how another boat could even dock there.
Afterwards, we wanted to go to the BBQ. Problem: We had no boat left.
So we waited two hours in the blazing sun (sunscreen is highly recommended; the Zanzibar sun is intense). This left us with a grand total of 10 minutes for snorkeling, since the waiting time was, of course, deducted from the actual activity.
The BBQ took place on an island geared entirely towards mass tourism: markets with cheap trinkets, crowds of people, and a food area that made you fear food poisoning rather than look forward to seafood. Not a trace of lobster, tuna, or calamari – we played it safe and got fries. At least they were hard to spoil.
When the captain later came to collect our snorkeling gear, the moment of relief arrived:
"Oh shit – these are the people I lost."
No joke. After that, there was a frantic search for someone who spoke English, half-hearted apologies, we had to leave the nice group, and were put up somewhere else again because this boat was bigger.
Finally, a quick stop in a bay for a dip – very quick – and then finally back.
Conclusion:
This tour is perfectly organized if the goal is to make tourists wait as long as possible, change boats multiple times, and shatter any illusion of a relaxing excursion. Absolute mass processing, no planning whatsoever, zero romance, zero relaxation.
If you want to experience the real Zanzibar: stay away.
If you like chaotic vacations: have fun.
full_address: RGJJ+2RW Blue Lagoon, Unnamed Road, Dongwe, Tanzania

content:
Wir haben unser eigenes Schnorchel Equipment und wollten gerne auf eigene Faust los schnorcheln. Alle haben uns gesagt, man muss auf jeden Fall ein Boot haben, aber wollen damit nur die Touren verkaufen. Es geht aber doch: Wir sind dann mit einem Roller beim Dongwe Beach Restaurant runter und so weit es geht nach Norden gefahren. Zu Fuß sind es vielleicht 15-20 Minuten, bis der Strand endet und es felsig wird. Von dort aus sieht man bereits die Bojen, die den Bereich kennzeichnen und wahrscheinlich auch die anderen Boote. Mit Flossen musste man nur noch vielleicht 5 Minuten schwimmen (je nach Strömung). Vorsicht mit all den Seeigeln beim Einstieg!
Die Blue Lagoon hat sehr viele bunte Fische, leider sind viele der Korallen nicht mehr am leben. Man sollte sehr aufpassen, nichts mit den Flossen oder sogar Händen zu berühren, um der Unterwasserwelt nicht zu schaden!!
translated_content:
We had our own snorkeling gear and wanted to snorkel on our own. Everyone told us we absolutely needed a boat, but they were just trying to sell us tours. It's actually possible: We took a scooter down from the Dongwe Beach Restaurant and drove as far north as we could. It's maybe a 15-20 minute walk until the beach ends and it gets rocky. From there, you can already see the buoys marking the area and probably the other boats as well. With fins, it was only a 5-minute swim (depending on the current). Be careful of all the sea urchins when entering the water!
The Blue Lagoon has lots of colorful fish, but unfortunately, many of the corals are no longer alive. You should be very careful not to touch anything with your fins or even your hands to avoid damaging the underwater world!

content:
We found this spice farm on Google Maps because of its great reviews, and it turned out to be exactly what we were hoping for.
We specifically wanted a small, authentic, locally run spice farm — not a big tourist operation or a commercialized attraction. And that’s exactly what we got here.
We contacted him via WhatsApp (the number is listed on Google Maps) and the communication was super quick and friendly. We arranged a time for the next day without any complications. He also asked in advance if we would like to stay for lunch and what we preferred — fish, meat, or vegetarian — and mentioned that the meal was definitely worth it.
The price was only $12 per person including lunch, which is honestly incredible value for the experience you get.
At first glance the spice farm almost looks like a simple garden — a bit wild and very natural — but once you start walking through it, you realize how much is actually growing there. There are so many different trees, plants, fruits, vegetables and spices hidden all around the property.
The tour itself was amazing. He is an incredibly friendly and funny host with lots of jokes and even some German skills, which made it extra fun for us. The whole experience was very interactive: we smelled, tasted and tried to guess many different spices and fruits — probably 10 to 15 different things — and we received small samples of many of them as well.
After the tour we sat down traditionally on the floor and were served lunch. Everything was freshly prepared and incredibly delicious. It felt very authentic and homemade, and we were also served tea with the meal.
At the end we had the chance to buy some spices directly from the farm — and the prices were unbelievably fair. For example, I bought eight large, high-quality vanilla pods for only about 2–3€ in total, plus several other spices. It didn’t feel touristy or overpriced at all — quite the opposite.
This place is the real deal: authentic, welcoming and run with a lot of heart.
Absolutely recommended — 10/10.

content:

Wir waren mit dem Hotel-Team unterwegs und einige Massai gesellten sich dazu. Sie waren sehr hilfreich, zeigten uns genau, wo wir durchgehen müssen, denn je nach dem ist es mit den Sandbänken, Seegras, Seeigeln und scharfen Korallen wie in einem Labyrinth. Uns haben die Massai wirklich sehr gut geholfen, auch wenn das Hotel-Team dabei war. Sie halfen auch den älteren Leuten, stützten, reichten die Hand usw. Beim Starfish-Spot posierten sie zusammen mit uns für Selfies und knipsten Gruppenfotos. Wir hatten viel geredet und gelacht. translated_content:
Beautiful spot. Locals collect starfish and leave them here. Otherwise, you'd have to be really lucky to find one while walking on the reef.
I recommend either going there with the hotel staff or trying to attract a Maasai, who will approach you anyway as soon as you start walking towards the reef at low tide. Of course, you might initially think the Maasai are trying to sell you something. Nope, they'll tell you all about the reef and are great conversationalists. They'll ask you lots of questions, so don't hesitate to ask them too. You'll learn all sorts of things about the language, culture, and the Maasai themselves.
We went with the hotel staff, and some Maasai joined us. They were very helpful, showing us exactly where to go, because depending on the location, it's like a labyrinth with the sandbanks, seagrass, sea urchins, and sharp coral. The Maasai were a great help to us, even with the hotel staff present. They also helped the elderly, supporting them, offering a hand, and so on. At the starfish spot, they posed with us for selfies and took group photos. We talked and laughed a lot. When we got back, we bought quite a few things in their shops to show our appreciation. Thank you to the Maasai who helped us.
full_address: 398F+79 Starfish spot, Pwani Mchangani, Tanzania

content: OK, let me tell you about this place. We were staying at the Royal Mandarin hotel and I started walking towards the low tide when Masai men reached out to me and told me about this place. I saw that it’s real through the comments but let me tell you more details about it. Those men definitely come near you and help you by being very respectful and polite, but they expect money from you. To be honest, they definitely deserve it because they truly take care of you. They show you different sea creatures as you’re getting closer to the starfish spot. They clear out the sea urchins that they’re on your way and they show you the right path. One thing that it’s misleading is that they try and reach you by walking for 50 minutes towards that spot and then when you say that, you’re in a rush to get back, you can get back in 20 to 30 minutes. But I definitely recommend going there. Just make sure that you have enough time to walk to that spot. Stay there and enjoy and then go back. I would say wake up really early because the sun is unbearable at times start walking right there and they even collect all the starfish and bring them to you. I don’t think it’s ethical to touch the starfish at all, but those men definitely do show you their mouth their eyes so they touch them. They also grab them and put them on you to take a picture. They put them on my head on my shoulders and on my hands. And they do make Christmas trees with all the starfish. The starfish look healthy and some are really large so I hope that they have been used to humans touching them. Nevertheless, it’s a really great spot and a really great idea to do in the morning while you’re staying on that side of the beach. Just make sure that you definitely have money on you because reaching that spot is not possible without the Masai. We left them 10,000 in cash each person.
full_address: 398F+79 Starfish spot, Pwani Mchangani, Tanzania

content: This area can be walked out to from the beaches at the nearby hotels such as Ocean Paradise Resort or Tui Blue at low tide. It is quite a walk and there are many other sea creatures to be aware of as you walk, particularly sea urchins which can be very painful if stepped on. There are Massai men on the beaches that will walk with you, guide you through the best route and show you the sea creatures on the way. They are friendly, respectful and caring towards the sea creatures. I was shown the sea urchins, sea cucumbers and clown fish as well as the starfish. The young Massai man that walked us out even insisted I wear his shoes to avoid injury as I had gone out barefoot, which  I would not recommend. Altogether we spent about 2 hours enjoying this experience. Taking tourists out to the reef is a large part of the livelihood of these men and their families and so I made sure I paid him fairly for his time and effort.

content:
This extensive archaeological site preserves the remains of a wealthy maritime settlement dating from the 11th–12th centuries.
Around 40 large coral-ragstone houses have been identified, many built around substantial courtyards. Among the ruins is a large structure identified by archaeologists as the palace of the local Shirazi governor or Sheha.
A small staircase leads down towards the beach. Carved into the coral ragstone, it features ancient holes thought to have held flagpoles, possibly serving as a navigational beacon or signalling point for incoming dhows.

Но как же приятно отдавать эти деньги труженикам, которые своими руками создают возможность прикоснуться к аутентичности прекрасной природы острова. Особенно это приятно в сравнении с деньгами, которые мы отдаем назойливыми и разбалованными продавьцами надоевших развлечений пляжного отдыха отелей, где цены завышены в десятки раз. translated_content: A heartfelt project by intelligent people who are passionate about their country's nature, speak excellent English, and treat guests with warmth and care, who visit this secluded spot in a traditional Zanzibar village called Tazari. I'll be honest, we only learned about this place because we came to see the chameleons and the cave, a 10-minute walk from the farm. The young farmer and his family are just getting started with this project, so our visit felt more like a small donation (just $4 per person). But how wonderful it is to give this money to the workers who, with their own hands, create the opportunity to experience the authenticity of the island's beautiful nature. This is especially gratifying compared to the money we spend on pushy and spoiled vendors of tired beach-themed entertainment at hotels where prices are tenfold inflated. We give the butterfly farm 5 stars not for the luxury, but for the warmth of the project.

Wo uns Felix viel über die Stadt und ihre Geschichte erzählte. Als Tipp: wenn ihr Gewürze kaufen wollt, nicht auf der Gewürzfarm, sondern am Markt in Stonetown kaufen - ist dort günstiger ;)

We gave him a tip for it.

content:
Mangapwani Slave Chamber Tour
Slave Chambers: Built around 1880 from the cave and connected to the seaside 2kms away, the area is surrounded by varieties of indigenous trees such as Breadfruit, Ramboutants and scent shrubs.
It was an important transit point for the captured slaves to be sold to the outside world at the time of the abolishment of slavery in 1873. Between 1880-1905, the chamber was being used as a place of concealment of the human cargo pending their disposal.
A utilized as the hideout by the Arabs for their human cargo ready for shipment. The four hour guided tour begins and ends at your hotel. Mangapwani (“Arab Shore”) lies in a district where many Arabs used to live.
In the village there is a Police Station, also a large government “Bungalow” which was built by the Arabs who originally owned Prison Island. Newly opened Serena Restaurant is nearby the Slave Caves. Swimming, Sun bathing may be done widely.

content:
My husband and I visited Stone Town with the hope of finding some meaningful artwork to take home, and we were lucky enough to stumble upon this beautiful boutique gallery tucked away in a quiet alley. The space was small but filled with truly unique and captivating paintings. We explored other parts of Stone Town afterward, but we kept thinking about this gallery and ended up coming back because nothing else compared to it.
We were a bit rushed that day, so the next morning we contacted Othman to ask if it was possible to see more artworks at our hotel, as our friends were also interested and it was too far to return to Stone Town. To our surprise, Othman went above and beyond and arranged a mini pop-up art exhibition right in our hotel car park the very same day.
The collection he brought was absolutely amazing. In the end, we and our friends purchased six paintings in total, and we couldn’t be happier to bring home such special memories of Zanzibar. Abdul, the driver, was incredibly friendly and even helped remove the paintings from the canvases to make traveling easier.
Othman is extremely knowledgeable and passionate, and he took the time to explain the background and stories behind the artworks, which made the experience even more meaningful. This was truly one of the highlights of our trip, and I highly recommend this gallery to anyone visiting Stone Town and looking for something authentic and unforgettable.

content:
Leider war diese Tour eine große Enttäuschung. Wir wählten die nakupenda, prison Island & Stone town.
Die Organisation war katastrophal: Schon beim Abholen wurden wir nur schnell abkassieret, man drückte uns in irgendeinen Bus – und verschwand. Wir wussten nicht, was los war. Kein Plan an wen wir uns halten sollen odersonstiges. Erst durch Nachfragen stellte sich heraus, dass es der richtige Bus ist. Nach wenigen Minuten Fahrt hielt der Bus an einer Tankstelle, ohne Info für die Gäste. Am Ende mussten alle 25 Minuten warten, nur weil zwei Gäste auf eine andere Tour gebucht waren.
Der Busfahrer fuhr wie eine gesenkte Sau, ohne Rücksicht auf Verluste. Mehrmals hatten wir ernsthafte Angst vor einem Unfall.
Auf Prison Island angekommen, ging es mit extrem langsamen Booten weiter. Die Boote waren echt verranzt & in keinem guten Zustand. Nach dem Motto „Hauptsache geht nicht unter“. Seekranke hatten hier schon verloren, da die Boote im Schneckentempo übers Meer gekrochen sind & es dadurch extrem schaukelt.Die Insel selbst ist heruntergekommen, überfüllt und wenig sehenswert.
Danach ging es zur Nakupenda Sandbank. Statt Trauminsel mit klarem Wasser: überfüllt, grünlich-trübes Wasser, Verkäufer bedrängen die Gäste permanent, selbst beim Essen. Am Strand lagen sogar Reste vom Mittagessen herum (z. B. Garnelenköpfe). Schattenplätze bestehen aus notdürftig gespannten Decken.
Das Essen: Für Meeresfrüchte-Fans vielleicht okay (Hummer usw.), für uns aber nichts. Als Alternative gab es Hühnchen – leider ungenießbar: meine Freundin bekam ein kleines Stück mit Fleisch, ich nur Knochen mit Haut und Knorpel. Reis und Pommes waren in Ordnung, Obst dagegen sehr lecker. Satt wurden wir nicht.
Auch die Rückfahrt war chaotisch: Ein Paar, das schon zuvor alle warten ließ, kam wieder nicht pünktlich. Das Boot legte ohne sie ab, musste umdrehen, und der Mann drehte völlig durch – aggressiv, beleidigend, fast gewalttätig gegenüber dem Guide. Sehr unangenehm für alle Mitreisenden.
Die Stone-Town-Tour bestand im Wesentlichen aus kurzem Durchhetzen durch die Straßen und viel Zeit in Souvenirläden.
Positiv: Die Guides (besonders Rasheed & Mudi) waren sehr freundlich und Getränke sowie Obst gab es genug.
Fazit: Eine reine Massenabfertigung ohne Qualität. Wir waren sehr enttäuscht, hatten teilweise sogar Angst im Bus, und würden stattdessen die Mnemba Island Tour empfehlen – dort ist es traumhaft und stressfrei.
translated_content:
Unfortunately, this tour was a huge disappointment. We chose the Nakupenda, Prison Island & Stone Town tour.
The organization was disastrous: Upon pickup, we were quickly charged, shoved onto some random bus, and then disappeared. We had no idea what was going on. There was no plan for who to contact or anything else. Only after asking around did we find out it was the right bus. After a few minutes, the bus stopped at a gas station without informing the passengers. In the end, everyone had to wait 25 minutes simply because two passengers were booked on a different tour.
The bus driver drove like a maniac, completely disregarding safety. Several times we were genuinely afraid of an accident.
Once we arrived at Prison Island, we continued our journey in extremely slow boats. The boats were truly dilapidated and in terrible condition. It was as if their motto was "as long as they don't sink." Seasickness sufferers were already at their wits' end here, as the boats crawled across the sea at a snail's pace, causing extreme rocking. The island itself is run-down, overcrowded, and not very appealing.
Afterwards, we went to the Nakupenda sandbank. Instead of a dream island with clear water, it was overcrowded, with greenish-murky water, and vendors constantly pestered the guests, even while eating. Leftovers from lunch were even lying around on the beach (e.g., shrimp heads). Shady spots consisted of makeshift blankets.
The food: Perhaps okay for seafood lovers (lobster, etc.), but not for us. As an alternative, there was chicken – unfortunately inedible: My girlfriend got a small piece with meat, I only got bones with skin and cartilage. Rice and fries were fine, but the fruit was very tasty. We weren't full.
The return trip was also chaotic: A couple who had already kept everyone waiting were late again. The boat left without them, had to turn around, and the man completely lost it – aggressive, insulting, almost violent towards the guide. Very unpleasant for all the other passengers.
The Stone Town tour essentially consisted of rushing through the streets and spending a lot of time in souvenir shops.
On the plus side: The guides (especially Rasheed and Mudi) were very friendly, and there were plenty of drinks and fruit.
In conclusion: A pure mass-market experience with no quality. We were very disappointed, were even afraid at times on the bus, and would recommend the Mnemba Island tour instead – it's beautiful and stress-free.
full_address: Rasco Tours Zanzibar, Nungwi, Tanzania

It's a shame because the beach is spectacular, the sea has gorgeous colors, and you can always swim because it's not much affected by the tides.

Estábamos en Zanzíbar hace más de una semana y ya habíamos hecho varias excursiones. Sin dudas Francis fue EL MEJOR!!

We were in Zanzibar for over a week and had already done several excursions. Without a doubt, Francis was THE BEST!!

The boat was beautiful, super comfortable with plenty of cushions, clean, with a table and lounge chairs for eating, and relaxing areas for sunbathing. There were snacks, fresh fruit, ice-cold drinks, and a speaker for music.
The staff was incredibly friendly and respectful.

Without a doubt, an unforgettable and highly recommended experience. Lubaacris is the most professional and reliable agency in Zanzibar 🤩.
Thank you and see you soon!!!
Meli and Gianmarco

content:
Kendwa Beach on Zanzibar''s northwestern coast is a haven for sun-seekers and water enthusiasts. Here''s a quick glimpse:
Paradise Found: Imagine soft, white sand beneath your toes, turquoise waters lapping at the shore, and swaying palm trees providing shade. That''s the idyllic picture Kendwa Beach paints.
Activities Galore: This beach caters to active spirits. Dive into the crystal-clear waters for snorkeling or scuba diving adventures exploring vibrant coral reefs. For those who prefer staying above water, options like kayaking, stand-up paddleboarding, and kiteboarding due to favorable wind conditions are all on the table.
Relaxation at its Finest: If unwinding is your priority, Kendwa Beach delivers. Stretch out on a sun lounger, listen to the calming rhythm of the waves, and soak up the African sunshine.
Lively Atmosphere: Unlike its neighbor Nungwi, Kendwa boasts a more vibrant scene. Beachside restaurants and bars offer delicious local and international cuisine alongside refreshing drinks. In the evenings, some spots transform with live music and dancing, making Kendwa a great choice for those who enjoy a bit of nightlife after a day of relaxation.
Perfect for All: Whether you crave adventure, relaxation, or a touch of both, Kendwa Beach offers something for everyone. Soak up the beauty, enjoy the activities, and experience the lively spirit of this captivating beach paradise.

content:
Думаю, лучший пляж на Занзибаре. Мягкий песок, спокойная вода, чистое дно. Отливы метров на 10 сдвигают линию моря, далеко идти не придётся, в отличие от востока острова.
Если собираетесь ехать на Занзибар, нужно ехать прямо сейчас. Тут живёт огромное количество морских звёзд, во время отлива их прямо десятки и сотни под ногами. Но местные жители вообще не разбираются в биологии, достают их из воды надолго, дают фоткаться туристам. Звёзды умирают, если больше 30 секунд находятся не в воде, так что через несколько лет их тут уже не останется.
translated_content:
I think this is the best beach in Zanzibar. Soft sand, calm water, and a clean seabed. Low tides shift the sea level by about 10 meters, so you won't have to walk far, unlike on the east side of the island.
If you're planning a trip to Zanzibar, you need to go now. There are a huge number of starfish here; at low tide, there are dozens and hundreds of them right under your feet. But the locals don't understand anything about starfish biology; they take them out of the water for long periods of time and let tourists take photos. The stars die if they're out of the water for more than 30 seconds, so in a few years, there won't be any left.

content: Bueno para empezar hemos hecho la caminata de 1 h , nada más llegar te para un hombre que te dice los precios y que es obligatorio ir con guía, precio para  adulto 12$/ persona. Además nos dice que tenemos que darle una propina obligatoria al guía de 25000 chelines. De risa. Después de mirarlo bien, le decimos que la propina es la que nosotros elijamos y no lo que nos había dicho. Y acepta. Ya empezamos mal. Luego la caminata por el bosque ha sido 10 minutos. Y después te sacan al la calle que hay al otro lado de la carretera justo a la entrada y siguiendo recto a mano izquierda te meten en una casa de alguien,en  una especie de patio a ver los monos. Si es verdad que están en libertad pero vamos….. luego si sigues hasta el final de la calle ves los manglares. Vamos que lo puedes hacer por tu cuenta. Realmente del bosque no ves nada. Una trampa para turistas. No lo recomiendo. Partiendo de la base que nos han intentado engañar nada más llegar diciendo que la propina es obligatoria. Precio del tour muy elevado para lo que ofrecen.
translated_content: Well, to begin with, we did the 1-hour hike. As soon as we arrived, a man stopped us and told us the prices and that it was mandatory to have a guide; the price for adults was $12 per person. He also told us we had to give the guide a mandatory tip of 25,000 shillings. It was laughable. After looking into it, we told him that the tip was whatever we chose, not what he had told us. And he agreed. We were already off to a bad start. Then the walk through the forest was only 10 minutes. After that, they took us out onto the street across the road, right at the entrance, and if you continue straight ahead on the left, they took you into someone's house, into a kind of courtyard, to see the monkeys. It's true they're free-roaming, but come on... then if you continue to the end of the street, you see the mangroves. Basically, you can do it on your own. You don't really see any of the forest. A tourist trap. I don't recommend it. Especially since they tried to trick us as soon as we arrived by saying the tip was mandatory. The tour price is very high for what they offer.

content: Kuza Cave is such an amazing place and a must see, especially if visiting Zanzibar with kids.  My son and I spent a whole day and evening there starting with a swim in the ceremonial cave waters which were gloriously clear, a great temperature to swim in & surrounded by an amazing cave.  Backdropping the cave swimming is the sounds of Swahili drumming put on by the very talented group at the attached cultural center.  We were welcomed into the drumming circle as we exited the cave and immediately provided drums so we could take part.  After a quick change of cloths we took a Swahili cooking class which offered us a deliciuos lunch.  While I rested my son spent the afternoon engrossed in various art projects centered around both African and global art, history and culture.  As afternoon rolled into evening we were invited back to dining room delicious Swahili starters and drinks.  We soon moved to an outdoor seating area where we spent the evening immersed in very well thought out, prepared and presented music & theatre performance put on by Swahili locals which provided a deep history of Africa and the origins of human existance.  A spectacularly education and relaxing day!

content:
Отдыхали на Занзибаре в 2021 году. Перез поездкой видели на многих сайтах и во многих передачах про Занзибар, что нужно побывать в этой пещере. На самом деле, как по мне, вход своих денег не стоял. We vacationed in Zanzibar in 2021. Before our trip, we'd seen on many websites and in many Zanzibar shows that we had to visit this cave. In reality, for me, the entrance wasn't worth the money. There was no properly equipped entrance, no one accompanied us or explained anything. It's not entirely clear what we were paying for.
Swimming in the water was unusual; the local fish nipped at our skin. I recommend going on your own, without a tour. If you go with a group, the water will be murky and the fish will bite you.

La grotte de Kuza est une formation géologique d''environ 250 000 ans.
Elle fut l''un des secrets les mieux gardés de Zanzibar !

Dans tous les cas quelque chose de très fort est toujours là de bien présent. On aimerait y rester seul un moment !...
translated_content:
Kuza Cave is a geological formation approximately 250,000 years old.
It was one of Zanzibar's best-kept secrets!
This place is truly exceptional. An atmosphere of mystery, peace, and beauty envelops you during your exploration. And the crystal-clear turquoise waters add to the enchantment. Ancient rituals have been practiced here since time immemorial. In any case, something very powerful is always present. You'd like to stay there alone for a while!

translated_content: The scenery that nature has provided is worthy, but it's not maintained as it should be. The rope that serves as a handrail to reach the crystal-clear water is untouchable, sticky and greasy from too many hands clinging to it. content: A really nice place to visit. The entrance fee is 20.000 shilling (in cash) and the money goes to the community around the cave. We visited before the rain season started so the water level was quite low, but in rain season the water level rises incredibly high (you can see the green algae on some photos taken at the top of the cave), so it would be a completely different experience to come and swim in the rain season. The water is cold when you step in (since the temperature is so high in general), but give it a few seconds and it becomes this really cool and relaxing experience. I’m really glad we went, I’m just glad I remembered to bring cash since they don’t take credit cards (as far as I could see). The water changes from quite shallow to deep in a heart beat (I’m 177 cm and couldn’t stand on half the area), so just know how to swim (or float) or stay close to the edge of the water. Oh, also, this is a natural cave so the stones in the water are sharp, this is not a pool, just so you remember to swim and place your feet carefully 😊 They also sell drinks at the community center before you enter the cave. And there is an old style swahili house you can enter to see how they used to build them (using no metal, just wood, earth, stones, rope and palm leaves)

content:
Были в январе 2021, можно легко найти самим (дорога прям напротив апартов Тина Хаус), вход 10$ с человека. Интересно посетить так так это необычное место и эмоции остаются в воспоминаниях. Вода прозрачная и прохладная, в такую жару самое оно! Специально прям ехать туда наверное не сильно надо, а вот если будете жить рядом в том районе, то интересно. Мы селились там рядом на 1 ночь, был перевалочный момент по пути и потом уехали на другой пляж.
Невероятные архитектурные формы, созданные самой природой, поражают воображение. Пещеры Куза представляют собой удивительное явление естественного рельефа, которому местное население приписывает мистические свойства.
Пресноводный водоем, скрытый скальным массивом от солнечного света на острове посреди соленых океанских волн, самим своим существованием наводит на мысли о происхождении чудес природы.
Коренные островитяне издревле считали своды Куза священными.
Многие века к ним приходили религиозные процессии для проведения обрядов и вознесения молитв. Старинные легенды овевают каменные лабиринты, до сих пор полностью не исследованные – в сгущающемся мраке в глубине можно разглядеть потаенные ответвления и коридоры и по сей день несколько дней в году выделяется для совершения традиционных церемоний, когда пещеру закрывают от посторонних глаз.
translated_content:
We visited in January 2021. It's easy to find (the road is right across from the Tina House apartments). Entrance is $10 per person. It's a unique place, and the memories are unforgettable. The water is clear and cool, perfect for this heat! You probably don't need to make a special trip there, but if you live nearby, it's a great experience. We stayed there for one night; we stopped there on the way, and then went to another beach.
The incredible architectural forms created by nature itself are breathtaking. The Kuza Caves are a remarkable natural formation, ascribed mystical properties by the local population.
A freshwater pond, hidden from sunlight by a rock massif on an island amidst salty ocean waves, its very existence evokes thoughts about the origins of natural wonders.
The indigenous islanders have long considered the Kuza Caves sacred. For centuries, religious processions have come here to perform rituals and offer prayers. Ancient legends surround the stone labyrinths, which remain completely unexplored. In the deepening darkness, hidden passages and corridors can be discerned. To this day, several days a year are set aside for traditional ceremonies, when the cave is closed to prying eyes.

content: Кораллки обязательно, кое-где камни скользкие, если видите зеленоватый налет, значит это мох и камень скользкий. Там темно, мрачно. Под стенами этой пещеры под водой есть гроты, ниши, углубления, довольно большие, и не очень. Туда интересно занырнуть и посидеть несколько секунд, ощущая себя в водной пещере, в скалистой норе целиком под водой, с каменным потолком над головой. Адреналин еще тот. Безопасно, если  хорошо видите, умеете дышать и ориентироваться.  Просто так поплескаться в общей массе с туристами, толкаясь в узких местах, мне лично было не очень интересно.
translated_content: There are definitely corals, and some rocks are slippery. If you see a greenish coating, it's moss and slippery rock. It's dark and gloomy there. For those who enjoy diving, snorkeling, and diving, here's a tip: bring a mask, snorkel, and underwater light. Tour guides don't mention this because they're afraid of liability, and it's impossible to see from the surface and in the darkness. Beneath the walls of this cave, underwater, there are grottoes, niches, and depressions, some quite large, some not so large. It's fascinating to dive in and sit for a few seconds, feeling like you're in a water cave, a rocky hole completely underwater, with a stone ceiling above your head. It's an adrenaline rush. It's safe if you have good vision, breathing, and orientation. I personally wasn't very interested in just splashing around with the crowd of tourists, jostling in narrow spaces.

content: It seems my experience was very different to others. I can only guess with the number of good reviews, perhaps we picked an off day to visit. The cave was one of the first on my list to try and I was disappointed and a little uncomfortable. On arrival I was surprised to feel unwelcome by the staff. This was not the welcome I have come to know of  Zanzibar. We paid $20 using a $50 and were told we could get our change on the way out. This seemed a little strange and judging by the less than welcoming feel we encountered, we asked if we might be able to have our money before going in to cave. The young man spoke with a lady who was watching while she cooked and returned to say no, we would get our money later. Perhaps this was all we needed to have a less than pleasant experience in the cave. We were told the water and caves were old and when we asked about the colour, was it the minerals in the caves, the answer was no it was just nature. I''m sorry to leave this review as I wish the organisers well in their contribution to the community from the money from this but it all felt like a lot of money for a 2 minute dip then leave?

Our goal is to provide educational, fun, and informative experiences for all of our guests, and it is clear that we did not achieve this goal during your visit. For this, I am truly sorry. We cannot improve without honest feedback, and I appreciate your taking time to share the details of your experience with us. If your travels bring you back to the area, I invite you to visit Kuza Cave again as my guest. I would welcome the opportunity to personally introduce you to the magic of the cave and its history. Again, thank you for your feedback.

translated_content:
Completely lost. We paid €90 for 3 people, and it was supposed to include:
- Boat: It's supposed to be for 10-12 people, but there were about 22 of us.
- Visit to a sandbar with a fruit lunch: We were there for 30 minutes, and the area was packed.
- Snorkeling: I don't think it was the worst snorkeling I've ever done. There were no fish, the coral was dead, and the area was full of some kind of jellyfish that, luckily, didn't sting.

- Seafood lunch: They pile you up on rice and fries, then serve you a mini salad, half a mini lobster (it must have been a European lobster, judging by the size), a tiny piece of tuna, 3 prawns, and 4 small pieces of octopus. Nothing like the picture they advertise.
- Visit to the Blue Lagoon with mangroves: The place is beautiful, but you only get access and they give you 15 minutes to swim, without allowing you to walk or boat around the rest of the lagoon.
- 5 beers: After we had already paid, they told us they weren't included and that some of the salespeople always do that to attract customers without actually including them. On top of all this, there were many hours in the sun, little shade, and a completely wasted amount of time.
I DO NOT RECOMMEND IT!

content:
Acabamos de hacer la excursión Blue Safari y ha sido, sin duda, una de las mayores decepciones del viaje.
Íbamos unas 30 personas en un barco tradicional, todos apretados y con muy poco espacio para sentarse. Durante la primera parte de la excursión no había sombra, lo que hizo el trayecto especialmente incómodo. Después de comer sí colocaron sombra para todos, pero algunos de nosotros ya nos habíamos quemado bajo el sol.
Uno de los principales reclamos, el Blue Lagoon, no se visitó porque, según dijeron, la marea no era buena. Desde allí se suponía que íbamos a ver los árboles de mango, pero tampoco se pudieron ver por el mismo motivo. Como alternativa, nos dijeron que podíamos ir nadando, ya que el barco no podía acercarse, algo que no es una opción real ni segura para todo el mundo, y en la práctica no se vio nada.
En su lugar, nos llevaron a una supuesta isla desierta de arena que estaba completamente masificada, llena de turistas y vendedores, sin ningún encanto y con ambiente de mercadillo turístico. De isla virgen, nada.
El picnic de frutas fue claramente insuficiente y mal repartido para tanta gente. Solo comieron los más rápidos; algunos ni siquiera pudieron probar ciertas frutas. Organización inexistente.
El snorkel es engañoso. No hay ni rastro de los corales, peces de colores y aguas cristalinas que aparecen en la publicidad. Se hace entre barcos, con el agua turbia, rodeado de gente y viendo siempre los mismos peces pequeños. Fondo marino gris, sin nada destacable.
La comida tampoco justifica el precio. Nada de “gran mariscada”: arroz, patatas, verduras y un poco de gambas, pulpo y media langosta hecha al fuego, algo seca, y sin opción real de repetir salvo el arroz. Correcta como comida básica, pero muy lejos de lo prometido.
Para terminar, la parte “cultural” se limita a ver un Baobab sin ninguna explicación y después tiempo libre en una zona de tiendas, claramente pensada para que gastes dinero. Nada más.
¿Pagar 150 € por dos personas por esta excursión? Nunca.
Es un precio totalmente desproporcionado para una excursión mal organizada, sobrevendida y enfocada únicamente a exprimir al turista.
SOMOS TURISTAS, NO TONTOS.
translated_content:
We just finished the Blue Safari excursion, and it was undoubtedly one of the biggest disappointments of the trip.
There were about 30 of us on a traditional boat, all crammed together with very little space to sit. During the first part of the excursion, there was no shade, which made the journey especially uncomfortable. After lunch, they did provide shade for everyone, but some of us had already gotten sunburned.
One of the main attractions, the Blue Lagoon, wasn't visited because, they said, the tide wasn't right. From there, we were supposed to see the mango trees, but we couldn't see them for the same reason. As an alternative, they told us we could swim there since the boat couldn't get close, which isn't a realistic or safe option for everyone, and in practice, we didn't see anything.
Instead, they took us to a supposedly deserted sand island that was completely overcrowded, full of tourists and vendors, with no charm whatsoever and a tourist market atmosphere. A pristine island? Not at all.
The fruit picnic was clearly insufficient and poorly distributed for so many people. Only the quickest ate; some didn't even get a taste of certain fruits. The organization was nonexistent.
The snorkeling is a deception. There's no sign of the coral, colorful fish, and crystal-clear waters shown in the advertisements. It's done among boats, in murky water, surrounded by people, and you always see the same small fish. The seabed is gray, with nothing remarkable about it.
The food doesn't justify the price either. Nothing like a "great seafood feast": rice, potatoes, vegetables, and a few shrimp, octopus, and half a lobster cooked over a fire—a bit dry—with no real option for seconds except for the rice. It was adequate as a basic meal, but far from what was promised.
Finally, the "cultural" part is limited to seeing a baobab tree without any explanation, followed by free time in a shopping area clearly designed to get you to spend money. Nothing more.
Pay €150 for two people for this excursion? Never. This is a completely disproportionate price for a poorly organized, oversold tour focused solely on squeezing money out of tourists.
WE ARE TOURISTS, NOT FOOLS.

We booked the Safari Blue through our hotel for €130 (2 people). It’s advertised as a day of snorkeling in a beautiful sandbank, but the reality was very disappointing.
•	Long, wasted travel time: 3 hours to get there and 2+ hours back in a poorly maintained, overcrowded boat with a weak outboard engine. Safety felt questionable.
•	Snorkeling is minimal: only about 20 minutes, in an overcrowded area with little to see. Not the highlight they promise.
•	Poor equipment: not enough for everyone, and in bad condition.
•	Low-quality food: plain white rice, fries, a small piece of tuna and overcooked octopus.
•	Overall, a wasted day for what should have been the main activity.
Would not recommend this experience.

content: We booked the Safari Blue excursion through our hotel, and being honest it was the worst experience we’ve had during our time in Zanzibar. The starting location was very difficult to reach, and although you can expect this in Zanzibar, we didn’t know that the whole day would be spent in transport rather than the experience. However, this was certainly not the worst part: 1. We sailed in a poorly kept boat, with more people that it was capable to transport. 2. They took us to an island crowded with people and kept us there for an hour, when apparently the activity was “Safari Blue” = snorkel; 3. The snorkel lasted for no more than 20 mins after which they took us to another island to have “lunch”. (Do not recommend)  4. Again the way back home was extremely long, this time sailing - which should be cool - but it’s not when you are with other 25 people in a packed wooden boat. Although the staff managed to fall asleep… Overall, I would certainly not recommend this experience or the agency it self. It is 100% a tourist trap and wouldn’t waste neither my day nor 130$ for such a poor experience.

Hi Shylet,
Thank you for sharing your feedback and for rating us 4 stars — we’re so pleased to hear you enjoyed the service and that your guide Miguel from Mexico helped make the experience relaxing.
We’re sorry to hear you experienced ear pain after your jump. Just to clarify, ear discomfort during skydiving isn’t caused by wind speed, so ear covers wouldn’t make a difference. It’s more often due to pressure changes during the climb to altitude, which can be made worse if you have a cold, flu, or a blocked nose. This can affect the Eustachian tubes and lead to discomfort that sometimes lasts a while after the skydive.
We hope you’re feeling better soon, and we truly appreciate your suggestion and your kind words about the team.
— The Skydive Zanzibar Team

content: The Old Portuguese Arch in Stone Town, Zanzibar, stands as a subtle yet significant relic of the island’s brief Portuguese era in the 16th and 17th centuries. Located near Victoria Garden, between Vuga Road and Malindi Road, this ancient stone arch is one of the few remaining structures from Portuguese rule, offering a glimpse into a period that left minimal architectural impact on Zanzibar. The arch’s weathered facade and enduring presence provide a tangible connection to the past, inviting visitors to reflect on the layers of history that have shaped Stone Town’s unique cultural tapestry.

content: В 15 веке в глубоких джунглях Занзибара, португальцами был найден вход в подземные лабиринты, соединяющиеся с океаном и начато строительство деревни с каменными домами неподалеку.  С тех пор частично сохранились эти постройки. И выше на холме находится древня Фукучани с 2000 местными жителями, которые занимаются в основном сельским хозяйством и рыболовством. Вокруг в джунглях - 200 летние баобабы, гигантские манговые деревья, банановые пальмы и прочие чудесные растения, которые кормят местных жителей. Ну а пещера модернизирована устойчивой  лестницей, но достаточно с отвесным спуском. Мы приехал. В момент отлива индийского океана, поэтому только  дойдя до самой последней ступени смогли прикоснуться к прозрачной морской воде. Со слов гида в момент отлива глубина составила 3 метра. А вот а момент вы Окой воды глубина около 7 метров. В на точнее время Мейера и руины используются для обучения школьников истории и географии. С Нунгви доехать до рецепты можно на тук туке за 20 минут с оплатой около 15 долларов раунд трип.
translated_content: In the 15th century, in the deep jungles of Zanzibar, the Portuguese discovered an entrance to a subterranean labyrinth connecting to the ocean and began building a village with stone houses nearby. Parts of these buildings have survived since then. Higher up on the hill is the ancient settlement of Fukuchani, home to 2,000 local residents, who primarily engage in agriculture and fishing. The surrounding jungle is filled with 200-year-old baobabs, giant mango trees, banana palms, and other wondrous plants that provide food for the locals. The cave has been modernized with a sturdy staircase, albeit a rather steep one. We arrived at low tide in the Indian Ocean, so only after reaching the very last step were we able to touch the clear seawater. According to the guide, the depth at low tide was 3 meters. But at high tide, the depth of the Okoye water is about 7 meters. At the current time, Meyer and the ruins are used to teach history and geography to schoolchildren. From Nungwi, the site can be reached by tuk-tuk in 20 minutes, for a roundtrip fee of about $15.

content:
Je ne comprend pas les commentaires qui disent que c est magnifique....
La visite des ruines prend 10 secondes on voit tout en sortant de la voiture.
Et la cave n à rien d exceptionnel.
Il y à un tout petit point de jour ce qui ne permet pas de voir le reste si on ne prévoit pas de frontale ou autre point de lumière.
Pour cette fois ci nous en avions une.
Quelle surprise de voir que sous l''eau tout est blindé de pollution bouteilles plastiques ect...
Le seul endroit qui n est pas pourri ce sont les 3 m2 visibles sans lampe.
Une honte en sachant que la cave est petite et qu''on paye 10 dollars par personne et qu''ils sont 3 ou 4 à rien faire à l''entrée sur leur téléphone.
Ils devrait utiliser cet argent pour entretenir le lieu au minimum.
A oui aussi on a le droit à 10 min dans l eau.... Et les 5 premières minutes le guide est là il vous regarde sans rien dire comme un vigile. Gênant.
Les caves de Maalum à PAJE sont un peu plus chères mais le site est entretenu à la perfection et on peut nager dans une magnifique cave naturelle pendant quelques heures.
translated_content:
I don't understand the comments saying it's magnificent... The visit to the ruins takes 10 seconds; you can see everything as soon as you get out of the car.
And the cave itself is nothing special.
There's a tiny bit of daylight, which makes it impossible to see the rest unless you have a headlamp or some other light source.
This time, we had one.
What a surprise to see that underwater, everything is covered in pollution: plastic bottles, etc.
The only place that isn't a mess is the 3 square meters visible without a lamp.
It's a disgrace, considering the cave is small and we pay $10 per person, and there are 3 or 4 people at the entrance doing nothing but their phones.
They should use that money to at least maintain the place.
Oh, and we also get 10 minutes in the water... And for the first 5 minutes, the guide is there, watching you without saying a word, like a security guard. Awkward.
The Maalum caves in PAJE are a little more expensive but the site is perfectly maintained and you can swim in a magnificent natural cave for a few hours.

content:
L''endroit est joli avec sa plage et ses falaises rocailleuses qui forment un paysage atypique.
On peut se garer sur un parking payant, mais au moins il est aménagé et surveillé.
L''accès est également aménagé.
Des locaux vendent leurs articles artisanaux.
On peut aussi se balader sur la plage selon l''état de la marée.
Lieu idéal pour pratiquer le drone.
Le seul bémol: être importunés sans cesse par des gens qui nous suivent pour nous soutirer des shillings.
Nous voulions nous promener tranquillement sur la plage, et on a été littéralement harcelés (sans agressivité mais c''est lourd et ennuyeux) par des jeunes qui nous suivaient comme s''ils étaient des guides officiels, et qui ont même mis de la musique sur leur téléphone, croyant nous faire plaisir, alors que nous cherchions juste un peu de tranquillité.
translated_content:
The place is lovely, with its beach and rocky cliffs creating a unique landscape.
There's a paid parking lot, but at least it's well-maintained and supervised.
Access is also easy.
Locals sell their handcrafted items.
You can also walk along the beach, depending on the tide.
It's an ideal spot for flying drones.
The only downside: being constantly bothered by people who follow us trying to get shillings.
We wanted to take a peaceful stroll on the beach, and we were literally harassed (not aggressively, but it was tiresome and annoying) by young people who followed us as if they were official guides, and who even played music on their phones, thinking they were doing us a favor, when all we wanted was a little peace and quiet.

content: Make sure before you go that you check the tide levels. If you get there when it’s high tide you won’t be able to see the rock. We drove from the north of a scooter and it was a great ride and cheaper than taxi. Took us through a few small towns and beautiful scenery. When you get there low tide and see the rock there is a bar down the beach you can walk to and have a drink also.
full_address: GGQR+M5J Mtende rock, Tanzania

content: Väga ilus looduslik pankrannik. Sissesõidul alale nõutakse kõigilt 2000 raha. Tšeki saab vastu, ametlik toetuse värk. Ägedad restot on kah seal rannas. Sõime kallima ja kõige maitsetuma õhtusöögi praegusel reisil. Aga vaated korallriffile sisaldusid hinda👌✌️🏝️. Hakuna matata☀️
